3516: @@ -0,0 +1,134 @@
3517: +# capture command
3518: +
3519: +### Description
3520: +
3521: +The `capture` command captures packets on lab link interfaces of one or more nodes and writes them as one [pcapng](https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-opsawg-pcapng-03.html) stream, to a file or to stdout for Wireshark.
3522: +
3523: +It works with every runtime:
3524: +
3525: +- **Docker and Podman**: containerlab opens a packet socket on each interface inside the node's network namespace. Nothing runs in the node, the node image needs no capture tools, and no extra software is needed on the host: the command needs root, like `deploy`. See [How Docker and Podman captures work](#how-docker-and-podman-captures-work).
3526: +- **c9s**: the `clabwire` sidecar of each node's pod captures the packets; see the [c9s runtime](../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md#packet-capture).
3527: +
3528: +The output is the same with both. [Edgeshark](../manual/wireshark.md) remains an alternative for Docker labs when you prefer to pick interfaces in a GUI.
3529: +
3530: +--8<-- "docs/cmd/deploy.md:env-vars-flags"
3531: +
3532: +### Usage
3533: +
3534: +`containerlab [global-flags] capture [local-flags]`
3535: +
3536: +### Flags
3537: +
3538: +#### topology | name
3539: +
3540: +Use the global `--topo | -t` flag to reference the lab topology file, or use the global `--name` flag to reference an already deployed lab by name. Without either, containerlab looks for a `*.clab.yml` file in the current directory, like the other lab commands.
3541: +
3542: +With Docker and Podman, the capturable interfaces are the links of the topology file, so `--name` needs the topology file the lab was deployed from to still be in place.
3543: +
3544: +#### target
3545: +
3546: +The local `--target` flag selects what to capture, as `<node>:<interface>[,<interface>...]`. Repeat it for more nodes:
3547: +
3548: +```text
3549: +--target srl1:e1-1,e1-2 --target srl2:e1-1
3550: +```
3551: +
3552: +The node name ends at the first colon, so interface names such as `1/1/3` or `ethernet-1/1` need no quoting. Node names are accepted as the topology file spells them; with Docker and Podman also as the container name (`clab-srl-srl1`), with c9s also as they were sanitized for Kubernetes (`R1` or `r1`). Interfaces are accepted by their name in the node or by the alias the topology used for them (`e1-1` or `ethernet-1/1` for SR Linux). `--list` shows both.
3553: +
3554: +Only lab link interfaces can be captured; the management interface cannot. An interface that is not a link interface of the node fails the command before anything is captured, and the error lists the node's capturable interfaces.
3555: +
3556: +#### duration
3557: +
3558: +The local `--duration` flag stops the capture after the given time (`30s`, `5m`, `2h`). The default `0` captures until the command is interrupted with Ctrl+C or SIGTERM. Captures may run longer than an hour; see [Long captures](#long-captures).
3559: +
3560: +#### packet-limit
3561: +
3562: +The local `--packet-limit` flag stops the capture after that many packets, counted across all targets. `0`, the default, means no limit.
3563: +
3564: +#### snap-length
3565: +
3566: +The local `--snap-length` flag sets how many bytes of each packet are kept, from 64 to 1048576. The default `0` keeps 256 KiB.
3567: +
3568: +#### write
3569: +
3570: +The local `--write | -w` flag names the output file. The default `-` writes to stdout.
3571: +
3572: +#### list
3573: +
3574: +The local `--list` flag lists the interfaces `capture` accepts, for every running node, with the node and interface at the other end of each link, instead of capturing. `--format | -f` selects `table` (default) or `json`.
3575: +
3576: +### Output
3577: +
3578: +The output is one pcapng section:
3579: +
3580: +- a Section Header Block with `shb_userappl` set to `containerlab`
3581: +- one Interface Description Block per target, in the order of the `--target` flags, written before any packet: link type Ethernet, the snap length, nanosecond timestamps, and the name `<node>:<interface>` (for example `srl1:e1-1`), with the node named as the topology spells it
3582: +- Enhanced Packet Blocks of all targets, in timestamp order: packets are held briefly (100 ms with Docker and Podman, 250 ms with c9s) and written ordered by timestamp, so packets of different interfaces come out in order even though each one is read on its own; a packet that arrives later than that is written as it comes
3583: +
3584: +The interface name shows in Wireshark's interface column (`frame.interface_name`), so a capture of several nodes can be filtered by node and interface.
3585: +
3586: +When the capture ends (duration, packet limit, Ctrl+C or SIGTERM), the command finishes the stream and exits with code 0; the file is a valid capture. Status messages go to stderr. With c9s, every `clabwire` capture in the pods ends with the command: containerlab closes its stdin, and `clabwire` (`--stop-on-stdin-close`) stops.
3587: +
3588: +`--list -f json` prints an array:
3589: +
3590: +```json
3591: +[
3592: +  {
3593: +    "node": "srl1",
3594: +    "interface": "e1-1",
3595: +    "alias": "ethernet-1/1",
3596: +    "peer_node": "srl2",
3597: +    "peer_interface": "ethernet-1/1"
3598: +  }
3599: +]
3600: +```
3601: +
3602: +`alias` is present only when the topology used an alias for the interface. `peer_node` is `host` for a host endpoint and `mgmt-net` for a management network endpoint.
3603: +
3604: +### How Docker and Podman captures work
3605: +
3606: +For each target, containerlab enters the node's network namespace, opens a Linux packet socket (`AF_PACKET`) bound to the interface, and leaves the namespace again; the socket keeps capturing on that interface. This is what `tcpdump` does inside the node, without needing `tcpdump` in the node or on the host. All sockets are opened before the first byte is written, so a capture that cannot start (a node that does not run, a missing interface) fails without output.
3607: +
3608: +- Packets carry the kernel's receive timestamps, so packets of different nodes compare on one clock.
3609: +- 802.1Q tags, which the kernel keeps outside the frame, are put back in place, so VLAN traffic shows its tags as on the wire.
3610: +- Each socket is in promiscuous mode for as long as it is open; the interface returns to its previous state when the capture ends.
3611: +- An interface that goes down and up again keeps being captured. When an interface disappears, for example while its node restarts, containerlab waits for it and reattaches once the node is back (`containerlab restart --node`). The time it was gone is reported as a warning with its start and end time.
3612: +
3613: +The command needs root (to open packet sockets and enter network namespaces), as other lab commands do.
3614: +
3615: +### Long captures
3616: +
3617: +Docker and Podman captures have no length limit. With c9s, one `clabwire` capture lasts at most one hour. `capture` chains captures: it starts the next one shortly before the current one ends, lets both run for a few seconds, and switches between them in the middle of that overlap. The repeated section and interface headers of the follow-up are dropped, and packets seen by both captures near the switch are written once (they are matched by content, because each capture stamps packets when it reads them). Once the switch time has passed, the previous capture is stopped through its stdin instead of running to its end. If a follow-up capture does not start in time, the missing interval is reported as a warning with its start and end time; it is never skipped silently. The timestamp order holds across switches: while one node's capture switches, packets of other nodes stamped after the switch wait for it.
3618: +
3619: +### Examples
3620: +
3621: +#### Capture two nodes for 30 seconds into one file
3622: +
3623: +```bash
3624: +containerlab capture -t srl.clab.yml \
3625: +  --target srl1:e1-1 --target srl2:e1-1 --duration 30s -w srl.pcapng
3626: +```
3627: +
3628: +#### Watch a capture live in Wireshark
3629: +
3630: +```bash
3631: +containerlab capture --name srl --target srl1:e1-1,e1-2 -w - | wireshark -k -i -
3632: +```
3633: +
3634: +#### Capture the first 100 packets with tshark
3635: +
3636: +```bash
3637: +containerlab capture --name srl --target srl1:ethernet-1/1 --packet-limit 100 -w - | tshark -r -
3638: +```
3639: +
3640: +#### List the capturable interfaces
3641: +
3642: +```bash
3643: +containerlab capture --name srl --list
3644: +```
3645: +
3646: +#### Capture a c9s lab
3647: +
3648: +```bash
3649: +containerlab -r c9s capture --name srl --target srl1:e1-1 --target srl2:e1-1 -w srl.pcapng
3650: +```

3657:  
3658:  The `inspect interfaces` subcommand provides information about the network interfaces of deployed nodes of a deployed lab.
3659:  The subcommand gathers information directly from deployed containers, and displays information about their operational state, network interface type, and if applicable, the applied network interface alias.

The node names follow `inspect` (`<lab>-<node>`), and the JSON fields are the same as with Docker.
3662: +

3664:  
3665:  `containerlab [global-flags] inspect interfaces [local-flags]`
3666:

3726:  
3727: +## Packet capture
3728: +
3729: +[`containerlab capture`](../../cmd/capture.md) captures lab link interfaces of
3730: +one or more nodes into one pcapng stream. Each node's pod runs the `clabwire`
3731: +sidecar, which realized the node's links; containerlab execs its capture
3732: +command (`/clabernetes/manager node-runtime packet-capture`) in the sidecar.
3733: +No capture service runs in the cluster, and nothing is captured outside the
3734: +lab's planned link interfaces.
3735: +
3736: +```bash
3737: +# both ends of a link, for 30 seconds
3738: +containerlab -r c9s capture -t clos.clab.yml \
3739: +  --target srl1:e1-1 --target srl2:e1-1 --duration 30s -w srl.pcapng
3740: +
3741: +# live in Wireshark until Wireshark or Ctrl+C ends it
3742: +containerlab -r c9s capture --name clos --target srl1:e1-1,e1-2 -w - | wireshark -k -i -
3743: +
3744: +# what can be captured, with the peer of each link
3745: +containerlab -r c9s capture --name clos --list
3746: +```
3747: +
3748: +How it works:
3749: +
3750: +- containerlab locates each target node's pod and runs one `clabwire` capture
3751: +  per node, with `--nodeName`, every requested interface of that node,
3752: +  `--format pcapng` and `--stop-on-stdin-close`, with stdin attached.
3753: +- The streams are merged into one section: one Interface Description Block per
3754: +  target named `<node>:<interface>` (the node as the topology spells it),
3755: +  written before the first packet, and the packets of every target with their
3756: +  interface IDs remapped.
3757: +- Packets are written in timestamp order. Each node's stream arrives over its
3758: +  own exec stream, so the merged stream holds every packet for 250 ms and
3759: +  writes the held packets ordered by timestamp. A packet that arrives later
3760: +  than that, stamped before a packet already written, is written as it comes;
3761: +  the number of such packets goes to the debug log.
3762: +- `clabwire` limits one capture to one hour. Longer captures, and captures
3763: +  without `--duration`, chain captures with a few seconds of overlap and switch
3764: +  in the middle of it; packets near the switch are matched by content so each
3765: +  is written once. A follow-up that does not start in time is reported as a
3766: +  gap, with its time span.
3767: +- `clabwire` audit records (JSON on its stderr, schema
3768: +  `c9s.direct-packet-capture-audit/v1alpha1`) with status `Denied` or `Failed`
3769: +  end the command with their reason. `Started` and `Succeeded` go to the debug
3770: +  log.
3771: +
3772: +Interface names are the names inside the node; targets may also use the alias
3773: +the topology used for an interface:
3774: +
3775: +| Kind | Interface | Alias |
3776: +| ---- | --------- | ----- |
3777: +| linux | `eth1` | |
3778: +| SR Linux | `e1-1` | `ethernet-1/1` |
3779: +| vr-sros / nokia_sros | `eth3` | `1/1/3` |
3780: +
3781: +The management interface and the pod's `c9s0` interface cannot be captured.
3782: +
3783: +Ctrl+C or SIGTERM ends a capture cleanly: the output stays a valid pcapng
3784: +file and the command exits with code 0. Kubernetes does not stop a command
3785: +when its exec stream closes, but it closes the command's stdin. containerlab
3786: +closes the stdin of every `clabwire` capture when the capture ends for any
3787: +reason (the duration or packet limit, Ctrl+C, an error, a failed write of the
3788: +output such as a closed Wireshark, or a newer segment taking over), and
3789: +`clabwire` then ends the capture within milliseconds. If the process does not
3790: +end within three seconds, containerlab cuts the exec stream. A killed
3791: +containerlab drops the connection, which closes stdin as well.
3792: +
3793: +Capturing needs `get` and `create` on `pods/exec` in the lab namespace, which
3794: +`clabernetes-lab-editor` grants. `inspect interfaces -r c9s` lists the same
3795: +interfaces, with the MAC address, index, MTU and operational state read from
3796: +sysfs in the device container (type `veth`, which is how `clabwire` realizes
3797: +lab links).
3798: +

3846:

3884:  
3885:  Containerlab offers a simple way to capture the packets from any interface of any node in the lab. This article will explain how to do that.
3886:  
3887:  ///tip
3888:  
3889: +The [`containerlab capture`](../cmd/capture.md) command captures one or more lab link interfaces, of one or more nodes, into one pcapng file or stream, with nothing to install in the nodes or on the host:
3890: +
3891: +```bash
3892: +containerlab capture --name quickstart --target srl:e1-1 -w - | wireshark -k -i -
3893: +```
3894: +
3895:  If you are looking for a free Web UI for packet capture with Wireshark, check out our [Edgeshark integration](#edgeshark-integration).
3896:  ///
3897:

3929: +// The clabwire packet capture contract (clabernetes 0.11 or newer).
3930: +const (
3931: +	clabwireContainer = "clabwire"
3932: +	clabwireManager   = "/clabernetes/manager"
3933: +	// captureAuditSchema is the schema of the JSON audit lines clabwire writes to stderr.
3934: +	captureAuditSchema = "c9s.direct-packet-capture-audit/v1alpha1"
3935: +
3936: +	captureAuditStarted   = "Started"
3937: +	captureAuditSucceeded = "Succeeded"
3938: +	captureAuditFailed    = "Failed"
3939: +	captureAuditDenied    = "Denied"
3940: +
3941: +	// maxCaptureSegment is the longest single clabwire capture; longer captures are chained.
3942: +	maxCaptureSegment = time.Hour
3943: +	// maxClabwirePackets is the packet limit of a single clabwire capture.
3944: +	maxClabwirePackets = 1_000_000
3945: +	// maxCaptureOverlap is how long two chained segments run side by side.
3946: +	maxCaptureOverlap = 10 * time.Second
3947: +	// maxCaptureCutWindow is the half-width of the window around the cut in which packets of
3948: +	// two segments are matched by content; it covers the difference between the timestamps
3949: +	// two clabwire processes give the same packet.
3950: +	maxCaptureCutWindow = 500 * time.Millisecond
3951: +	// minCaptureSegment is the shortest segment the chain requests.
3952: +	minCaptureSegment = 100 * time.Millisecond
3953: +	// captureEndGrace is how long a capture with a duration waits for its last clabwire
3954: +	// process to end after the duration passed.
3955: +	captureEndGrace = 30 * time.Second
3956: +	// captureStartRetries bounds the attempts to start a follow-up segment.
3957: +	captureStartRetries = 3
3958: +	// captureStdinCloseGrace is how long a segment's exec may take to end after its stdin was
3959: +	// closed before the stream is cut.
3960: +	captureStdinCloseGrace = 3 * time.Second
3961: +	// clabwireStopOnStdinClose makes clabwire end a capture when its stdin closes. A
3962: +	// Kubernetes exec does not stop its process when the stream ends, but it closes the
3963: +	// process's stdin, so every capture runs with stdin attached and this flag.
3964: +	clabwireStopOnStdinClose = "--stop-on-stdin-close"
3965: +
3966: +	// envCaptureSegment overrides the segment length. It exists to exercise chaining in tests
3967: +	// without hour-long captures.
3968: +	envCaptureSegment = "CLAB_C9S_CAPTURE_SEGMENT"
3969: +	// defaultCaptureReorderWindow is how long the merged stream holds a packet back so packets
3970: +	// of other nodes stamped earlier but delivered later still go out before it.
3971: +	defaultCaptureReorderWindow = 250 * time.Millisecond
3972: +	// envCaptureReorderWindow overrides the reorder window; 0 writes packets as they arrive.
3973: +	// It is an internal knob, not a supported setting.
3974: +	envCaptureReorderWindow = "CLAB_C9S_CAPTURE_REORDER_WINDOW"
3975: +)

3978: +// a *labruntime.CommandExitError.

3982: +	command []string,

3988: +type clabwireInterface struct {
3989: +	Node          string `json:"node"`
3990: +	Interface     string `json:"interface"`
3991: +	Alias         string `json:"alias,omitempty"`

3993: +	PeerInterface string `json:"peerInterface"`

3996: +// captureAudit is one clabwire audit line.

4000: +	Status        string    `json:"status"`
4001: +	NodeName      string    `json:"nodeName"`
4002: +	Format        string    `json:"format"`
4003: +	Reason        string    `json:"reason"`
4004: +	Packets       int       `json:"packets"`

4013: +	if r.podExec != nil {
4014: +		return r.podExec
4015: +	}
4016: +
4017: +	return r.streamPodExec

4020: +// captureSegmentLength is the length of one clabwire capture before the next takes over.
4021: +func (r *Runtime) captureSegmentLength() time.Duration {
4022: +	if r.captureSegment > 0 && r.captureSegment <= maxCaptureSegment {
4023: +		return r.captureSegment
4024: +	}
4025: +
4026: +	return maxCaptureSegment
4027: +}
4028: +
4029: +// captureReorderWindowLength is the reorder window of the merged stream; zero disables
4030: +// reordering.
4031: +func (r *Runtime) captureReorderWindowLength() time.Duration {
4032: +	switch {
4033: +	case r.captureReorderWindow < 0:
4034: +		return 0
4035: +	case r.captureReorderWindow > 0:
4036: +		return r.captureReorderWindow
4037: +	}
4038: +
4039: +	return defaultCaptureReorderWindow
4040: +}
4041: +
4042: +// captureReorderWindowFromEnv reads the reorder window knob: unset or invalid keeps the
4043: +// default (0), "0" disables reordering (-1).
4044: +func captureReorderWindowFromEnv() time.Duration {
4045: +	value, err := time.ParseDuration(os.Getenv(envCaptureReorderWindow))
4046: +	switch {
4047: +	case err != nil || value < 0:
4048: +		return 0
4049: +	case value == 0:
4050: +		return -1
4051: +	}
4052: +
4053: +	return value
4054: +}
4055: +
4056: +func captureSegmentFromEnv() time.Duration {
4057: +	value, err := time.ParseDuration(os.Getenv(envCaptureSegment))
4058: +	if err != nil || value <= 0 {
4059: +		return 0
4060: +	}
4061: +
4062: +	return value
4063: +}

4065: +// CaptureInterfaces lists the capturable lab link interfaces of the requested nodes, or of every
4066: +// node, as clabwire reports them, with their peers. Node names are reported as the topology
4067: +// spells them.
4068: +func (r *Runtime) CaptureInterfaces(
4069: +	ctx context.Context,
4070: +	req clablabruntime.NodeRequest,
4071: +) ([]clablabruntime.CaptureInterface, error) {
4072: +	r, err := r.connect(ctx, req.Identity)
4073: +	if err != nil {
4074: +		return nil, err
4075: +	}
4076: +
4077: +	locations, err := r.LocateNode(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
4078: +		Name: req.Name, Namespace: req.Namespace, Nodes: req.Nodes, Identity: req.Identity,
4079: +	})
4080: +	if err != nil {
4081: +		return nil, err
4082: +	}
4083: +	if len(req.Nodes) == 0 {
4084: +		// a lab-wide listing skips nodes that do not run
4085: +		running := locations[:0]
4086: +		for _, location := range locations {
4087: +			if location.Pod != "" {
4088: +				running = append(running, location)
4089: +			}
4090: +		}
4091: +		locations = running
4092: +	}
4093: +
4094: +	listed, err := r.listCaptureInterfaces(ctx, req.Name, locations)
4095: +	if err != nil {
4096: +		return nil, err
4097: +	}
4098: +	names, err := r.nodeDisplayNames(ctx, req.Name, locations)
4099: +	if err != nil {
4100: +		return nil, err
4101: +	}
4102: +
4103: +	result := make([]clablabruntime.CaptureInterface, 0)
4104: +	for _, location := range locations {
4105: +		for _, entry := range listed[location.NodeName] {
4106: +			result = append(result, clablabruntime.CaptureInterface{
4107: +				Node:          names.display(entry.Node),
4108: +				Interface:     entry.Interface,
4109: +				Alias:         entry.Alias,
4110: +				PeerNode:      names.display(entry.PeerNode),
4111: +				PeerInterface: entry.PeerInterface,
4112: +			})
4113: +		}
4114: +	}
4115: +	sort.SliceStable(result, func(i, j int) bool {
4116: +		if result[i].Node != result[j].Node {
4117: +			return result[i].Node < result[j].Node
4118: +		}
4119: +
4120: +		return result[i].Interface < result[j].Interface
4121: +	})
4122: +
4123: +	return result, nil
4124: +}
4125: +
4126: +// listCaptureInterfaces runs one --list-interfaces per pod and returns the entries per Node.
4127: +func (r *Runtime) listCaptureInterfaces(
4128: +	ctx context.Context,
4129: +	lab string,
4130: +	locations []clablabruntime.NodeLocation,
4131: +) (map[string][]clabwireInterface, error) {
4132: +	pods := map[string]clablabruntime.NodeLocation{}
4133: +	wanted := map[string]bool{}
4134: +	for _, location := range locations {
4135: +		if location.Pod == "" {
4136: +			return nil, fmt.Errorf("c9s node %s/%s/%s has no pod; is it running?",
4137: +				location.Namespace, lab, location.NodeName)
4138: +		}
4139: +		pods[location.Namespace+"/"+location.Pod] = location
4140: +		wanted[location.NodeName] = true
4141: +	}
4142: +
4143: +	var mu sync.Mutex
4144: +	result := map[string][]clabwireInterface{}
4145: +	group, groupCtx := errgroup.WithContext(ctx)
4146: +	group.SetLimit(interfaceSampleWorkers)
4147: +	exec := r.execInPodContainer()
4148: +	for _, location := range pods {
4149: +		group.Go(func() error {
4150: +			var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
4151: +			err := exec(groupCtx, location.Namespace, location.Pod, clabwireContainer,
4152: +				[]string{clabwireManager, "node-runtime", "packet-capture", "--list-interfaces"},
4153: +				nil, &stdout, &stderr)
4154: +			if err != nil {
4155: +				return fmt.Errorf("failed to list the capturable interfaces of pod %s/%s: %w%s",
4156: +					location.Namespace, location.Pod, err, stderrSuffix(stderr.Bytes()))
4157: +			}
4158: +
4159: +			var entries []clabwireInterface
4160: +			if err := json.Unmarshal(stdout.Bytes(), &entries); err != nil {
4161: +				return fmt.Errorf("failed to parse the capturable interfaces of pod %s/%s: %w",
4162: +					location.Namespace, location.Pod, err)
4163: +			}
4164: +
4165: +			mu.Lock()
4166: +			defer mu.Unlock()
4167: +			for _, entry := range entries {
4168: +				if wanted[entry.Node] {
4169: +					result[entry.Node] = append(result[entry.Node], entry)
4170: +				}
4171: +			}
4172: +
4173: +			return nil
4174: +		})
4175: +	}
4176: +	if err := group.Wait(); err != nil {
4177: +		return nil, err
4178: +	}
4179: +
4180: +	return result, nil
4181: +}
4182: +
4183: +func stderrSuffix(stderr []byte) string {
4184: +	text := strings.TrimSpace(string(stderr))
4185: +	if text == "" {
4186: +		return ""
4187: +	}
4188: +
4189: +	return ": " + text
4190: +}

4196: +	if original := n[name]; original != "" {
4197: +		return original
4198: +	}
4199: +
4200: +	return name

4204: +// lab's Nodes.

4206: +	ctx context.Context,
4207: +	lab string,
4208: +	locations []clablabruntime.NodeLocation,
4209: +) (nodeNames, error) {
4210: +	names := nodeNames{}
4211: +	if len(locations) == 0 {
4212: +		return names, nil
4213: +	}
4214: +
4215: +	nodes, err := r.nodesForTopology(ctx, lab, locations[0].Namespace)
4216: +	if err != nil {

4218: +	}
4219: +	for idx := range nodes.Items {
4220: +		if original := nodes.Items[idx].GetLabels()[labelOriginalNodeName]; original != "" {
4221: +			names[nodes.Items[idx].GetName()] = original
4222: +		}
4223: +	}
4224: +
4225: +	return names, nil

4228: +// captureGroup is the part of a capture one clabwire process serves: the requested interfaces of
4229: +// one node, in one pod.
4230: +type captureGroup struct {
4231: +	location clablabruntime.NodeLocation
4232: +	display  string
4233: +	// interfaces are the planned interface names, in the order the merged stream lists them.
4234: +	interfaces []string
4235: +	// ids are the merged interface IDs of interfaces.
4236: +	ids []uint32
4237: +}
4238: +
4239: +// resolvedCapture is a validated capture request.
4240: +type resolvedCapture struct {
4241: +	groups []*captureGroup
4242: +	// names are the merged interface names (<node>:<interface>), indexed by merged ID.
4243: +	names []string
4244: +}
4245: +
4246: +// resolveCaptureTargets locates every target node, checks every interface against the
4247: +// interfaces clabwire allows, and groups the targets per node.
4248: +func (r *Runtime) resolveCaptureTargets(
4249: +	ctx context.Context,
4250: +	req clablabruntime.CaptureRequest,
4251: +) (*resolvedCapture, error) {
4252: +	nodeOrder := make([]string, 0, len(req.Targets))
4253: +	seenNodes := map[string]bool{}
4254: +	for _, target := range req.Targets {
4255: +		if !seenNodes[target.Node] {
4256: +			seenNodes[target.Node] = true
4257: +			nodeOrder = append(nodeOrder, target.Node)
4258: +		}
4259: +	}
4260: +
4261: +	locations, err := r.LocateNode(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
4262: +		Name: req.Name, Namespace: req.Namespace, Nodes: nodeOrder, Identity: req.Identity,
4263: +	})
4264: +	if err != nil {
4265: +		return nil, err
4266: +	}
4267: +	byRequest := make(map[string]clablabruntime.NodeLocation, len(nodeOrder))
4268: +	for idx, name := range nodeOrder {
4269: +		byRequest[name] = locations[idx]
4270: +	}
4271: +
4272: +	listed, err := r.listCaptureInterfaces(ctx, req.Name, locations)
4273: +	if err != nil {
4274: +		return nil, err
4275: +	}
4276: +	names, err := r.nodeDisplayNames(ctx, req.Name, locations)
4277: +	if err != nil {
4278: +		return nil, err
4279: +	}
4280: +
4281: +	resolved := &resolvedCapture{}
4282: +	groups := map[string]*captureGroup{}
4283: +	seen := map[string]bool{}
4284: +	for _, target := range req.Targets {
4285: +		location := byRequest[target.Node]
4286: +		entry, ok := findCaptureInterface(listed[location.NodeName], target.Interface)
4287: +		if !ok {
4288: +			return nil, fmt.Errorf("interface %q of node %q is not a capturable link "+
4289: +				"interface; capturable: %s", target.Interface, target.Node,
4290: +				describeCaptureInterfaces(listed[location.NodeName]))
4291: +		}
4292: +
4293: +		key := location.NodeName + "\x00" + entry.Interface
4294: +		if seen[key] {
4295: +			return nil, fmt.Errorf("interface %q of node %q is requested more than once",
4296: +				entry.Interface, target.Node)
4297: +		}
4298: +		seen[key] = true
4299: +
4300: +		group := groups[location.NodeName]
4301: +		if group == nil {
4302: +			group = &captureGroup{
4303: +				location: location,
4304: +				display:  names.display(location.NodeName),
4305: +			}
4306: +			groups[location.NodeName] = group
4307: +			resolved.groups = append(resolved.groups, group)
4308: +		}
4309: +
4310: +		id := uint32(len(resolved.names)) //nolint:gosec // bounded by the targets
4311: +		group.interfaces = append(group.interfaces, entry.Interface)
4312: +		group.ids = append(group.ids, id)
4313: +		resolved.names = append(resolved.names, group.display+":"+entry.Interface)
4314: +	}
4315: +
4316: +	return resolved, nil
4317: +}
4318: +
4319: +// findCaptureInterface matches a requested interface by its planned name or its alias.
4320: +func findCaptureInterface(entries []clabwireInterface, name string) (clabwireInterface, bool) {
4321: +	for _, entry := range entries {
4322: +		if entry.Interface == name {
4323: +			return entry, true
4324: +		}
4325: +	}
4326: +	for _, entry := range entries {
4327: +		if entry.Alias != "" && entry.Alias == name {
4328: +			return entry, true
4329: +		}
4330: +	}
4331: +
4332: +	return clabwireInterface{}, false
4333: +}
4334: +
4335: +func describeCaptureInterfaces(entries []clabwireInterface) string {
4336: +	if len(entries) == 0 {
4337: +		return "none"
4338: +	}
4339: +
4340: +	names := make([]string, 0, len(entries))
4341: +	for _, entry := range entries {
4342: +		name := entry.Interface
4343: +		if entry.Alias != "" {
4344: +			name += " (" + entry.Alias + ")"
4345: +		}
4346: +		names = append(names, name)
4347: +	}
4348: +
4349: +	return strings.Join(names, ", ")
4350: +}
4351: +
4352: +// Capture streams pcapng from lab link interfaces to w: one section, one Interface Description
4353: +// Block per target in request order named <node>:<interface>, then the packets of every target.
4354: +//
4355: +// Each node's interfaces are captured by one clabwire process in the node's pod. clabwire limits
4356: +// a capture to one hour, so a longer capture (or one without Duration) chains captures: the next
4357: +// one starts before the current one ends, and the stream switches at a cut in the overlap. See
4358: +// captureChain for how packets of the overlap are kept once.
4359: +//
4360: +// Packets go out in timestamp order across nodes, through a reorder buffer (captureReorder).
4361: +//
4362: +// Every clabwire process runs with stdin attached and --stop-on-stdin-close: a Kubernetes exec
4363: +// does not stop its process when the stream closes, so containerlab closes stdin whenever a
4364: +// segment ends (the capture ends, fails, its output fails, or a newer segment took over) and
4365: +// clabwire ends the capture itself.
4366: +//
4367: +// Capture returns when Duration has passed, PacketLimit packets were written, or ctx ends; an
4368: +// ended ctx is not an error. Every block reaches w in one write, so the stream is a valid capture
4369: +// whenever it stops. A clabwire Denied or Failed audit record is returned as an error.
4370: +func (r *Runtime) Capture(
4371: +	ctx context.Context,
4372: +	req clablabruntime.CaptureRequest,
4373: +	w io.Writer,
4374: +) error {
4375: +	if err := clabcapture.ValidateRequest(&req); err != nil {
4376: +		return err
4377: +	}
4378: +
4379: +	r, err := r.connect(ctx, req.Identity)
4380: +	if err != nil {
4381: +		return err
4382: +	}
4383: +
4384: +	resolved, err := r.resolveCaptureTargets(ctx, req)
4385: +	if err != nil {
4386: +		return err
4387: +	}

4491: +// captureChain runs the chained clabwire captures of one group.
4492: +//
4493: +// Chaining and the cut: segment k+1 starts `overlap` before segment k is due to end, so both
4494: +// capture the same packets for a while. clabwire stamps packets when it reads them, so two
4495: +// processes give the same packet timestamps a few microseconds apart, and timestamps alone
4496: +// cannot pair them. The chain therefore cuts in the middle of the overlap and matches packets by
4497: +// content close to the cut:
4498: +//
4499: +//  1. When segment k+1 reports Started (pod clock, from its audit record), the cut is
4500: +//     T = midpoint of [Started(k+1), Started(k) + duration(k)]: both segments run then.
4501: +//  2. Segment k keeps streaming live, but only packets stamped before T; it remembers the
4502: +//     content of what it wrote since segment k+1 started.
4503: +//  3. Segment k+1's packets are held back until segment k has ended. Then the ones stamped
4504: +//     before T-W are dropped (segment k had them), the ones stamped within W of T are dropped
4505: +//     when segment k wrote the same bytes on the same interface, and every other one is written.
4506: +//     From then on segment k+1 streams live.
4507: +//
4508: +// Once the pod clock passed T+W, segment k's stdin is closed so it ends without running to its
4509: +// planned end. While packets are held back, the chain holds the reorder buffer at T-W, so other
4510: +// nodes' later packets do not overtake them in the merged stream.
4511: +//
4512: +// W (500 ms, less for short test segments) covers the stamping difference. Identical frames on
4513: +// the same interface within W of the cut can be paired with each other, which can drop a true
4514: +// repeat; nothing else is lost or doubled. A follow-up segment that does not start in time leaves
4515: +// a gap, which is reported through CaptureRequest.OnGap (or logged), never silently ignored.
4516: +type captureChain struct {
4517: +	capture *captureRun
4518: +	group   *captureGroup
4519: +
4520: +	events chan segmentEvent
4521: +	wg     sync.WaitGroup
4522: +
4523: +	active *captureSegment
4524: +	next   *captureSegment
4525: +	// cut is the switch time between active and next, in nanoseconds; zero until known.
4526: +	cut int64
4527: +	// emitted remembers the content of the packets active wrote while next runs.
4528: +	emitted map[uint64]int
4529: +	// held are the packets of next until active ends.
4530: +	held     []*clabcapture.Packet
4531: +	segments int
4532: +	retries  int
4533: +	// final is set once no further segment is due.
4534: +	final bool
4535: +	// stopping is set once ctx ended: the segments are asked to end and what they still
4536: +	// deliver is written.
4537: +	stopping bool
4538: +}

4540: +// run runs the chain until its last segment ended. When ctx ends, it stops the segments and
4541: +// keeps writing the packets they read until then; a segment that does not end within
4542: +// captureStdinCloseGrace is cut.
4543: +func (c *captureChain) run(ctx context.Context) error {
4544: +	c.events = make(chan segmentEvent, 256)
4545: +	// the segments outlive ctx so they can deliver their last packets; segmentsCtx cuts them
4546: +	segmentsCtx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.WithoutCancel(ctx))
4547: +	var abort *time.Timer
4548: +	defer func() {
4549: +		if abort != nil {
4550: +			abort.Stop()
4551: +		}
4552: +		cancel()
4553: +		c.drain()
4554: +		c.capture.out.Release(c)

4583: +// stop ends the chain early, like a deadline would: no further segment starts and the running
4584: +// ones are asked to end. The chain then writes what they deliver until they ended.

Captures may run longer than an hour; see [Long captures](#long-captures).\n3559: +\n3560: +#### packet-limit\n3561: +\n3562: +The local `--packet-limit` flag stops the capture after that many packets, counted across all targets. `0`, the default, means no limit.\n3563: +\n3564: +#### snap-length\n3565: +\n3566: +The local `--snap-length` flag sets how many bytes of each packet are kept, from 64 to 1048576. The default `0` keeps 256 KiB.\n3567: +\n3568: +#### write\n3569: +\n3570: +The local `--write | -w` flag names the output file. The default `-` writes to stdout.\n3571: +\n3572: +#### list\n3573: +\n3574: +The local `--list` flag lists the interfaces `capture` accepts, for every running node, with the node and interface at the other end of each link, instead of capturing. `--format | -f` selects `table` (default) or `json`.\n3575: +\n3576: +### Output\n3577: +\n3578: +The output is one pcapng section:\n3579: +\n3580: +- a Section Header Block with `shb_userappl` set to `containerlab`\n3581: +- one Interface Description Block per target, in the order of the `--target` flags, written before any packet: link type Ethernet, the snap length, nanosecond timestamps, and the name `<node>:<interface>` (for example `srl1:e1-1`), with the node named as the topology spells it\n3582: +- Enhanced Packet Blocks of all targets, in timestamp order: packets are held briefly (100 ms with Docker and Podman, 250 ms with c9s) and written ordered by timestamp, so packets of different interfaces come out in order even though each one is read on its own; a packet that arrives later than that is written as it comes\n3583: +\n3584: +The interface name shows in Wireshark's interface column (`frame.interface_name`), so a capture of several nodes can be filtered by node and interface.\n3585: +\n3586: +When the capture ends (duration, packet limit, Ctrl+C or SIGTERM), the command finishes the stream and exits with code 0; the file is a valid capture. Status messages go to stderr. With c9s, every `clabwire` capture in the pods ends with the command: containerlab closes its stdin, and `clabwire` (`--stop-on-stdin-close`) stops.\n3587: +\n3588: +`--list -f json` prints an array:\n3589: +\n3590: +```json\n3591: +[\n3592: +  {\n3593: +    \"node\": \"srl1\",\n3594: +    \"interface\": \"e1-1\",\n3595: +    \"alias\": \"ethernet-1/1\",\n3596: +    \"peer_node\": \"srl2\",\n3597: +    \"peer_interface\": \"ethernet-1/1\"\n3598: +  }\n3599: +]\n3600: +```\n3601: +\n3602: +`alias` is present only when the topology used an alias for the interface. `peer_node` is `host` for a host endpoint and `mgmt-net` for a management network endpoint.\n3603: +\n3604: +### How Docker and Podman captures work\n3605: +\n3606: +For each target, containerlab enters the node's network namespace, opens a Linux packet socket (`AF_PACKET`) bound to the interface, and leaves the namespace again; the socket keeps capturing on that interface. This is what `tcpdump` does inside the node, without needing `tcpdump` in the node or on the host. All sockets are opened before the first byte is written, so a capture that cannot start (a node that does not run, a missing interface) fails without output.\n3607: +\n3608: +- Packets carry the kernel's receive timestamps, so packets of different nodes compare on one clock.\n3609: +- 802.1Q tags, which the kernel keeps outside the frame, are put back in place, so VLAN traffic shows its tags as on the wire.\n3610: +- Each socket is in promiscuous mode for as long as it is open; the interface returns to its previous state when the capture ends.\n3611: +- An interface that goes down and up again keeps being captured. When an interface disappears, for example while its node restarts, containerlab waits for it and reattaches once the node is back (`containerlab restart --node`). The time it was gone is reported as a warning with its start and end time.\n3612: +\n3613: +The command needs root (to open packet sockets and enter network namespaces), as other lab commands do.\n3614: +\n3615: +### Long captures\n3616: +\n3617: +Docker and Podman captures have no length limit. With c9s, one `clabwire` capture lasts at most one hour. `capture` chains captures: it starts the next one shortly before the current one ends, lets both run for a few seconds, and switches between them in the middle of that overlap. The repeated section and interface headers of the follow-up are dropped, and packets seen by both captures near the switch are written once (they are matched by content, because each capture stamps packets when it reads them). Once the switch time has passed, the previous capture is stopped through its stdin instead of running to its end. If a follow-up capture does not start in time, the missing interval is reported as a warning with its start and end time; it is never skipped silently. The timestamp order holds across switches: while one node's capture switches, packets of other nodes stamped after the switch wait for it.\n3618: +\n3619: +### Examples\n3620: +\n3621: +#### Capture two nodes for 30 seconds into one file\n3622: +\n3623: +```bash\n3624: +containerlab capture -t srl.clab.yml \\\n3625: +  --target srl1:e1-1 --target srl2:e1-1 --duration 30s -w srl.pcapng\n3626: +```\n3627: +\n3628: +#### Watch a capture live in Wireshark\n3629: +\n3630: +```bash\n3631: +containerlab capture --name srl --target srl1:e1-1,e1-2 -w - | wireshark -k -i -\n3632: +```\n3633: +\n3634: +#### Capture the first 100 packets with tshark\n3635: +\n3636: +```bash\n3637: +containerlab capture --name srl --target srl1:ethernet-1/1 --packet-limit 100 -w - | tshark -r -\n3638: +```\n3639: +\n3640: +#### List the capturable interfaces\n3641: +\n3642: +```bash\n3643: +containerlab capture --name srl --list\n3644: +```\n3645: +\n3646: +#### Capture a c9s lab\n3647: +\n3648: +```bash\n3649: +containerlab -r c9s capture --name srl --target srl1:e1-1 --target srl2:e1-1 -w srl.pcapng\n3650: +```\n3651: diff --git a/docs/cmd/inspect/interfaces.md b/docs/cmd/inspect/interfaces.md\n3652: index 3dc8e27..2354dc1 100644\n3653: --- a/docs/cmd/inspect/interfaces.md\n3654: +++ b/docs/cmd/inspect/interfaces.md\n3655: @@ -3,10 +3,12 @@\n3656:  ### Description\n3657:  \n3658:  The `inspect interfaces` subcommand provides information about the network interfaces of deployed nodes of a deployed lab.\n3659:  The subcommand gathers information directly from deployed containers, and displays information about their operational state, network interface type, and if applicable, the applied network interface alias.\n3660:  \n3661: +With the [c9s runtime](../../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md#packet-capture), the listing covers the lab link interfaces of each running node, the ones [`capture`](../capture.md) accepts, with the alias the topology used, and the MAC address, index, MTU and operational state read in the node's device container. The node names follow `inspect` (`<lab>-<node>`), and the JSON fields are the same as with Docker.\n3662: +\n3663:  ### Usage\n3664:  \n3665:  `containerlab [global-flags] inspect interfaces [local-flags]`\n3666:  \n3667:  A shorthand can be used for this subcommand: `int` or `intf`.\n3668: diff --git a/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md b/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md\n3669: index 0ce708d..8174c98 100644\n3670: --- a/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md\n3671: +++ b/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md\n3672: @@ -110,10 +110,13 @@ The c9s runtime currently supports the main lab lifecycle and node operations:\n3673:  | `start` | sets the node's `spec.runState` to `Running` |\n3674:  | `stop` | sets the node's `spec.runState` to `Stopped` |\n3675:  | `restart` | requests a Pod replacement with a `c9s.run/restart-requested` token |\n3676:  | `save` | runs the node's save lifecycle inside its device container |\n3677:  | `events` | watches Clabernetes resources and pods |\n3678: +| `logs` | streams the device container log |\n3679: +| `capture` | captures lab link interfaces through the `clabwire` sidecar into one pcapng stream |\n3680: +| `inspect interfaces` | lists the capturable link interfaces with their sysfs state |\n3681:  | `validate` | checks c9s compatibility without creating Kubernetes resources |\n3682:  | `deploy --dry-run` | compiles and diffs Namespace, ConfigMap, NodeProfile, Link, and Node resources without changing them |\n3683:  | `deploy --emit-crs` | prints the Namespace, ConfigMap, and Topology (or NodeProfile, Link, and Node) manifests deploy would create, without contacting the cluster |\n3684:  \n3685:  ## Requirements\n3686: @@ -141,11 +144,11 @@ Containerlab needs a clabernetes release that has:\n3687:  \n3688:  - Each node's stream arrives over its\n3758: +  own exec stream, so the merged stream holds every packet for 250 ms and\n3759: +  writes the held packets ordered by timestamp. A packet that arrives later\n3760: +  than that, stamped before a packet already written, is written as it comes;\n3761: +  the number of such packets goes to the debug log.\n3762: +- `clabwire` limits one capture to one hour. Longer captures, and captures\n3763: +  without `--duration`, chain captures with a few seconds of overlap and switch\n3764: +  in the middle of it; packets near the switch are matched by content so each\n3765: +  is written once. A follow-up that does not start in time is reported as a\n3766: +  gap, with its time span.\n3767: +- `clabwire` audit records (JSON on its stderr, schema\n3768: +  `c9s.direct-packet-capture-audit/v1alpha1`) with status `Denied` or `Failed`\n3769: +  end the command with their reason. `Started` and `Succeeded` go to the debug\n3770: +  log.\n3771: +\n3772: +Interface names are the names inside the node; targets may also use the alias\n3773: +the topology used for an interface:\n3774: +\n3775: +| Kind | Interface | Alias |\n3776: +| ---- | --------- | ----- |\n3777: +| linux | `eth1` | |\n3778: +| SR Linux | `e1-1` | `ethernet-1/1` |\n3779: +| vr-sros / nokia_sros | `eth3` | `1/1/3` |\n3780: +\n3781: +The management interface and the pod's `c9s0` interface cannot be captured.\n3782: +\n3783: +Ctrl+C or SIGTERM ends a capture cleanly: the output stays a valid pcapng\n3784: +file and the command exits with code 0. Nothing runs in the node, the node image needs no capture tools, and no extra software is needed on the host: the command needs root, like `deploy`. See [How Docker and Podman captures work](#how-docker-and-podman-captures-work).\n+- **c9s**: the `clabwire` sidecar of each node's pod captures the packets; see the [c9s runtime](../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md#packet-capture).\n+\n+The output is the same with both. [Edgeshark](../manual/wireshark.md) remains an alternative for Docker labs when you prefer to pick interfaces in a GUI.\n+\n+--8<-- \"docs/cmd/deploy.md:env-vars-flags\"\n+\n+### Usage\n+\n+`containerlab [global-flags] capture [local-flags]`\n+\n+### Flags\n+\n+#### topology | name\n+\n+Use the global `--topo | -t` flag to reference the lab topology file, or use the global `--name` flag to reference an already deployed lab by name. Without either, containerlab looks for a `*.clab.yml` file in the current directory, like the other lab commands.\n+\n+With Docker and Podman, the capturable interfaces are the links of the topology file, so `--name` needs the topology file the lab was deployed from to still be in place.\n+\n+#### target\n+\n+The local `--target` flag selects what to capture, as `<node>:<interface>[,<interface>...]`. Repeat it for more nodes:\n+\n+```text\n+--target srl1:e1-1,e1-2 --target srl2:e1-1\n+```\n+\n+The node name ends at the first colon, so interface names such as `1/1/3` or `ethernet-1/1` need no quoting. Node names are accepted as the topology file spells them; with Docker and Podman also as the container name (`clab-srl-srl1`), with c9s also as they were sanitized for Kubernetes (`R1` or `r1`). Interfaces are accepted by their name in the node or by the alias the topology used for them (`e1-1` or `ethernet-1/1` for SR Linux). `--list` shows both.\n+\n+Only lab link interfaces can be captured; the management interface cannot. An interface that is not a link interface of the node fails the command before anything is captured, and the error lists the node's capturable interfaces.\n+\n+#### duration\n+\n+The local `--duration` flag stops the capture after the given time (`30s`, `5m`, `2h`). The default `0` captures until the command is interrupted with Ctrl+C or SIGTERM. Captures may run longer than an hour; see [Long captures](#long-captures).\n+\n+#### packet-limit\n+\n+The local `--packet-limit` flag stops the capture after that many packets, counted across all targets. `0`, the default, means no limit.\n+\n+#### snap-length\n+\n+The local `--snap-length` flag sets how many bytes of each packet are kept, from 64 to 1048576. The default `0` keeps 256 KiB.\n+\n+#### write\n+\n+The local `--write | -w` flag names the output file. The default `-` writes to stdout.\n+\n+#### list\n+\n+The local `--list` flag lists the interfaces `capture` accepts, for every running node, with the node and interface at the other end of each link, instead of capturing. `--format | -f` selects `table` (default) or `json`.\n+\n+### Output\n+\n+The output is one pcapng section:\n+\n+- a Section Header Block with `shb_userappl` set to `containerlab`\n+- one Interface Description Block per target, in the order of the `--target` flags, written before any packet: link type Ethernet, the snap length, nanosecond timestamps, and the name `<node>:<interface>` (for example `srl1:e1-1`), with the node named as the topology spells it\n+- Enhanced Packet Blocks of all targets, in timestamp order: packets are held briefly (100 ms with Docker and Podman, 250 ms with c9s) and written ordered by timestamp, so packets of different interfaces come out in order even though each one is read on its own; a packet that arrives later than that is written as it comes\n+\n+The interface name shows in Wireshark's interface column (`frame.interface_name`), so a capture of several nodes can be filtered by node and interface.\n+\n+When the capture ends (duration, packet limit, Ctrl+C or SIGTERM), the command finishes the stream and exits with code 0; the file is a valid capture. Status messages go to stderr. With c9s, every `clabwire` capture in the pods ends with the command: containerlab closes its stdin, and `clabwire` (`--stop-on-stdin-close`) stops.\n+\n+`--list -f json` prints an array:\n+\n+```json\n+[\n+  {\n+    \"node\": \"srl1\",\n+    \"interface\": \"e1-1\",\n+    \"alias\": \"ethernet-1/1\",\n+    \"peer_node\": \"srl2\",\n+    \"peer_interface\": \"ethernet-1/1\"\n+  }\n+]\n+```\n+\n+`alias` is present only when the topology used an alias for the interface. `peer_node` is `host` for a host endpoint and `mgmt-net` for a management network endpoint.\n+\n+### How Docker and Podman captures work\n+\n+For each target, containerlab enters the node's network namespace, opens a Linux packet socket (`AF_PACKET`) bound to the interface, and leaves the namespace again; the socket keeps capturing on that interface. This is what `tcpdump` does inside the node, without needing `tcpdump` in the node or on the host. All sockets are opened before the first byte is written, so a capture that cannot start (a node that does not run, a missing interface) fails without output.\n+\n+- Packets carry the kernel's receive timestamps, so packets of different nodes compare on one clock.\n+- 802.1Q tags, which the kernel keeps outside the frame, are put back in place, so VLAN traffic shows its tags as on the wire.\n+- Each socket is in promiscuous mode for as long as it is open; the interface returns to its previous state when the capture ends.\n+- An interface that goes down and up again keeps being captured. When an interface disappears, for example while its node restarts, containerlab waits for it and reattaches once the node is back (`containerlab restart --node`). The time it was gone is reported as a warning with its start and end time.\n+\n+The command needs root (to open packet sockets and enter network namespaces), as other lab commands do.\n+\n+### Long captures\n+\n+Docker and Podman captures have no length limit. With c9s, one `clabwire` capture lasts at most one hour. `capture` chains captures: it starts the next one shortly before the current one ends, lets both run for a few seconds, and switches between them in the middle of that overlap. The repeated section and interface headers of the follow-up are dropped, and packets seen by both captures near the switch are written once (they are matched by content, because each capture stamps packets when it reads them). Once the switch time has passed, the previous capture is stopped through its stdin instead of running to its end. If a follow-up capture does not start in time, the missing interval is reported as a warning with its start and end time; it is never skipped silently. The timestamp order holds across switches: while one node's capture switches, packets of other nodes stamped after the switch wait for it.\n+\n+### Examples\n+\n+#### Capture two nodes for 30 seconds into one file\n+\n+```bash\n+containerlab capture -t srl.clab.yml \\\n+  --target srl1:e1-1 --target srl2:e1-1 --duration 30s -w srl.pcapng\n+```\n+\n+#### Watch a capture live in Wireshark\n+\n+```bash\n+containerlab capture --name srl --target srl1:e1-1,e1-2 -w - | wireshark -k -i -\n+```\n+\n+#### Capture the first 100 packets with tshark\n+\n+```bash\n+containerlab capture --name srl --target srl1:ethernet-1/1 --packet-limit 100 -w - | tshark -r -\n+```\n+\n+#### List the capturable interfaces\n+\n+```bash\n+containerlab capture --name srl --list\n+```\n+\n+#### Capture a c9s lab\n+\n+```bash\n+containerlab -r c9s capture --name srl --target srl1:e1-1 --target srl2:e1-1 -w srl.pcapng\n+```\ndiff --git a/docs/cmd/inspect/interfaces.md b/docs/cmd/inspect/interfaces.md\nindex 3dc8e27..2354dc1 100644\n--- a/docs/cmd/inspect/interfaces.md\n+++ b/docs/cmd/inspect/interfaces.md\n@@ -3,10 +3,12 @@\n ### Description\n \n The `inspect interfaces` subcommand provides information about the network interfaces of deployed nodes of a deployed lab.\n The subcommand gathers information directly from deployed containers, and displays information about their operational state, network interface type, and if applicable, the applied network interface alias.\n \n+With the [c9s runtime](../../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md#packet-capture), the listing covers the lab link interfaces of each running node, the ones [`capture`](../capture.md) accepts, with the alias the topology used, and the MAC address, index, MTU and operational state read in the node's device container. See\n the [`logs` command](../../cmd/logs.md) for the flags.\n \n+## Packet capture\n+\n+[`containerlab capture`](../../cmd/capture.md) captures lab link interfaces of\n+one or more nodes into one pcapng stream. Each node's stream arrives over its\n+  own exec stream, so the merged stream holds every packet for 250 ms and\n+  writes the held packets ordered by timestamp. A packet that arrives later\n+  than that, stamped before a packet already written, is written as it comes;\n+  the number of such packets goes to the debug log.\n+- `clabwire` limits one capture to one hour. Longer captures, and captures\n+  without `--duration`, chain captures with a few seconds of overlap and switch\n+  in the middle of it; packets near the switch are matched by content so each\n+  is written once. Kubernetes does not stop a command\n+when its exec stream closes, but it closes the command's stdin. containerlab\n+closes the stdin of every `clabwire` capture when the capture ends for any\n+reason (the duration or packet limit, Ctrl+C, an error, a failed write of the\n+output such as a closed Wireshark, or a newer segment taking over), and\n+`clabwire` then ends the capture within milliseconds. If the process does not\n+end within three seconds, containerlab cuts the exec stream. A killed\n+containerlab drops the connection, which closes stdin as well.\n+\n+Capturing needs `get` and `create` on `pods/exec` in the lab namespace, which\n+`clabernetes-lab-editor` grants. `inspect interfaces -r c9s` lists the same\n+interfaces, with the MAC address, index, MTU and operational state read from\n+sysfs in the device container (type `veth`, which is how `clabwire` realizes\n+lab 4785: +// switchSegments makes the next segment the active one after the active one ended, writing the
4786: +// held packets of the next one that the active one did not write.
4787: +func (c *captureChain) switchSegments(ctx context.Context, timer *time.Timer) (bool, error) {
4788: +	// the held packets are in the reorder buffer once this returns
4789: +	defer c.capture.out.Release(c)
4790: +
4791: +	ended := c.active
4792: +	if c.stopping && c.next != nil && c.next.started.IsZero() {
4793: +		// the chain is stopping: a follow-up that has not started takes nothing over
4794: +		c.next, c.held, c.emitted, c.cut = nil, nil, nil, 0
4795: +	}
4796: +	if c.final && c.next == nil {
4797: +		return true, nil
4798: +	}
4799: +
4800: +	if c.next == nil || c.next.started.IsZero() || c.cut == 0 {
4801: +		from := ended.ended
4802: +		if from.IsZero() {
4803: +			from = ended.plannedEnd()
4804: +		}
4805: +		gap := clablabruntime.CaptureGap{
4806: +			Node: c.group.display, Interfaces: c.group.interfaces, From: from,
4807: +			Reason: "the follow-up capture did not overlap the previous one",
4808: +		}
4809: +		if c.next != nil && !c.next.started.IsZero() {
4810: +			gap.To = c.next.started
4811: +		}
4812: +		c.capture.reportGap(gap)
4813: +	}
4814: +
4815: +	if c.next != nil && c.next.done && !c.stopping {
4816: +		// the follow-up already ended (it started too late to take over): keep what it
4817: +		// captured and continue with a fresh segment
4818: +		for _, packet := range c.held {
4819: +			if stop, err := c.emit(packet); stop || err != nil {
4820: +				return true, err
4821: +			}
4822: +		}
4823: +		c.next, c.held, c.emitted, c.cut = nil, nil, nil, 0
4824: +	}
4825: +
4826: +	if c.next == nil {
4827: +		if !c.capture.deadline.IsZero() &&
4828: +			!time.Now().Before(c.capture.deadline.Add(-c.capture.window)) {
4829: +			return true, nil
4830: +		}
4831: +		c.active = c.start(ctx, c.segmentDuration(time.Now()))
4832: +		resetTimer(timer, c.nextStartIn())
4833: +
4834: +		return false, nil
4835: +	}
4836: +
4837: +	window := c.capture.window.Nanoseconds()
4838: +	for _, packet := range c.held {
4839: +		if c.cut != 0 {
4840: +			if packet.Timestamp < c.cut-window {
4841: +				continue
4842: +			}
4843: +			if packet.Timestamp < c.cut+window {
4844: +				key := packetKey(packet)
4845: +				if c.emitted[key] > 0 {
4846: +					c.emitted[key]--
4847: +					continue
4848: +				}
4849: +			}
4850: +		}
4851: +		if stop, err := c.emit(packet); stop || err != nil {
4852: +			return true, err
4853: +		}
4854: +	}
4855: +
4856: +	c.active, c.next = c.next, nil
4857: +	c.held, c.emitted, c.cut = nil, nil, 0
4858: +	if c.active.done {
4859: +		// the chain is stopping and the follow-up ended before the active one
4860: +		return true, nil
4861: +	}
4862: +	resetTimer(timer, c.nextStartIn())
4863: +
4864: +	return false, nil
4865: +}
4866: +
4867: +func resetTimer(timer *time.Timer, d time.Duration) {
4868: +	if !timer.Stop() {
4869: +		select {
4870: +		case <-timer.C:
4871: +		default:
4872: +		}
4873: +	}
4874: +	timer.Reset(d)
4875: +}
4876: +
4877: +// packetKey identifies a packet by its interface and content.
4878: +func packetKey(packet *clabcapture.Packet) uint64 {
4879: +	hash := fnv.New64a()
4880: +	var id [4]byte
4881: +	id[0] = byte(packet.InterfaceID)
4882: +	id[1] = byte(packet.InterfaceID >> 8)
4883: +	_, _ = hash.Write(id[:])
4884: +	_, _ = hash.Write(packet.Data)
4885: +
4886: +	return hash.Sum64()
4887: +}
4888: +
4889: +// start runs one clabwire capture and reports its packets, audit records and end as events.
4890: +func (c *captureChain) start(ctx context.Context, duration time.Duration) *captureSegment {
4891: +	segmentCtx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
4892: +	stdinReader, stdinWriter := io.Pipe()
4893: +	segment := &captureSegment{
4894: +		index: c.segments, localStart: time.Now(), duration: duration, cancel: cancel,
4895: +		closeStdin: func() { _ = stdinWriter.Close() },
4896: +	}
4897: +	c.segments++
4898: +
4899: +	command := []string{
4900: +		clabwireManager, "node-runtime", "packet-capture",
4901: +		"--nodeName", c.group.location.NodeName,
4902: +		"--format", "pcapng",
4903: +		"--snapLength", strconv.Itoa(c.capture.req.SnapLength),
4904: +		"--duration", duration.String(),
4905: +		clabwireStopOnStdinClose,
4906: +	}
4907: +	for _, name := range c.group.interfaces {
4908: +		command = append(command, "--interface", name)
4909: +	}
4910: +	if c.capture.req.PacketLimit > 0 {
4911: +		remaining := int64(c.capture.req.PacketLimit) - c.capture.out.Written()
4912: +		command = append(command, "--packetLimit",
4913: +			strconv.FormatInt(min(max(remaining, 1), maxClabwirePackets), 10))
4914: +	}
4915: +
4916: +	send := func(event segmentEvent) {
4917: +		event.segment = segment
4918: +		select {
4919: +		case c.events <- event:
4920: +		case <-segmentCtx.Done():
4921: +		}
4922: +	}
4923: +
4924: +	stdoutReader, stdoutWriter := io.Pipe()
4925: +	stderr := &auditLineWriter{send: func(audit *captureAudit) { send(segmentEvent{audit: audit}) }}
4926: +
4927: +	// The exec outlives the segment's context by up to captureStdinCloseGrace: when the segment
4928: +	// ends for any reason (the capture is cancelled or failed, the output failed, or a newer
4929: +	// segment took over), its stdin is closed first so clabwire ends on its own, and the stream
4930: +	// is cut only if it does not.
4931: +	execCtx, cancelExec := context.WithCancel(context.WithoutCancel(segmentCtx))
4932: +	execDone := make(chan struct{})
4933: +
4934: +	c.wg.Add(3)
4935: +	readDone := make(chan error, 1)
4936: +	go func() {
4937: +		defer c.wg.Done()
4938: +		readDone <- c.readSegment(stdoutReader, func(packet *clabcapture.Packet) {
4939: +			send(segmentEvent{packet: packet})
4940: +		})
4941: +		_, _ = io.Copy(io.Discard, stdoutReader)
4942: +	}()
4943: +	go func() {
4944: +		defer c.wg.Done()
4945: +		select {
4946: +		case <-execDone:
4947: +			return
4948: +		case <-segmentCtx.Done():
4949: +		}
4950: +		segment.closeStdin()
4951: +		grace := time.NewTimer(captureStdinCloseGrace)
4952: +		defer grace.Stop()
4953: +		select {
4954: +		case <-execDone:
4955: +		case <-grace.C:
4956: +			log.Debug("Capture segment did not end after its stdin closed, cutting the stream",
4957: +				"node", c.group.display, "segment", segment.index)
4958: +			cancelExec()
4959: +		}
4960: +	}()
4961: +	go func() {
4962: +		defer c.wg.Done()
4963: +		defer cancel()
4964: +		defer cancelExec()
4965: +
4966: +		err := c.capture.r.execInPodContainer()(execCtx, c.group.location.Namespace,
4967: +			c.group.location.Pod, clabwireContainer, command, stdinReader, stdoutWriter, stderr)
4968: +		close(execDone)
4969: +		// the process ended: release the stdin copy of the exec stream
4970: +		segment.closeStdin()
4971: +		_ = stdoutWriter.Close()
4972: +		readErr := <-readDone
4973: +		stderr.flush()
4974: +		if err == nil && readErr != nil {
4975: +			err = readErr
4976: +		}
4977: +		if err != nil && stderr.text() != "" {
4978: +			if unsupported := unsupportedClabwire(
4979: +				c.group.location,
4980: +				stderr.text(),
4981: +			); unsupported != nil {
4982: +				err = unsupported
4983: +			} else {
4984: +				err = fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", err, stderr.text())
4985: +			}
4986: +		}
4987: +		send(segmentEvent{done: true, err: err})
4988: +	}()
4989: +
4990: +	return segment
4991: +}
4992: +
4993: +// unsupportedClabwire recognizes a clabwire that rejects --stop-on-stdin-close, which every
4994: +// capture passes: its release predates the capture contract the runtime needs.
4995: +func unsupportedClabwire(location clablabruntime.NodeLocation, stderr string) error {
4996: +	if !strings.Contains(stderr, "flag provided but not defined") ||
4997: +		!strings.Contains(stderr, strings.TrimPrefix(clabwireStopOnStdinClose, "-")) {
4998: +		return nil
4999: +	}
5000: +
5001: +	return &unsupportedClabernetesError{reason: fmt.Sprintf(
5002: +		"clabwire in pod %s/%s does not accept packet-capture %s",
5003: +		location.Namespace, location.Pod, clabwireStopOnStdinClose)}
5004: +}
5005: +
5006: +// readSegment checks that a segment's interfaces are the requested ones and passes its packets
5007: +// on with the segment's interface index.
5008: +func (c *captureChain) readSegment(stdout io.Reader, packet func(*clabcapture.Packet)) error {
5009: +	reader := clabcapture.NewReader(stdout)
5010: +	interfaces := 0
5011: +	for {
5012: +		event, err := reader.Next()
5013: +		if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
5014: +			return nil
5015: +		}
5016: +		if errors.Is(err, io.ErrUnexpectedEOF) {
5017: +			// the process was stopped inside a block
5018: +			return nil
5019: +		}
5020: +		if err != nil {
5021: +			return fmt.Errorf("failed to read the clabwire capture: %w", err)
5022: +		}
5023: +		if event.Interface != nil {
5024: +			if interfaces >= len(c.group.interfaces) ||
5025: +				event.Interface.Name != c.group.interfaces[interfaces] {
5026: +				return fmt.Errorf("clabwire described interface %q, want %s in order",
5027: +					event.Interface.Name, strings.Join(c.group.interfaces, ", "))
5028: +			}
5029: +			interfaces++
5030: +			continue
5031: +		}
5032: +		if event.Packet != nil {
5033: +			packet(event.Packet)
5034: +		}
5035: +	}
5036: +}
5037: +
5038: +// auditLineWriter parses clabwire's stderr: audit records go to send, other lines are kept for
5039: +// error messages.
5040: +type auditLineWriter struct {
5041: +	send func(*captureAudit)
5042: +
5043: +	mu      sync.Mutex
5044: +	partial []byte
5045: +	other   []string
5046: +}
5047: +
5048: +func (w *auditLineWriter) Write(data []byte) (int, error) {
5049: +	w.mu.Lock()
5050: +	w.partial = append(w.partial, data...)
5051: +	var lines [][]byte
5052: +	for {
5053: +		idx := bytes.IndexByte(w.partial, '\n')
5054: +		if idx < 0 {
5055: +			break
5056: +		}
5057: +		lines = append(lines, append([]byte(nil), w.partial[:idx]...))
5058: +		w.partial = w.partial[idx+1:]
5059: +	}
5060: +	w.mu.Unlock()
5061: +
5062: +	for _, line := range lines {
5063: +		w.line(line)
5064: +	}
5065: +
5066: +	return len(data), nil
5067: +}
5068: +
5069: +func (w *auditLineWriter) flush() {
5070: +	w.mu.Lock()
5071: +	line := w.partial
5072: +	w.partial = nil
5073: +	w.mu.Unlock()
5074: +	if len(bytes.TrimSpace(line)) != 0 {
5075: +		w.line(line)
5076: +	}
5077: +}
5078: +
5079: +func (w *auditLineWriter) line(line []byte) {
5080: +	line = bytes.TrimSpace(line)
5081: +	if len(line) == 0 {
5082: +		return
5083: +	}
5084: +
5085: +	var audit captureAudit
5086: +	if err := json.Unmarshal(
5087: +		line,
5088: +		&audit,
5089: +	); err == nil &&
5090: +		audit.SchemaVersion == captureAuditSchema {
5091: +		w.send(&audit)
5092: +		return
5093: +	}
5094: +
5095: +	w.mu.Lock()
5096: +	defer w.mu.Unlock()
5097: +	if len(w.other) < 20 {
5098: +		w.other = append(w.other, string(line))
5099: +	}
5100: +}
5101: +
5102: +func (w *auditLineWriter) text() string {
5103: +	w.mu.Lock()
5104: +	defer w.mu.Unlock()
5105: +
5106: +	return strings.Join(w.other, "; ")
5107: +}

5133: +
5134: +// streamPodExec runs a command in a pod container without a terminal and streams its stdout
5135: +// and stderr. A non-nil stdin is attached: when it ends, the process's stdin is closed (the
5136: +// websocket v5 close signal, or a half-closed SPDY stream). A nonzero exit returns a
5137: +// *labruntime.CommandExitError.
5138: +func (r *Runtime) streamPodExec(
5139: +	ctx context.Context,
5140: +	namespace, pod, container string,
5141: +	command []string,
5142: +	stdin io.Reader,
5143: +	stdout, stderr io.Writer,
5144: +) error {
5145: +	execURL := r.kubeClient.CoreV1().RESTClient().Post().
5146: +		Resource("pods").
5147: +		Name(pod).
5148: +		Namespace(namespace).
5149: +		SubResource("exec").
5150: +		VersionedParams(&corev1.PodExecOptions{
5151: +			Container: container,
5152: +			Command:   command,
5153: +			Stdin:     stdin != nil,
5154: +			Stdout:    stdout != nil,
5155: +			Stderr:    stderr != nil,
5156: +		}, scheme.ParameterCodec).URL()
5157: +
5158: +	executor, err := r.newExecutor(execURL)
5159: +	if err != nil {
5160: +		return err
5161: +	}
5162: +
5163: +	// client-go reports streams cut by a cancelled context through the context's logger; a
5164: +	// capture ends that way on purpose, so it goes to the debug log
5165: +	err = executor.StreamWithContext(withKubernetesClientDebugLogs(ctx),
5166: +		remotecommand.StreamOptions{
5167: +			Stdin:  stdin,
5168: +			Stdout: stdout,
5169: +			Stderr: stderr,
5170: +		})
5171: +
5172: +	var exitErr kubeexec.ExitError
5173: +	if errors.As(err, &exitErr) {
5174: +		return &clablabruntime.CommandExitError{Code: exitErr.ExitStatus()}
5175: +	}
5176: +	if err != nil {
5177: +		return fmt.Errorf("failed to execute command in pod %s/%s container %s: %w",
5178: +			namespace, pod, container, err)
5179: +	}
5180: +
5181: +	return nil
5182: +}

5184: +// InspectInterfaces lists the capturable link interfaces of the requested nodes, or of every
5185: +// running node, in the shape of `inspect interfaces`: per node (named <lab>-<node> like in
5186: +// inspect), the interface and its alias as clabwire reports them, and the MAC address, index,
5187: +// MTU and operational state read from sysfs in the device container. A node whose device
5188: +// container has no shell reports its interfaces without these attributes.
5189: +func (r *Runtime) InspectInterfaces(
5190: +	ctx context.Context,
5191: +	req clablabruntime.NodeRequest,
5192: +) ([]*clabtypes.ContainerInterfaces, error) {
5193: +	r, err := r.connect(ctx, req.Identity)
5194: +	if err != nil {
5195: +		return nil, err
5196: +	}
5197: +
5198: +	locations, err := r.LocateNode(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
5199: +		Name: req.Name, Namespace: req.Namespace, Nodes: req.Nodes, Identity: req.Identity,
5200: +	})
5201: +	if err != nil {
5202: +		return nil, err
5203: +	}
5204: +
5205: +	running := make([]clablabruntime.NodeLocation, 0, len(locations))
5206: +	for _, location := range locations {
5207: +		if location.Pod == "" {
5208: +			log.Warn("Skipping interface detection of a node that does not run",
5209: +				"node", location.NodeName)
5210: +			continue
5211: +		}
5212: +		running = append(running, location)
5213: +	}
5214: +
5215: +	listed, err := r.listCaptureInterfaces(ctx, req.Name, running)
5216: +	if err != nil {
5217: +		return nil, err
5218: +	}
5219: +	states := r.sampleInterfaceStates(ctx, running)
5220: +
5221: +	result := make([]*clabtypes.ContainerInterfaces, 0, len(running))
5222: +	for _, location := range running {
5223: +		container := &clabtypes.ContainerInterfaces{
5224: +			ContainerName: req.Name + "-" + location.NodeName,
5225: +			Interfaces:    []*clabtypes.ContainerInterfaceDetails{},
5226: +		}
5227: +		for _, entry := range listed[location.NodeName] {
5228: +			details := &clabtypes.ContainerInterfaceDetails{
5229: +				InterfaceName:  entry.Interface,
5230: +				InterfaceAlias: entry.Alias,
5231: +				// clabwire realizes every lab link interface as a veth pair
5232: +				InterfaceType: "veth",
5233: +			}
5234: +			if state, ok := states[location.NodeName][entry.Interface]; ok {
5235: +				details.InterfaceMAC = state.MAC
5236: +				details.InterfaceIndex = state.Index
5237: +				details.InterfaceMTU = state.MTU
5238: +				details.InterfaceState = state.OperState
5239: +			}
5240: +			container.Interfaces = append(container.Interfaces, details)
5241: +		}
5242: +		sort.Slice(container.Interfaces, func(i, j int) bool {
5243: +			return container.Interfaces[i].InterfaceName < container.Interfaces[j].InterfaceName
5244: +		})
5245: +		result = append(result, container)
5246: +	}
5247: +	sort.Slice(result, func(i, j int) bool {
5248: +		return result[i].ContainerName < result[j].ContainerName
5249: +	})
5250: +
5251: +	return result, nil
5252: +}
5253: +
5254: +// sampleInterfaceStates reads the sysfs interface attributes of every node's device container,
5255: +// one exec per node, with the script the interface events use.
5256: +func (r *Runtime) sampleInterfaceStates(
5257: +	ctx context.Context,
5258: +	locations []clablabruntime.NodeLocation,
5259: +) map[string]map[string]c9sIfaceState {
5260: +	var mu sync.Mutex
5261: +	result := map[string]map[string]c9sIfaceState{}
5262: +
5263: +	var wg sync.WaitGroup
5264: +	workers := make(chan struct{}, interfaceSampleWorkers)
5265: +	exec := r.execInPodContainer()
5266: +	for _, location := range locations {
5267: +		wg.Add(1)
5268: +		go func() {
5269: +			defer wg.Done()
5270: +			workers <- struct{}{}
5271: +			defer func() { <-workers }()
5272: +
5273: +			var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
5274: +			err := exec(ctx, location.Namespace, location.Pod, location.Container,
5275: +				[]string{"sh", "-c", interfaceSampleScript}, nil, &stdout, &stderr)
5276: +			if err != nil {
5277: +				log.Debug("Cannot read the interface state of a c9s node",
5278: +					"node", location.NodeName, "error", err)
5279: +				return
5280: +			}
5281: +			_, ifaces, _, err := parseInterfaceSample(stdout.Bytes())
5282: +			if err != nil {
5283: +				log.Debug("Cannot parse the interface state of a c9s node",
5284: +					"node", location.NodeName, "error", err)
5285: +				return
5286: +			}
5287: +
5288: +			byName := make(map[string]c9sIfaceState, len(ifaces))
5289: +			for _, iface := range ifaces {
5290: +				byName[iface.Name] = iface
5291: +			}
5292: +			mu.Lock()
5293: +			result[location.NodeName] = byName
5294: +			mu.Unlock()
5295: +		}()
5296: +	}
5297: +	wg.Wait()
5298: +
5299: +	return result
5300: +}

5327: +	"k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1/unstructured"
5328: +	k8sruntime "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/runtime"
5329: +)

5364: +var captureListing = map[string][]clabwireInterface{ //nolint:gochecknoglobals
5365: +	"lab1-r1-abc": {

5367: +			Node:          "r1",
5368: +			Interface:     "e1-1",

5374: +	},
5375: +	"lab1-r2-def": {
5376: +		{
5377: +			Node:          "r2",
5378: +			Interface:     "e1-1",
5379: +			Alias:         "ethernet-1/1",
5380: +			PeerNode:      "r1",
