5386: +// fakeClabwire plays clabwire packet-capture and --list-interfaces in the fake pod exec. Every
5387: +// capture process sees the same traffic: one packet per tick on each requested interface,
5388: +// carrying the tick number, stamped with the tick time plus a per-process jitter (clabwire stamps
5389: +// packets when it reads them).
5390: +type fakeClabwire struct {
5391: +	t     *testing.T
5392: +	epoch time.Time
5393: +	tick  time.Duration
5394: +
5395: +	mu       sync.Mutex
5396: +	commands [][]string
5397: +	// processes counts the capture processes started per node
5398: +	processes map[string]int
5399: +
5400: +	// startDelay delays the Started record of the given process index (all nodes).
5401: +	startDelay map[int]time.Duration
5402: +	// firstStartDelay delays the Started record of a node's first process.
5403: +	firstStartDelay map[string]time.Duration
5404: +	// fail makes a process write this audit status and exit 1.
5405: +	fail string
5406: +	// stderrOnly makes a process write this text to stderr and exit 1, like a clabwire that
5407: +	// rejects a flag.
5408: +	stderrOnly string
5409: +	// stampSkew stamps the packets of a node this much earlier, as if its stream reached
5410: +	// containerlab this much later than the others.
5411: +	stampSkew map[string]time.Duration
5412: +	// stdinClosed counts the processes that ended because their stdin closed, per node.
5413: +	stdinClosed map[string]int
5414: +	// written counts the packets written to stdout, per node.
5415: +	written map[string]int
5416: +	// sysfs is the device container's interface sample.
5417: +	sysfs string
5418: +}
5419: +
5420: +func newFakeClabwire(t *testing.T, tick time.Duration) *fakeClabwire {
5421: +	t.Helper()
5422: +
5423: +	return &fakeClabwire{
5424: +		t: t, epoch: time.Now(), tick: tick, processes: map[string]int{},
5425: +		startDelay: map[int]time.Duration{}, stampSkew: map[string]time.Duration{},
5426: +		firstStartDelay: map[string]time.Duration{},
5427: +		stdinClosed:     map[string]int{},
5428: +		written:         map[string]int{},
5429: +	}
5430: +}
5431: +
5432: +func (f *fakeClabwire) exec(
5433: +	ctx context.Context,
5434: +	namespace, pod, container string,
5435: +	command []string,
5436: +	stdin io.Reader,
5437: +	stdout, stderr io.Writer,
5438: +) error {
5439: +	f.mu.Lock()
5440: +	f.commands = append(
5441: +		f.commands,
5442: +		append([]string{namespace + "/" + pod + "/" + container}, command...),
5443: +	)
5444: +	f.mu.Unlock()
5445: +
5446: +	if container != clabwireContainer {
5447: +		_, _ = io.WriteString(stdout, f.sysfs)
5448: +		return nil
5449: +	}
5450: +	if slices.Contains(command, "--list-interfaces") {
5451: +		return json.NewEncoder(stdout).Encode(captureListing[pod])
5452: +	}
5453: +
5454: +	return f.capture(ctx, command, stdin, stdout, stderr)
5455: +}
5456: +
5457: +func flagValues(command []string, name string) []string {
5458: +	var values []string
5459: +	for idx := 0; idx+1 < len(command); idx++ {
5460: +		if command[idx] == name {
5461: +			values = append(values, command[idx+1])
5462: +		}
5463: +	}
5464: +
5465: +	return values
5466: +}
5467: +
5468: +func (f *fakeClabwire) audit(
5469: +	stderr io.Writer,
5470: +	status, node string,
5471: +	interfaces []string,
5472: +	reason string,
5473: +) {
5474: +	record := map[string]any{
5475: +		"schemaVersion": captureAuditSchema, "time": time.Now().UTC(), "operation": "PacketCapture",
5476: +		"status": status, "nodeName": node, "format": "pcapng", "reason": reason,
5477: +	}
5478: +	entries := []map[string]any{}
5479: +	for _, name := range interfaces {
5480: +		entries = append(entries, map[string]any{"name": name})
5481: +	}
5482: +	record["interfaces"] = entries
5483: +	data, _ := json.Marshal(record)
5484: +	_, _ = stderr.Write(append(data, '\n'))
5485: +}
5486: +
5487: +func (f *fakeClabwire) capture(
5488: +	ctx context.Context,
5489: +	command []string,
5490: +	stdin io.Reader,
5491: +	stdout, stderr io.Writer,
5492: +) error {
5493: +	f.mu.Lock()
5494: +	rejected := f.stderrOnly
5495: +	f.mu.Unlock()
5496: +	if rejected != "" {
5497: +		_, _ = io.WriteString(stdout, "Incorrect Usage: "+rejected+"\n\nNAME:\n   manager\n")
5498: +		_, _ = io.WriteString(stderr, rejected+"\n")
5499: +		return &clablabruntime.CommandExitError{Code: 1}
5500: +	}
5501: +
5502: +	// clabwire ends the capture when stdin closes (--stop-on-stdin-close)
5503: +	if !slices.Contains(command, clabwireStopOnStdinClose) || stdin == nil {
5504: +		f.t.Errorf("capture without stdin and %s: %v", clabwireStopOnStdinClose, command)
5505: +		return fmt.Errorf("no stdin")
5506: +	}
5507: +	stdinClosed := make(chan struct{})
5508: +	go func() {
5509: +		_, _ = io.Copy(io.Discard, stdin)
5510: +		close(stdinClosed)
5511: +	}()
5512: +
5513: +	node := flagValues(command, "--nodeName")[0]
5514: +	interfaces := flagValues(command, "--interface")
5515: +	duration, err := time.ParseDuration(flagValues(command, "--duration")[0])
5516: +	if err != nil {
5517: +		f.t.Errorf("duration: %v", err)
5518: +	}
5519: +	if !slices.Equal(flagValues(command, "--format"), []string{"pcapng"}) {
5520: +		f.t.Errorf("capture without --format pcapng: %v", command)
5521: +	}
5522: +
5523: +	f.mu.Lock()
5524: +	index := f.processes[node]
5525: +	f.processes[node]++
5526: +	delay := f.startDelay[index]
5527: +	if index == 0 {
5528: +		delay += f.firstStartDelay[node]
5529: +	}
5530: +	failure := f.fail
5531: +	skew := f.stampSkew[node]
5532: +	f.mu.Unlock()
5533: +
5534: +	if failure != "" {
5535: +		f.audit(stderr, failure, node, interfaces, "interface \"eth9\" is not uniquely planned")
5536: +		return &clablabruntime.CommandExitError{Code: 1}
5537: +	}
5538: +
5539: +	select {
5540: +	case <-time.After(delay):
5541: +	case <-ctx.Done():
5542: +		return ctx.Err()
5543: +	case <-stdinClosed:
5544: +		f.audit(stderr, captureAuditStarted, node, interfaces, "")
5545: +		f.audit(stderr, captureAuditSucceeded, node, interfaces, "client closed: stdin reached EOF")
5546: +		return nil
5547: +	}
5548: +
5549: +	writer := clabcapture.NewWriter(stdout)
5550: +	f.audit(stderr, captureAuditStarted, node, interfaces, "")
5551: +	if err := writer.WriteHeader(interfaces, clabcapture.DefaultSnapLength); err != nil {
5552: +		return err
5553: +	}
5554: +
5555: +	// clabwire's own section header names it
5556: +	end := time.Now().Add(duration)
5557: +	jitter := time.Duration(index%3) * 7 * time.Microsecond
5558: +	next := time.Now().Sub(f.epoch)/f.tick + 1
5559: +	for {
5560: +		at := f.epoch.Add(next * f.tick)
5561: +		if at.After(end) {
5562: +			break
5563: +		}
5564: +		select {
5565: +		case <-ctx.Done():
5566: +			return ctx.Err()
5567: +		case <-stdinClosed:
5568: +			f.mu.Lock()
5569: +			f.stdinClosed[node]++
5570: +			f.mu.Unlock()
5571: +			f.audit(
5572: +				stderr,
5573: +				captureAuditSucceeded,
5574: +				node,
5575: +				interfaces,
5576: +				"client closed: stdin reached EOF",
5577: +			)
5578: +			return nil
5579: +		case <-time.After(time.Until(at)):
5580: +		}
5581: +		for id := range interfaces {
5582: +			data := make([]byte, 64)
5583: +			binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(data[0:], uint64(next))
5584: +			copy(data[8:], node+":"+interfaces[id])
5585: +			if err := writer.WritePacket(uint32(id), &clabcapture.Packet{ //nolint:gosec // small
5586: +				Timestamp: at.Add(jitter - skew).UnixNano(), OriginalLength: 64, Data: data,
5587: +			}); err != nil {
5588: +				return err
5589: +			}
5590: +			f.mu.Lock()
5591: +			f.written[node]++
5592: +			f.mu.Unlock()
5593: +		}
5594: +		next++
5595: +	}
5596: +	f.audit(stderr, captureAuditSucceeded, node, interfaces, "")
5597: +
5598: +	return nil
5599: +}
5600: +
5601: +func (f *fakeClabwire) captureCommands() [][]string {
5602: +	f.mu.Lock()
5603: +	defer f.mu.Unlock()
5604: +
5605: +	var result [][]string
5606: +	for _, command := range f.commands {
5607: +		if slices.Contains(command, "packet-capture") &&
5608: +			!slices.Contains(command, "--list-interfaces") {
5609: +			result = append(result, command)
5610: +		}
5611: +	}
5612: +
5613: +	return result
5614: +}
5615: +
5616: +// captureTestRuntime is lab1 in lab-ns with nodes r1 (topology name R1) and r2, each in its
5617: +// own pod, and a fake clabwire.
5618: +func captureTestRuntime(t *testing.T, tick time.Duration) (*Runtime, *fakeClabwire) {
5619: +	t.Helper()
5620: +
5621: +	r := newTestRuntimeWithKubeObjects(
5622: +		[]*unstructured.Unstructured{
5623: +			captureTestNode("r1", "R1", "node-r1-x"),
5624: +			captureTestNode("r2", "", "node-r2-x"),
5625: +		},
5626: +		[]k8sruntime.Object{
5627: +			captureTestPod("lab1-r1-abc", "r1"),
5628: +			captureTestPod("lab1-r2-def", "r2"),
5629: +		},
5630: +	)
5631: +	r.labNamespaceOverride = "lab-ns"
5632: +	clabwire := newFakeClabwire(t, tick)
5633: +	r.podExec = clabwire.exec
5634: +
5635: +	return r, clabwire
5636: +}
5637: +
5638: +// parsedCapture is a pcapng stream read back.
5639: +type parsedCapture struct {
5640: +	sections   int
5641: +	interfaces []string
5642: +	packets    []clabcapture.Packet
5643: +}
5644: +
5645: +func parseCapture(t *testing.T, data []byte) parsedCapture {
5646: +	t.Helper()
5647: +
5648: +	reader := clabcapture.NewReader(bytes.NewReader(data))
5649: +	var parsed parsedCapture
5650: +	for {
5651: +		event, err := reader.Next()
5652: +		if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
5653: +			break
5654: +		}
5655: +		if err != nil {
5656: +			t.Fatalf("invalid capture: %v", err)
5657: +		}
5658: +		if event.Interface != nil {
5659: +			if len(parsed.packets) != 0 {
5660: +				t.Fatal("interface description after the first packet")
5661: +			}
5662: +			if event.Interface.TSResol != 9 /* nanoseconds */ {
5663: +				t.Fatalf("interface %s tsresol = %d", event.Interface.Name, event.Interface.TSResol)
5664: +			}
5665: +			parsed.interfaces = append(parsed.interfaces, event.Interface.Name)
5666: +		}
5667: +		if event.Packet != nil {
5668: +			parsed.packets = append(parsed.packets, *event.Packet)
5669: +		}
5670: +	}
5671: +	parsed.sections = reader.Sections()
5672: +
5673: +	return parsed
5674: +}
5675: +
5676: +func packetSequence(packet clabcapture.Packet) uint64 {
5677: +	return binary.BigEndian.Uint64(packet.Data[0:8])
5678: +}
5679: +
5680: +func packetOrigin(packet clabcapture.Packet) string {
5681: +	return strings.TrimRight(string(packet.Data[8:]), "\x00")
5682: +}
5683: +
5684: +func TestCaptureInterfacesUsesTopologyNames(t *testing.T) {
5685: +	t.Parallel()
5686: +
5687: +	r, _ := captureTestRuntime(t, time.Millisecond)
5688: +	interfaces, err := r.CaptureInterfaces(
5689: +		context.Background(),
5690: +		clablabruntime.NodeRequest{Name: "lab1"},
5691: +	)
5692: +	if err != nil {
5693: +		t.Fatal(err)
5694: +	}
5695: +	want := []clablabruntime.CaptureInterface{
5696: +		{
5697: +			Node:          "R1",
5698: +			Interface:     "e1-1",
5699: +			Alias:         "ethernet-1/1",
5700: +			PeerNode:      "r2",
5701: +			PeerInterface: "ethernet-1/1",
5702: +		},
5703: +		{Node: "R1", Interface: "e1-2", PeerNode: "host", PeerInterface: "r1-e1-2"},
5704: +		{
5705: +			Node:          "r2",
5706: +			Interface:     "e1-1",
5707: +			Alias:         "ethernet-1/1",
5708: +			PeerNode:      "R1",
5709: +			PeerInterface: "ethernet-1/1",
5710: +		},
5711: +	}
5712: +	if !slices.Equal(interfaces, want) {
5713: +		t.Fatalf("interfaces = %+v\nwant %+v", interfaces, want)
5714: +	}
5715: +
5716: +	one, err := r.CaptureInterfaces(context.Background(), clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
5717: +		Name: "lab1", Nodes: []string{"r2"},
5718: +	})
5719: +	if err != nil || len(one) != 1 || one[0].Node != "r2" {
5720: +		t.Fatalf("r2 interfaces = %+v, %v", one, err)
5721: +	}
5722: +}
5723: +
5724: +func TestCaptureMergesNodesIntoOneSection(t *testing.T) {
5725: +	t.Parallel()
5726: +
5727: +	r, clabwire := captureTestRuntime(t, 10*time.Millisecond)
5728: +	var out bytes.Buffer
5729: +	err := r.Capture(context.Background(), clablabruntime.CaptureRequest{
5730: +		Name: "lab1",
5731: +		// the topology name of r1, an alias, and a second node between two r1 interfaces
5732: +		Targets: []clablabruntime.CaptureTarget{
5733: +			{Node: "R1", Interface: "ethernet-1/1"},
5734: +			{Node: "r2", Interface: "e1-1"},
5735: +			{Node: "r1", Interface: "e1-2"},
5736: +		},
5737: +		Duration: 300 * time.Millisecond,
5738: +	}, &out)
5739: +	if err != nil {
5740: +		t.Fatal(err)
5741: +	}
5742: +
5743: +	parsed := parseCapture(t, out.Bytes())
5744: +	if parsed.sections != 1 {
5745: +		t.Fatalf("sections = %d, want one merged section", parsed.sections)
5746: +	}
5747: +	wantNames := []string{"R1:e1-1", "r2:e1-1", "R1:e1-2"}
5748: +	if !slices.Equal(parsed.interfaces, wantNames) {
5749: +		t.Fatalf("interfaces = %v, want %v", parsed.interfaces, wantNames)
5750: +	}
5751: +
5752: +	// one clabwire process per node, with all of the node's interfaces in request order
5753: +	commands := clabwire.captureCommands()
5754: +	if len(commands) != 2 {
5755: +		t.Fatalf("capture processes = %d, want one per node: %v", len(commands), commands)
5756: +	}
5757: +	for _, command := range commands {
5758: +		node := flagValues(command, "--nodeName")[0]
5759: +		want := map[string][]string{"r1": {"e1-1", "e1-2"}, "r2": {"e1-1"}}[node]
5760: +		if got := flagValues(command, "--interface"); !slices.Equal(got, want) {
5761: +			t.Fatalf("%s interfaces = %v, want %v", node, got, want)
5762: +		}
5763: +		if !strings.HasSuffix(command[0], "/"+clabwireContainer) {
5764: +			t.Fatalf("capture ran in %s, want the clabwire container", command[0])
5765: +		}
5766: +	}
5767: +
5768: +	// every packet carries the merged ID of its interface
5769: +	wantOrigin := map[uint32]string{0: "r1:e1-1", 1: "r2:e1-1", 2: "r1:e1-2"}
5770: +	perInterface := map[uint32]int{}
5771: +	for _, packet := range parsed.packets {
5772: +		if packetOrigin(packet) != wantOrigin[packet.InterfaceID] {
5773: +			t.Fatalf("packet from %s has interface ID %d", packetOrigin(packet), packet.InterfaceID)
5774: +		}
5775: +		perInterface[packet.InterfaceID]++
5776: +	}
5777: +	for id := range uint32(3) {
5778: +		if perInterface[id] == 0 {
5779: +			t.Fatalf("no packets on %s: %v", wantNames[id], perInterface)
5780: +		}
5781: +	}
5782: +}
5783: +
5784: +// TestCaptureChainsSegmentsWithoutDuplicatesOrGaps runs captures longer than one segment: every
5785: +// tick must appear exactly once per interface, across every switch.
5786: +func TestCaptureChainsSegmentsWithoutDuplicatesOrGaps(t *testing.T) {
5787: +	t.Parallel()
5788: +
5789: +	r, clabwire := captureTestRuntime(t, 4*time.Millisecond)
5790: +	r.captureSegment = 300 * time.Millisecond
5791: +
5792: +	var gaps []clablabruntime.CaptureGap
5793: +	var out bytes.Buffer
5794: +	err := r.Capture(context.Background(), clablabruntime.CaptureRequest{
5795: +		Name: "lab1",
5796: +		Targets: []clablabruntime.CaptureTarget{
5797: +			{Node: "r1", Interface: "e1-1"},
5798: +			{Node: "r1", Interface: "e1-2"},
5799: +		},
5800: +		Duration: 1300 * time.Millisecond,
5801: +		OnGap:    func(gap clablabruntime.CaptureGap) { gaps = append(gaps, gap) },
5802: +	}, &out)
5803: +	if err != nil {
5804: +		t.Fatal(err)
5805: +	}
5806: +	if len(gaps) != 0 {
5807: +		t.Fatalf("gaps = %+v", gaps)
5808: +	}
5809: +	if processes := len(clabwire.captureCommands()); processes < 4 {
5810: +		t.Fatalf("capture processes = %d, want a chain of at least 4 segments", processes)
5811: +	}
5812: +
5813: +	parsed := parseCapture(t, out.Bytes())
5814: +	if parsed.sections != 1 || len(parsed.interfaces) != 2 {
5815: +		t.Fatalf("sections = %d, interfaces = %v; want the follow-up headers dropped",
5816: +			parsed.sections, parsed.interfaces)
5817: +	}
5818: +	for id := range uint32(2) {
5819: +		var sequence []uint64
5820: +		for _, packet := range parsed.packets {
5821: +			if packet.InterfaceID == id {
5822: +				sequence = append(sequence, packetSequence(packet))
5823: +			}
5824: +		}
5825: +		if len(sequence) < 200 {
5826: +			t.Fatalf("interface %d has %d packets", id, len(sequence))
5827: +		}
5828: +		slices.Sort(sequence)
5829: +		for idx := 1; idx < len(sequence); idx++ {
5830: +			switch {
5831: +			case sequence[idx] == sequence[idx-1]:
5832: +				t.Fatalf("interface %d: tick %d written twice", id, sequence[idx])
5833: +			case sequence[idx] != sequence[idx-1]+1:
5834: +				t.Fatalf(
5835: +					"interface %d: ticks %d to %d missing",
5836: +					id,
5837: +					sequence[idx-1]+1,
5838: +					sequence[idx]-1,
5839: +				)
5840: +			}
5841: +		}
5842: +	}
5843: +}

6053: +// TestCaptureClosesStdinWhenItEnds ends every clabwire process through its stdin, whether the
6054: +// caller cancels the capture or the output fails, so no capture is left running in the pod.
6055: +// TestCaptureWritesWhatItReadWhenTheContextEnds stops a capture while the output is slow and
6056: +// the chains have packets queued: every packet clabwire wrote before it ended is in the file.
6057: +func TestCaptureWritesWhatItReadWhenTheContextEnds(t *testing.T) {
6058: +	t.Parallel()
6059: +
6060: +	r, clabwire := captureTestRuntime(t, time.Millisecond)
6061: +	// without a reorder window, a blocked output blocks the chains
6062: +	r.captureReorderWindow = -1
6063: +	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
6064: +	defer cancel()
6065: +
6066: +	out := &gatedWriter{open: make(chan struct{})}
6067: +	go func() {
6068: +		time.Sleep(50 * time.Millisecond)
6069: +		out.block()
6070: +		// the segments keep reading while the chains wait for the output
6071: +		time.Sleep(400 * time.Millisecond)
6072: +		cancel()
6073: +		close(out.open)
6074: +	}()
6075: +
6076: +	if err := r.Capture(ctx, clablabruntime.CaptureRequest{
6077: +		Name: "lab1",
6078: +		Targets: []clablabruntime.CaptureTarget{
6079: +			{Node: "r1", Interface: "e1-1"},
6080: +			{Node: "r2", Interface: "e1-1"},
6081: +		},
6082: +	}, out); err != nil {
6083: +		t.Fatal(err)
6084: +	}
6085: +
6086: +	parsed := parseCapture(t, out.bytes())
6087: +	got := map[string]int{}
6088: +	for _, packet := range parsed.packets {
6089: +		node, _, _ := strings.Cut(packetOrigin(packet), ":")
6090: +		got[node]++
6091: +	}
6092: +	clabwire.mu.Lock()
6093: +	defer clabwire.mu.Unlock()
6094: +	for _, node := range []string{"r1", "r2"} {
6095: +		if clabwire.written[node] < 300 || got[node] != clabwire.written[node] {
6096: +			t.Fatalf("%s: clabwire wrote %d packets, the capture has %d", node,
6097: +				clabwire.written[node], got[node])
6098: +		}
6099: +	}
6100: +}
6101: +
6102: +// gatedWriter collects writes; once blocked, writes wait until open is closed.
6103: +type gatedWriter struct {
6104: +	open chan struct{}
6105: +
6106: +	mu      sync.Mutex
6107: +	blocked bool
6108: +	data    bytes.Buffer
6109: +}
6110: +
6111: +func (w *gatedWriter) block() {
6112: +	w.mu.Lock()
6113: +	w.blocked = true
6114: +	w.mu.Unlock()
6115: +}
6116: +
6117: +func (w *gatedWriter) Write(data []byte) (int, error) {
6118: +	w.mu.Lock()
6119: +	blocked := w.blocked
6120: +	w.mu.Unlock()
6121: +	if blocked {
6122: +		<-w.open
6123: +	}
6124: +	w.mu.Lock()
6125: +	defer w.mu.Unlock()
6126: +
6127: +	return w.data.Write(data)
6128: +}
6129: +
6130: +func (w *gatedWriter) bytes() []byte {
6131: +	w.mu.Lock()
6132: +	defer w.mu.Unlock()
6133: +
6134: +	return w.data.Bytes()
6135: +}
6136: +
6137: +func TestCaptureClosesStdinWhenItEnds(t *testing.T) {
6138: +	t.Parallel()
6139: +
6140: +	targets := []clablabruntime.CaptureTarget{
6141: +		{Node: "r1", Interface: "e1-1"},
6142: +		{Node: "r2", Interface: "e1-1"},
6143: +	}
6144: +
6145: +	t.Run("cancel", func(t *testing.T) {
6146: +		t.Parallel()
6147: +
6148: +		r, clabwire := captureTestRuntime(t, 2*time.Millisecond)
6149: +		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 200*time.Millisecond)
6150: +		defer cancel()
6151: +
6152: +		if err := r.Capture(ctx, clablabruntime.CaptureRequest{Name: "lab1", Targets: targets},
6153: +			io.Discard); err != nil {
6154: +			t.Fatal(err)
6155: +		}
6156: +		requireStdinClosedEverywhere(t, clabwire)
6157: +	})
6158: +
6159: +	t.Run("output fails", func(t *testing.T) {
6160: +		t.Parallel()
6161: +
6162: +		r, clabwire := captureTestRuntime(t, 2*time.Millisecond)
6163: +		output := &failingWriter{accept: 3}
6164: +		err := r.Capture(context.Background(), clablabruntime.CaptureRequest{
6165: +			Name: "lab1", Targets: targets, Duration: time.Hour,
6166: +		}, output)
6167: +		if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "broken pipe") {
6168: +			t.Fatalf("Capture() = %v, want the write error", err)
6169: +		}
6170: +		requireStdinClosedEverywhere(t, clabwire)
6171: +	})
6172: +}
6173: +
6174: +// failingWriter accepts some writes, then fails like a closed pipe.
6175: +type failingWriter struct {
6176: +	mu     sync.Mutex
6177: +	accept int
6178: +}
6179: +
6180: +func (w *failingWriter) Write(data []byte) (int, error) {
6181: +	w.mu.Lock()
6182: +	defer w.mu.Unlock()
6183: +	if w.accept == 0 {
6184: +		return 0, errors.New("write |1: broken pipe")
6185: +	}
6186: +	w.accept--
6187: +
6188: +	return len(data), nil
6189: +}
6190: +
6191: +func requireStdinClosedEverywhere(t *testing.T, clabwire *fakeClabwire) {
6192: +	t.Helper()
6193: +
6194: +	clabwire.mu.Lock()
6195: +	defer clabwire.mu.Unlock()
6196: +	for _, node := range []string{"r1", "r2"} {
6197: +		if clabwire.processes[node] == 0 || clabwire.stdinClosed[node] != clabwire.processes[node] {
6198: +			t.Fatalf("%s: %d processes, %d ended through stdin", node,
6199: +				clabwire.processes[node], clabwire.stdinClosed[node])
6200: +		}
6201: +	}
6202: +}
6203: +
6204: +// TestCaptureRejectsAClabwireWithoutStopOnStdinClose turns the usage error of an older clabwire
6205: +// into the release error.
6206: +func TestCaptureRejectsAClabwireWithoutStopOnStdinClose(t *testing.T) {
6207: +	t.Parallel()
6208: +
6209: +	r, clabwire := captureTestRuntime(t, time.Millisecond)
6210: +	clabwire.stderrOnly = "flag provided but not defined: -stop-on-stdin-close"
6211: +
6212: +	err := r.Capture(context.Background(), clablabruntime.CaptureRequest{
6213: +		Name: "lab1", Targets: []clablabruntime.CaptureTarget{{Node: "r2", Interface: "e1-1"}},
6214: +		Duration: time.Second,
6215: +	}, io.Discard)
6216: +	if !errors.Is(err, clablabruntime.ErrUnsupportedRuntimeVersion) ||
6217: +		!strings.Contains(err.Error(), "clabwire in pod lab-ns/lab1-r2-def does not accept "+
6218: +			"packet-capture --stop-on-stdin-close") ||
6219: +		!strings.Contains(err.Error(), "(0.11 or newer)") {
6220: +		t.Fatalf("Capture() = %v, want the release error", err)
6221: +	}
6222: +}
6223: +
6224: +// requireTimeOrdered checks that the merged stream's timestamps never decrease.
6225: +func requireTimeOrdered(t *testing.T, packets []clabcapture.Packet) {
6226: +	t.Helper()
6227: +
6228: +	for idx := 1; idx < len(packets); idx++ {
6229: +		if packets[idx].Timestamp < packets[idx-1].Timestamp {
6230: +			t.Fatalf("packet %d (%s) at %d precedes packet %d (%s) at %d", idx,
6231: +				packetOrigin(packets[idx]), packets[idx].Timestamp, idx-1,
6232: +				packetOrigin(packets[idx-1]), packets[idx-1].Timestamp)
6233: +		}
6234: +	}
6235: +}
6236: +
6237: +// TestCaptureMergesNodesInTimestampOrder merges two nodes whose streams arrive with different
6238: +// delays: r2's packets are stamped 60 ms before they reach containerlab. The reorder window puts
6239: +// them in order; without it they are not.
6240: +func TestCaptureMergesNodesInTimestampOrder(t *testing.T) {
6241: +	t.Parallel()
6242: +
6243: +	for _, reorder := range []bool{true, false} {
6244: +		t.Run(fmt.Sprintf("reorder=%v", reorder), func(t *testing.T) {
6245: +			t.Parallel()
6246: +
6247: +			r, clabwire := captureTestRuntime(t, 5*time.Millisecond)
6248: +			clabwire.stampSkew["r2"] = 60 * time.Millisecond
6249: +			if !reorder {
6250: +				r.captureReorderWindow = -1
6251: +			}
6252: +
6253: +			var out bytes.Buffer
6254: +			err := r.Capture(context.Background(), clablabruntime.CaptureRequest{
6255: +				Name: "lab1",
6256: +				Targets: []clablabruntime.CaptureTarget{
6257: +					{Node: "r1", Interface: "e1-1"},
6258: +					{Node: "r2", Interface: "e1-1"},
6259: +				},
6260: +				Duration: 500 * time.Millisecond,
6261: +			}, &out)
6262: +			if err != nil {
6263: +				t.Fatal(err)
6264: +			}
6265: +
6266: +			packets := parseCapture(t, out.Bytes()).packets
6267: +			ordered := slices.IsSortedFunc(packets, func(a, b clabcapture.Packet) int {
6268: +				return int(a.Timestamp - b.Timestamp)
6269: +			})
6270: +			if reorder {
6271: +				requireTimeOrdered(t, packets)
6272: +			} else if ordered {
6273: +				t.Fatal("the skewed streams came out ordered without the reorder window")
6274: +			}
6275: +		})
6276: +	}
6277: +}
6278: +
6279: +// TestCaptureChainsSeveralNodesInOrderWithoutDuplicates chains two nodes with skewed streams and a
6280: +// reorder window shorter than a segment switch:
6281: +// every tick appears exactly once per interface and the merged stream stays in timestamp order
6282: +// across every segment switch, while old segments are ended through stdin at the switch.
6283: +func TestCaptureChainsSeveralNodesInOrderWithoutDuplicates(t *testing.T) {
6284: +	t.Parallel()
6285: +
6286: +	r, clabwire := captureTestRuntime(t, 4*time.Millisecond)
6287: +	r.captureSegment = 300 * time.Millisecond
6288: +	// a window shorter than a switch: the chains' holds keep the order across the switches
6289: +	r.captureReorderWindow = 15 * time.Millisecond
6290: +	clabwire.stampSkew["r2"] = 5 * time.Millisecond
6291: +	// r2 switches segments 120 ms after r1, so one chain streams live while the other holds
6292: +	clabwire.firstStartDelay["r2"] = 120 * time.Millisecond
6293: +
6294: +	var gaps []clablabruntime.CaptureGap
6295: +	var out bytes.Buffer
6296: +	err := r.Capture(context.Background(), clablabruntime.CaptureRequest{
6297: +		Name: "lab1",
6298: +		Targets: []clablabruntime.CaptureTarget{
6299: +			{Node: "r1", Interface: "e1-1"},
6300: +			{Node: "r2", Interface: "e1-1"},
6301: +		},
6302: +		Duration: 1300 * time.Millisecond,
6303: +		OnGap:    func(gap clablabruntime.CaptureGap) { gaps = append(gaps, gap) },
6304: +	}, &out)
6305: +	if err != nil {
6306: +		t.Fatal(err)
6307: +	}
6308: +	if len(gaps) != 0 {
6309: +		t.Fatalf("gaps = %+v", gaps)
6310: +	}
6311: +
6312: +	parsed := parseCapture(t, out.Bytes())
6313: +	requireTimeOrdered(t, parsed.packets)
6314: +	for id := range uint32(2) {
6315: +		var sequence []uint64

6496: @@ -0,0 +1,69 @@
6497: +#!/usr/bin/env python3
6498: +# Copyright 2020 Nokia
6499: +# Licensed under the BSD 3-Clause License.
6500: +# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
6501: +"""Summarize a little-endian pcapng file as containerlab capture writes it, as JSON.
6502: +
6503: +Prints the number of sections, the interface names in order, the packet count per interface,
6504: +whether packets are in timestamp order, the number of 802.1Q tagged frames and the number of
6505: +ICMP echo requests and replies (untagged or tagged).
6506: +"""
6507: +
6508: +import json
6509: +import struct
6510: +import sys
6511: +
6512: +SHB, IDB, EPB = 0x0A0D0D0A, 0x00000001, 0x00000006
6513: +
6514: +
6515: +def main(path):
6516: +    with open(path, "rb") as f:
6517: +        data = f.read()
6518: +
6519: +    sections, names, counts, stamps = 0, [], {}, []
6520: +    vlan, echo = 0, 0
6521: +    offset = 0
6522: +    while offset < len(data):
6523: +        block_type, length = struct.unpack_from("<II", data, offset)
6524: +        body = data[offset + 8 : offset + length - 4]
6525: +        if block_type == SHB:
6526: +            sections += 1
6527: +        elif block_type == IDB:
6528: +            options, name = body[8:], ""
6529: +            while len(options) >= 4:
6530: +                code, size = struct.unpack_from("<HH", options)
6531: +                if code == 0:
6532: +                    break
6533: +                if code == 2:
6534: +                    name = options[4 : 4 + size].decode()
6535: +                options = options[4 + size + (4 - size % 4) % 4 :]
6536: +            names.append(name)
6537: +        elif block_type == EPB:
6538: +            iface, high, low, captured = struct.unpack_from("<IIII", body)
6539: +            frame = body[20 : 20 + captured]
6540: +            counts[names[iface]] = counts.get(names[iface], 0) + 1
6541: +            stamps.append(high << 32 | low)
6542: +            ethertype, l3 = struct.unpack_from(">H", frame, 12)[0], 14
6543: +            if ethertype == 0x8100:
6544: +                vlan += 1
6545: +                ethertype, l3 = struct.unpack_from(">H", frame, 16)[0], 18
6546: +            if ethertype == 0x0800 and frame[l3 + 9] == 1 and frame[l3 + 20] in (0, 8):
6547: +                echo += 1
6548: +        offset += length
6549: +
6550: +    print(
6551: +        json.dumps(
6552: +            {
6553: +                "sections": sections,
6554: +                "interfaces": names,
6555: +                "packets": counts,
6556: +                "ordered": stamps == sorted(stamps),
6557: +                "vlan_frames": vlan,
6558: +                "icmp_echo": echo,
6559: +            }
6560: +        )
6561: +    )
6562: +
6563: +
6564: +if __name__ == "__main__":
6565: +    main(sys.argv[1])

6983: @@ -0,0 +1,35 @@
6984: +#!/bin/sh
6985: +# Prints the packet-capture processes running in the clabwire container of a c9s node's pod.
6986: +# usage: clabwire-captures.sh <namespace> <node>
6987: +#
6988: +# A process of a Kubernetes exec is not visible through the API, so this looks at the worker
6989: +# that runs the pod: a KinD node, which is a Docker container. It lists the processes whose
6990: +# cgroup belongs to the clabwire container. Exits 2 when the worker is not a Docker container.
6991: +set -eu
6992: +
6993: +namespace=$1
6994: +node=$2
6995: +
6996: +pod=$(kubectl -n "$namespace" get pod -l "c9s.run/topologyNode=$node" \
6997: +  -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')
6998: +worker=$(kubectl -n "$namespace" get pod "$pod" -o jsonpath='{.spec.nodeName}')
6999: +# clabwire is a sidecar (an init container that keeps running)
7000: +container=$(kubectl -n "$namespace" get pod "$pod" -o jsonpath=\
7001: +'{.status.initContainerStatuses[?(@.name=="clabwire")].containerID}{.status.containerStatuses[?(@.name=="clabwire")].containerID}')
7002: +container=${container#*://}
7003: +
7004: +if ! docker inspect --type container "$worker" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
7005: +  echo "worker $worker of pod $namespace/$pod is not a Docker container (KinD)" >&2
7006: +  exit 2
7007: +fi
7008: +if [ -z "$container" ]; then
7009: +  echo "pod $namespace/$pod has no running clabwire container" >&2
7010: +  exit 1
7011: +fi
7012: +
7013: +docker exec "$worker" sh -c "
7014: +  for proc in /proc/[0-9]*; do
7015: +    if grep -qs '$container' \"\$proc/cgroup\"; then
7016: +      tr '\\0' ' ' < \"\$proc/cmdline\" 2>/dev/null && echo
7017: +    fi
7018: +  done" | grep 'packet-capture' || true

API, so this looks at the worker\n6989: +# that runs the pod: a KinD node, which is a Docker container. packet-capture processes running in the clabwire container of a c9s node's pod.\n+# usage: clabwire-captures.sh <namespace> <node>\n+#\n+# A process of a Kubernetes exec is not visible through the API, so this looks at the worker\n+# that runs the pod: a KinD node, which is a Docker container. It lists the processes whose\n+# cgroup belongs to the clabwire container. Exits 2 when the worker is not a Docker container.\n+set -eu\n+\n+namespace=$1\n+node=$2\n+\n+pod=$(kubectl -n \"$namespace\" get pod -l \"c9s.run/topologyNode=$node\" \\\n+  -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')\n+worker=$(kubectl -n \"$namespace\" get pod \"$pod\" -o jsonpath='{.spec.nodeName}')\n+# clabwire is a sidecar (an init container that keeps running)\n+container=$(kubectl -n \"$namespace\" get pod \"$pod\" -o jsonpath=\\\n+'{.status.initContainerStatuses[?(@.name==\"clabwire\")].containerID}{.status.containerStatuses[?(@.name==\"clabwire\")].containerID}')\n+container=${container#*://}\n+\n+if ! docker inspect --type container \"$worker\" >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n+  echo \"worker $worker of pod $namespace/$pod is not a Docker container (KinD)\" >&2\n+  exit 2\n+fi\n+if [ -z \"$container\" ]; then\n+  echo \"pod $namespace/$pod has no running clabwire container\" >&2\n+  exit 1\n+fi\n+\n+docker exec \"$worker\" sh -c \"\n+  for proc in /proc/[0-9]*; do\n+    if grep -qs '$container' \\\"\\$proc/cgroup\\\"; then\n+      tr '\\\\0' ' ' < \\\"\\$proc/cmdline\\\" 2>/dev/null && echo\n+    fi\n+  done\" | grep 'packet-capture' || true",

19: const (
20: 	// localReorderWindow is how long the merged stream holds packets of local sockets back to
21: 	// write them in timestamp order. Each socket hands over its packets within
22: 	// localBlockTimeout, so a few times that covers the delivery skew between sockets.
23: 	localReorderWindow = 100 * time.Millisecond
24: 	// localBlockTimeout is how long the kernel fills a ring block before it hands it over.
25: 	localBlockTimeout = 10 * time.Millisecond
26: 	// localPollTimeout is how often a socket reader checks whether the capture ended.
27: 	localPollTimeout = 100 * time.Millisecond
28: 	// localReopenInterval is how often a reader tries to reopen the socket of an interface
29: 	// that went down or disappeared.
30: 	localReopenInterval = 200 * time.Millisecond
31: 	// localDrainQuiet is how long after the end of a capture a reader keeps waiting for packets
32: 	// still in the socket's ring: the kernel hands over a block within two block timeouts.
33: 	localDrainQuiet = 5 * localBlockTimeout
34: 	// localDrainTimeout bounds the drain while packets keep arriving.
35: 	localDrainTimeout = 250 * time.Millisecond
36: 	// localRingBlocks and localMinBlockSize size the receive ring of each socket: eight blocks
37: 	// of at least 1 MiB, each larger than the snap length.
38: 	localRingBlocks   = 8
39: 	localMinBlockSize = 1 << 20

48: // ExecFunc runs f in the network namespace of a node.
49: type ExecFunc func(ctx context.Context, f func(ns.NetNS) error) error

51: // LocalTarget is one interface of a node on this machine (Docker or Podman) to capture.
52: type LocalTarget struct {
53: 	// Node is the node name as the topology spells it.
54: 	Node string
55: 	// Interface is the interface name inside the node.
56: 	Interface string
57: 	// Exec runs a function in the node's network namespace.

61: // packetSource reads the packets of one interface.
62: type packetSource interface {
63: 	// ReadPacket returns the next packet; the data is only valid until the next call. It
64: 	// returns errReadTimeout when no packet arrived within the poll timeout.
65: 	ReadPacket() ([]byte, gopacket.CaptureInfo, error)
66: 	Close()
67: }

69: // openSourcesFunc opens one packet source per interface in the network namespace exec enters.
70: type openSourcesFunc func(

77: // CaptureLocal streams pcapng from interfaces of nodes on this machine to w, with the same
78: // output and end conditions as labruntime.PacketCapturer.Capture: one section, one Interface
79: // Description Block per target named <node>:<interface>, then the packets of every target in
80: // timestamp order. targets lists the interfaces of req.Targets, resolved, in the same order.
81: //
82: // Each interface is read through a packet socket opened in the node's network namespace, so
83: // nothing runs in the node and the node image needs no capture tools; it needs CAP_NET_RAW and
84: // the right to enter the namespace, so root. An interface that goes down is reopened once it is
85: // up again; one that disappears (its node stopped or was recreated) is reattached when it is
86: // back, and the time it was gone is reported as a gap through req.OnGap (or logged).
87: func CaptureLocal(
88: 	ctx context.Context,
89: 	req clablabruntime.CaptureRequest,
90: 	targets []LocalTarget,
91: 	w io.Writer,
92: ) error {
93: 	return localCapture{
94: 		open:           openPacketSockets,
95: 		window:         localReorderWindow,
96: 		reopenInterval: localReopenInterval,
97: 	}.run(ctx, req, targets, w)
98: }
99: 
100: // localCapture is a local capture with its socket opener and timings, which tests replace.
101: type localCapture struct {
102: 	open           openSourcesFunc
103: 	window         time.Duration
104: 	reopenInterval time.Duration
105: }
106: 
107: func (l localCapture) run(
108: 	ctx context.Context,
109: 	req clablabruntime.CaptureRequest,
110: 	targets []LocalTarget,
111: 	w io.Writer,
112: ) error {
113: 	if err := ValidateRequest(&req); err != nil {
114: 		return err
115: 	}
116: 	if len(targets) != len(req.Targets) {
117: 		return fmt.Errorf("capture has %d resolved targets for %d requested ones",
118: 			len(targets), len(req.Targets))
119: 	}
120: 
121: 	sources, err := l.openAll(ctx, targets, req.SnapLength)
122: 	if err != nil {
123: 		return err
124: 	}
125: 
126: 	names := make([]string, len(targets))
127: 	for idx, target := range targets {
128: 		names[idx] = target.Node + ":" + target.Interface
129: 	}
130: 
131: 	captureCtx, stop := context.WithCancel(ctx)
132: 	defer stop()
133: 	if req.Duration > 0 {
134: 		var cancelTimeout context.CancelFunc
135: 		captureCtx, cancelTimeout = context.WithTimeout(captureCtx, req.Duration)
136: 		defer cancelTimeout()
137: 	}
138: 
139: 	out, err := NewOutput(w, names, req.SnapLength, req.PacketLimit, l.window, stop)
140: 	if err != nil {
141: 		for _, source := range sources {
142: 			source.Close()
143: 		}
144: 
145: 		return err
146: 	}
147: 
148: 	var wg sync.WaitGroup
149: 	for idx, source := range sources {
150: 		reader := &localReader{
151: 			capture: l,
152: 			out:     out,
153: 			id:      uint32(idx), //nolint:gosec // bounded by the targets
154: 			target:  targets[idx],
155: 			snap:    req.SnapLength,
156: 			onGap:   req.OnGap,
157: 		}
158: 		wg.Go(func() {
159: 			reader.run(captureCtx, source)
160: 		})
161: 	}
162: 	wg.Wait()
163: 
164: 	return out.Close()
165: }
166: 
167: // openAll opens the sockets of every target before anything is written, one namespace entry
168: // per node, so a capture that cannot start fails without output.
169: func (l localCapture) openAll(
170: 	ctx context.Context,
171: 	targets []LocalTarget,
172: 	snapLength int,
173: ) ([]packetSource, error) {
174: 	type nodeTargets struct {
175: 		exec    ExecFunc
176: 		indexes []int
177: 		names   []string
178: 	}
179: 	var order []string
180: 	byNode := map[string]*nodeTargets{}
181: 	for idx, target := range targets {
182: 		group := byNode[target.Node]
183: 		if group == nil {
184: 			group = &nodeTargets{exec: target.Exec}
185: 			byNode[target.Node] = group
186: 			order = append(order, target.Node)
187: 		}
188: 		group.indexes = append(group.indexes, idx)
189: 		group.names = append(group.names, target.Interface)
190: 	}
191: 
192: 	sources := make([]packetSource, len(targets))
193: 	closeAll := func() {
194: 		for _, source := range sources {
195: 			if source != nil {
196: 				source.Close()
197: 			}
198: 		}
199: 	}
200: 	for _, node := range order {
201: 		group := byNode[node]
202: 		opened, err := l.open(ctx, group.exec, group.names, snapLength)
203: 		if err != nil {
204: 			closeAll()
205: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to start the capture on node %q: %w", node, err)
206: 		}
207: 		for idx, source := range opened {
208: 			sources[group.indexes[idx]] = source
209: 		}
210: 	}
211: 
212: 	return sources, nil
213: }

215: // localReader reads one interface into the merged stream.
216: type localReader struct {
217: 	capture localCapture
218: 	out     *Output
219: 	id      uint32
220: 	target  LocalTarget
221: 	snap    int
222: 	onGap   func(clablabruntime.CaptureGap)
223: }
224: 
225: func (r *localReader) run(ctx context.Context, source packetSource) {
226: 	defer func() {
227: 		if source != nil {
228: 			source.Close()
229: 		}
230: 	}()
231: 
232: 	for {
233: 		if ctx.Err() != nil {
234: 			r.drain(source, time.Now())
235: 			return
236: 		}
237: 
238: 		data, info, err := source.ReadPacket()
239: 		if errors.Is(err, errReadTimeout) {
240: 			continue
241: 		}
242: 		if err != nil {
243: 			// The socket reports an error once its interface went down or was removed, and
244: 			// keeps reporting it: it is reopened.
245: 			log.Debug("Capture socket failed, reopening it", "node", r.target.Node,
246: 				"interface", r.target.Interface, "error", err)
247: 			source.Close()
248: 			source = r.reopen(ctx)
249: 			if source == nil {
250: 				return
251: 			}
252: 
253: 			continue
254: 		}
255: 
256: 		if more, err := r.out.Emit(r.id, r.packet(data, info)); !more || err != nil {
257: 			return
258: 		}
259: 	}
260: }
261: 
262: // drain writes the packets that arrived before end but were still in the socket's ring: the
263: // kernel hands over a ring block once it is full or its block timeout passed, so the last
264: // packets before a capture ended may not have been read yet.
265: func (r *localReader) drain(source packetSource, end time.Time) {
266: 	deadline := end.Add(localDrainTimeout)
267: 	for time.Now().Before(deadline) {
268: 		data, info, err := source.ReadPacket()
269: 		if errors.Is(err, errReadTimeout) && time.Since(end) < localDrainQuiet {
270: 			continue
271: 		}
272: 		if err != nil || info.Timestamp.After(end) {
273: 			return
274: 		}
275: 		if more, err := r.out.Emit(r.id, r.packet(data, info)); !more || err != nil {
276: 			return
277: 		}
278: 	}
279: }
280: 
281: // packet copies a packet out of the socket's ring, cut to the snap length.
282: func (r *localReader) packet(data []byte, info gopacket.CaptureInfo) *Packet {
283: 	length := info.Length
284: 	for _, ancillary := range info.AncillaryData {
285: 		if _, ok := ancillary.(afpacket.AncillaryVLAN); ok {
286: 			// the tag was put back into the data and counts toward the frame length
287: 			length += vlanHeaderLength
288: 			break
289: 		}
290: 	}
291: 	length = max(length, len(data))
292: 
293: 	captured := make([]byte, min(len(data), r.snap))
294: 	copy(captured, data)
295: 
296: 	return &Packet{
297: 		Timestamp:      info.Timestamp.UnixNano(),
298: 		OriginalLength: uint32(length), //nolint:gosec // bounded by the interface MTU
299: 		Data:           captured,
300: 	}
301: }
302: 
303: // reopen opens the interface's socket again once its node and interface are back. It returns
304: // nil when the capture ended first. Time the interface could not be opened is reported as a gap;
305: // an interface that only went down is not, as it has no traffic while down.
306: func (r *localReader) reopen(ctx context.Context) packetSource {
307: 	from := time.Now()
308: 	var unavailable error
309: 
310: 	timer := time.NewTimer(r.capture.reopenInterval)
311: 	defer timer.Stop()
312: 
313: 	for {
314: 		select {
315: 		case <-ctx.Done():
316: 			if unavailable != nil {
317: 				r.reportGap(from, time.Time{}, unavailable)
318: 			}
319: 
320: 			return nil
321: 		case <-timer.C:
322: 		}
323: 
324: 		opened, err := r.capture.open(ctx, r.target.Exec, []string{r.target.Interface}, r.snap)
325: 		if err != nil {
326: 			if unavailable == nil {
327: 				log.Debug("Capture interface is not available, waiting for it",
328: 					"node", r.target.Node, "interface", r.target.Interface, "error", err)
329: 			}
330: 			unavailable = err
331: 			resetTimer(timer, r.capture.reopenInterval)
332: 
333: 			continue
334: 		}
335: 		if unavailable != nil {
336: 			r.reportGap(from, time.Now(), unavailable)
337: 		}
338: 
339: 		return opened[0]
340: 	}
341: }
342: 
343: func (r *localReader) reportGap(from, to time.Time, cause error) {
344: 	ReportGap(r.onGap, clablabruntime.CaptureGap{
345: 		Node:       r.target.Node,
346: 		Interfaces: []string{r.target.Interface},
347: 		From:       from,
348: 		To:         to,
349: 		Reason:     fmt.Sprintf("the interface was not available: %v", cause),
350: 	})
351: }
352: 
353: // openPacketSockets opens one packet socket per interface in the namespace exec enters. A socket
354: // stays bound to its interface after the thread left the namespace.
355: func openPacketSockets(
356: 	ctx context.Context,
357: 	exec ExecFunc,
358: 	interfaces []string,
359: 	snapLength int,
360: ) ([]packetSource, error) {
361: 	sources := make([]packetSource, 0, len(interfaces))
362: 	err := exec(ctx, func(ns.NetNS) error {
363: 		for _, name := range interfaces {
364: 			source, err := openPacketSocket(name, snapLength)
365: 			if err != nil {
366: 				return fmt.Errorf("interface %q: %w", name, err)
367: 			}
368: 			sources = append(sources, source)
369: 		}
370: 
371: 		return nil
372: 	})
373: 	if err != nil {
374: 		for _, source := range sources {
375: 			source.Close()
376: 		}
377: 
378: 		return nil, err
379: 	}
380: 
381: 	return sources, nil
382: }
383: 
384: // afpacketSource is a TPACKET_V3 receive ring on one interface.
385: type afpacketSource struct {
386: 	handle *afpacket.TPacket
387: }
388: 
389: func openPacketSocket(name string, snapLength int) (*afpacketSource, error) {
390: 	// A TPACKET_V3 block holds whole frames: it must be larger than the snap length, plus the
391: 	// block and frame headers, and a multiple of the page size.
392: 	pageSize := os.Getpagesize()
393: 	blockSize := max(localMinBlockSize, snapLength+pageSize)
394: 	blockSize = (blockSize + pageSize - 1) / pageSize * pageSize
395: 
396: 	handle, err := afpacket.NewTPacket(
397: 		afpacket.OptInterface(name),
398: 		afpacket.OptTPacketVersion(afpacket.TPacketVersion3),
399: 		afpacket.OptFrameSize(blockSize),
400: 		afpacket.OptBlockSize(blockSize),
401: 		afpacket.OptNumBlocks(localRingBlocks),
402: 		afpacket.OptBlockTimeout(localBlockTimeout),
403: 		afpacket.OptPollTimeout(localPollTimeout),
404: 		// the kernel moves 802.1Q tags out of the frame; captures show them in place
405: 		afpacket.OptAddVLANHeader(true),
406: 	)
407: 	if err != nil {
408: 		return nil, err
409: 	}
410: 	// promiscuous mode is a membership of this socket and ends with it
411: 	if err := handle.SetPromiscuous(true); err != nil {
412: 		handle.Close()
413: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to enable promiscuous mode: %w", err)
414: 	}
415: 
416: 	return &afpacketSource{handle: handle}, nil
417: }
418: 
419: func (s *afpacketSource) ReadPacket() ([]byte, gopacket.CaptureInfo, error) {
420: 	data, info, err := s.handle.ZeroCopyReadPacketData()
421: 	if errors.Is(err, afpacket.ErrTimeout) {
422: 		return nil, info, errReadTimeout
423: 	}
424: 
425: 	return data, info, err
426: }
427: 
428: func (s *afpacketSource) Close() {
429: 	s.handle.Close()
430: }

12: // maxReorderBytes bounds the packet data the reorder buffer holds. Past it, the oldest packets
13: // are written early, which can put them out of order.
14: const maxReorderBytes = 64 << 20
15: 
16: // Reorder writes the packets of several capture sources in timestamp order.
17: //
18: // Each source (a node's capture stream, or a local interface socket) delivers its packets with
19: // its own delay. The buffer holds every packet for `window` after it arrived and writes the held
20: // packets in timestamp order, so a packet that was stamped earlier but delivered up to `window`
21: // later still goes out first. A packet stamped before the last packet written arrived too late
22: // to be ordered: it is written as it comes and counted, and the count goes to the debug log when
23: // the capture ends.
24: //
25: // A source can place a hold at the earliest timestamp it may still write (Hold); packets stamped
26: // after a hold wait for it to be released (Release). The c9s runtime holds while it switches
27: // between chained capture segments.
28: type Reorder struct {
29: 	write  func(id uint32, packet *Packet) error
30: 	onFail func()
31: 	window time.Duration
32: 	now    func() time.Time
33: 
34: 	mu     sync.Mutex
35: 	queue  reorderQueue
36: 	bytes  int
37: 	seq    uint64
38: 	holds  map[any]int64
39: 	err    error
40: 	wake   chan struct{}
41: 	stats  reorderStats
42: 	cursor int64 // timestamp of the latest packet written in order
43: }
44: 
45: type reorderStats struct {
46: 	late    int
47: 	maxLate time.Duration
48: 	forced  int
49: }

51: // reorderedPacket is a packet waiting in the buffer.
52: type reorderedPacket struct {
53: 	id      uint32
54: 	packet  *Packet
55: 	arrived time.Time
56: 	seq     uint64
57: }

59: // reorderQueue is a min-heap by timestamp, then arrival.
60: type reorderQueue []reorderedPacket
61: 
62: func (q reorderQueue) Len() int { return len(q) }
63: 
64: func (q reorderQueue) Less(i, j int) bool {
65: 	if q[i].packet.Timestamp != q[j].packet.Timestamp {
66: 		return q[i].packet.Timestamp < q[j].packet.Timestamp
67: 	}
68: 
69: 	return q[i].seq < q[j].seq
70: }

72: func (q reorderQueue) Swap(i, j int) { q[i], q[j] = q[j], q[i] }

74: func (q *reorderQueue) Push(
75: 	x any,
76: ) {
77: 	*q = append(*q, x.(reorderedPacket))
78: } //nolint:forcetypeassert // heap contract

80: func (q *reorderQueue) Pop() any {
81: 	old := *q
82: 	item := old[len(old)-1]
83: 	*q = old[:len(old)-1]
84: 
85: 	return item
86: }

88: // NewReorder returns a buffer that writes through write; onFail is called once a write
89: // failed. A window of zero or less writes every packet as it arrives.
90: func NewReorder(
91: 	window time.Duration,
92: 	write func(id uint32, packet *Packet) error,
93: 	onFail func(),
94: ) *Reorder {
95: 	return &Reorder{

98: 	}

101: // push hands a packet to the buffer. It returns the error of a failed write.
102: func (q *Reorder) Push(id uint32, packet *Packet) error {
103: 	q.mu.Lock()
104: 	defer q.mu.Unlock()
105: 
106: 	if q.err != nil {
107: 		return q.err
108: 	}
109: 	if q.window <= 0 {
110: 		return q.writeLocked(id, packet)
111: 	}

119:

121: 	}
122:

125: 	q.bytes += len(packet.Data)
126: 	for q.bytes > maxReorderBytes && q.queue.Len() > 0 {
127: 		q.stats.forced++

130: 		}
131: 	}

133: 	select {

139: }

143: 	q.mu.Lock()
144: 	defer q.mu.Unlock()

155:

160: 		}
161: 	}
162: }

164: // run writes due packets until ctx ends.
165: func (q *Reorder) Run(ctx context.Context) {
166: 	if q.window <= 0 {
167: 		return
168: 	}
169: 
170: 	timer := time.NewTimer(time.Hour)
171: 	defer timer.Stop()
172: 
173: 	for {
174: 		next := q.writeDue()
175: 		wait := time.Hour
176: 		if !next.IsZero() {
177: 			wait = max(next.Sub(q.now()), time.Millisecond)
178: 		}
179: 		resetTimer(timer, wait)
180: 
181: 		select {
182: 		case <-ctx.Done():
183: 			return
184: 		case <-q.wake:
185: 		case <-timer.C:
186: 		}
187: 	}
188: }

190: // writeDue writes the packets that waited for the window and are not behind a hold, in
191: // timestamp order. It returns when the next packet is due, or zero when that depends on a new
192: // packet or a released hold.
193: func (q *Reorder) writeDue() time.Time {
194: 	q.mu.Lock()
195: 	defer q.mu.Unlock()
196: 
197: 	held, limit := false, int64(0)
198: 	for _, timestamp := range q.holds {
199: 		if !held || timestamp < limit {
200: 			held, limit = true, timestamp
201: 		}
202: 	}
203: 
204: 	now := q.now()
205: 	for q.queue.Len() > 0 && q.err == nil {

207: 		if held && head.packet.Timestamp > limit {
208: 			return time.Time{}
209: 		}
210: 		if due := head.arrived.Add(q.window); due.After(now) {
211: 			return due
212: 		}
213: 		if q.popLocked() != nil {
214: 			return time.Time{}
215: 		}
216: 	}
217: 
218: 	return time.Time{}
219: }

222: func (q *Reorder) Flush() {
223: 	q.mu.Lock()
224: 	defer q.mu.Unlock()
225: 
226: 	for q.queue.Len() > 0 && q.err == nil {
227: 		if q.popLocked() != nil {

229: 		}
230: 	}

249: 	if err := q.write(id, packet); err != nil {
250: 		if q.err == nil {
251: 			q.err = err
252: 			if q.onFail != nil {
253: 				q.onFail()
254: 			}
255: 		}
256: 
257: 		return err
258: 	}
259: 
260: 	return nil
261: }

1: // Package capture writes the pcapng streams of `containerlab capture`: one section with one
2: // interface per capture target, packets merged across targets in timestamp order. The local
3: // capturer reads lab link interfaces of Docker and Podman nodes through packet sockets; the c9s
4: // lab runtime feeds the same writer from clabwire streams.
5: package capture
6: 
7: import (
8: 	"bufio"
9: 	"encoding/binary"
10: 	"errors"
11: 	"fmt"
12: 	"io"
13: 	"math"
14: 	"sync"
15: )
16: 
17: // pcapng block layout (https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-opsawg-pcapng-03.html). clabwire
18: // writes little-endian sections, and so does the merged stream containerlab writes.
19: const (
20: 	pcapngSectionHeaderType  = 0x0a0d0d0a
21: 	pcapngInterfaceType      = 0x00000001
22: 	pcapngEnhancedPacketType = 0x00000006
23: 	pcapngByteOrderMagic     = 0x1a2b3c4d
24: 	pcapngOptionEnd          = 0
25: 	pcapngOptionUserAppl     = 4
26: 	pcapngOptionIfName       = 2
27: 	pcapngOptionIfTSResol    = 9
28: 	pcapngLinkTypeEthernet   = 1
29: 	// pcapngNanoseconds is the if_tsresol value for 10^-9 s resolution.
30: 	pcapngNanoseconds = 9
31: 	// pcapngMaxBlockLength bounds a block read from a capture stream: a packet of the largest
32: 	// clabwire snap length (1 MiB) plus framing.
33: 	pcapngMaxBlockLength = 1<<20 + 1024
34: 	// captureUserApplication names the writer in the merged section header.
35: 	captureUserApplication = "containerlab"
36: )
37: 
38: var errPCAPNGByteOrder = errors.New("pcapng section is not little-endian")
39: 
40: // InterfaceDescription is an Interface Description Block.
41: type InterfaceDescription struct {
42: 	LinkType   uint16
43: 	SnapLength uint32
44: 	Name       string
45: 	// TSResol is the raw if_tsresol value; 6 (microseconds) when the block has none.
46: 	TSResol byte
47: }
48: 
49: // Packet is an Enhanced Packet Block with its timestamp in nanoseconds.
50: type Packet struct {
51: 	InterfaceID    uint32
52: 	Timestamp      int64
53: 	OriginalLength uint32
54: 	Data           []byte
55: }
56: 
57: // Reader reads the blocks of a pcapng stream as clabwire writes it: one or more
58: // little-endian sections, each with its Interface Description Blocks before its packets.
59: type Reader struct {
60: 	r          *bufio.Reader
61: 	interfaces []InterfaceDescription
62: 	// sections counts the Section Header Blocks read so far.
63: 	sections int
64: }
65: 
66: // NewReader returns a reader of the pcapng stream r.
67: func NewReader(r io.Reader) *Reader {
68: 	return &Reader{r: bufio.NewReaderSize(r, 64<<10)}
69: }
70: 
71: // Sections returns the number of Section Header Blocks read so far.
72: func (p *Reader) Sections() int {
73: 	return p.sections
74: }
75: 
76: // Event is one block of interest: a new interface or a packet.
77: type Event struct {
78: 	Interface *InterfaceDescription
79: 	Packet    *Packet
80: }
81: 
82: // Next returns the next interface or packet, skipping other block types. It returns io.EOF at
83: // the clean end of the stream, and io.ErrUnexpectedEOF for a stream cut inside a block.
84: func (p *Reader) Next() (Event, error) {
85: 	for {
86: 		var header [8]byte
87: 		if _, err := io.ReadFull(p.r, header[:]); err != nil {
88: 			if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
89: 				return Event{}, io.EOF
90: 			}
91: 
92: 			return Event{}, io.ErrUnexpectedEOF
93: 		}
94: 
95: 		blockType := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(header[0:4])
96: 		length := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(header[4:8])
97: 		if blockType == pcapngSectionHeaderType {
98: 			// the byte-order magic tells a big-endian section apart before its length is
99: 			// trusted: that length reads byte swapped
100: 			magic, err := p.r.Peek(4)
101: 			if err != nil {
102: 				return Event{}, io.ErrUnexpectedEOF
103: 			}
104: 			if binary.BigEndian.Uint32(magic) == pcapngByteOrderMagic {
105: 				return Event{}, errPCAPNGByteOrder
106: 			}
107: 		}
108: 		if length < 12 || length%4 != 0 || length > pcapngMaxBlockLength {

154: func parsePCAPNGInterface(body []byte) (InterfaceDescription, error) {
155: 	if len(body) < 8 {
156: 		return InterfaceDescription{}, fmt.Errorf("short pcapng interface description")
157: 	}
158: 	intf := InterfaceDescription{
159: 		LinkType:   binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(body[0:2]),
160: 		SnapLength: binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[4:8]),
161: 		TSResol:    6,
162: 	}
163: 
164: 	options := body[8:]
165: 	for len(options) >= 4 {
166: 		code := binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(options[0:2])
167: 		size := int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(options[2:4]))
168: 		if code == pcapngOptionEnd {
169: 			break
170: 		}
171: 		padded := size + pcapngPadding(size)
172: 		if 4+padded > len(options) {
173: 			return InterfaceDescription{}, fmt.Errorf("truncated pcapng interface option")
174: 		}
175: 		value := options[4 : 4+size]
176: 		switch code {
177: 		case pcapngOptionIfName:
178: 			intf.Name = string(value)
179: 		case pcapngOptionIfTSResol:
180: 			if size == 1 {
181: 				intf.TSResol = value[0]
182: 			}
183: 		}
184: 		options = options[4+padded:]
185: 	}
186: 
187: 	return intf, nil
188: }

190: func (p *Reader) parsePacket(body []byte) (Packet, error) {
191: 	if len(body) < 20 {
192: 		return Packet{}, fmt.Errorf("short pcapng enhanced packet")
193: 	}
194: 	packet := Packet{
195: 		InterfaceID:    binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[0:4]),
196: 		OriginalLength: binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[16:20]),
197: 	}
198: 	if int(packet.InterfaceID) >= len(p.interfaces) {
199: 		return Packet{}, fmt.Errorf("pcapng packet for undeclared interface %d",
200: 			packet.InterfaceID)
201: 	}
202: 	captured := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[12:16])
203: 	if int(captured) > len(body)-20 {
204: 		return Packet{}, fmt.Errorf("pcapng packet data exceeds its block")
205: 	}
206: 	packet.Data = body[20 : 20+captured]
207: 
208: 	raw := uint64(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[4:8]))<<32 |
209: 		uint64(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[8:12]))
210: 	timestamp, err := pcapngNanosecondsFrom(raw, p.interfaces[packet.InterfaceID].TSResol)
211: 	if err != nil {
212: 		return Packet{}, err
213: 	}
214: 	packet.Timestamp = timestamp
215: 
216: 	return packet, nil
217: }

219: // pcapngNanosecondsFrom converts a timestamp in an interface's resolution to nanoseconds.
220: // Only decimal resolutions up to nanoseconds occur in clabwire streams.
221: func pcapngNanosecondsFrom(raw uint64, tsresol byte) (int64, error) {
222: 	if tsresol&0x80 != 0 || tsresol > pcapngNanoseconds {
223: 		return 0, fmt.Errorf("unsupported pcapng timestamp resolution %#x", tsresol)
224: 	}
225: 	scale := uint64(1)
226: 	for range pcapngNanoseconds - int(tsresol) {
227: 		scale *= 10
228: 	}
229: 	if raw > math.MaxInt64/scale {
230: 		return 0, fmt.Errorf("pcapng timestamp out of range")
231: 	}
232: 
233: 	return int64(raw * scale), nil //nolint:gosec // bounded above
234: }
235: 
236: // Writer writes one little-endian section with nanosecond timestamps. Every block goes out
237: // in one Write under a lock, so concurrent writers never interleave blocks and a stream cut
238: // between writes is still a valid capture.
239: type Writer struct {
240: 	mu  sync.Mutex
241: 	w   io.Writer
242: 	err error
243: }
244: 
245: // NewWriter returns a writer of one pcapng section to w.
246: func NewWriter(w io.Writer) *Writer {
247: 	return &Writer{w: w}
248: }
249: 
250: // WriteHeader writes the Section Header Block and one Interface Description Block per name, in
251: // order; packets refer to the interfaces by that index.
252: func (p *Writer) WriteHeader(names []string, snapLength uint32) error {
253: 	section := make([]byte, 16)
254: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(section[0:], pcapngByteOrderMagic)
255: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(section[4:], 1)
256: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(section[6:], 0)
257: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(section[8:], math.MaxUint64)
258: 	section = appendPCAPNGOption(section, pcapngOptionUserAppl, []byte(captureUserApplication))
259: 	section = appendPCAPNGOption(section, pcapngOptionEnd, nil)
260: 
261: 	header := pcapngBlock(pcapngSectionHeaderType, section)
262: 	for _, name := range names {
263: 		description := make([]byte, 8)
264: 		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(description[0:], pcapngLinkTypeEthernet)
265: 		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(description[4:], snapLength)
266: 		description = appendPCAPNGOption(description, pcapngOptionIfName, []byte(name))
267: 		description = appendPCAPNGOption(description, pcapngOptionIfTSResol,
268: 			[]byte{pcapngNanoseconds})
269: 		description = appendPCAPNGOption(description, pcapngOptionEnd, nil)
270: 		header = append(header, pcapngBlock(pcapngInterfaceType, description)...)
271: 	}
272: 
273: 	return p.write(header)
274: }
275: 
276: // WritePacket writes an Enhanced Packet Block for the interface with the given index.
277: func (p *Writer) WritePacket(interfaceID uint32, packet *Packet) error {
278: 	timestamp := uint64(packet.Timestamp) //nolint:gosec // capture timestamps are positive
279: 	body := make([]byte, 20, 20+len(packet.Data)+3)
280: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(body[0:], interfaceID)
281: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(body[4:], uint32(timestamp>>32))
282: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(body[8:], uint32(timestamp)) //nolint:gosec // low 32 bits
283: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(body[12:], uint32(len(packet.Data)))
284: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(body[16:], packet.OriginalLength)
285: 	body = append(body, packet.Data...)
286: 	body = append(body, make([]byte, pcapngPadding(len(packet.Data)))...)
287: 
288: 	return p.write(pcapngBlock(pcapngEnhancedPacketType, body))
289: }
290: 
291: // Err returns the first write error, or nil.
292: func (p *Writer) Err() error {
293: 	p.mu.Lock()
294: 	defer p.mu.Unlock()
295: 
296: 	return p.err
297: }
298: 
299: func (p *Writer) write(block []byte) error {
300: 	p.mu.Lock()
301: 	defer p.mu.Unlock()
302: 
303: 	if p.err != nil {
304: 		return p.err
305: 	}
306: 	if _, err := p.w.Write(block); err != nil {
307: 		p.err = fmt.Errorf("failed to write the capture: %w", err)
308: 	}
309: 
310: 	return p.err
311: }
312: 
313: func pcapngBlock(blockType uint32, body []byte) []byte {
314: 	total := uint32(12 + len(body)) //nolint:gosec // bounded by the snap length
315: 	block := make([]byte, 8, total)
316: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(block[0:], blockType)
317: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(block[4:], total)
318: 	block = append(block, body...)
319: 
320: 	return binary.LittleEndian.AppendUint32(block, total)
321: }
322: 
323: func appendPCAPNGOption(body []byte, code uint16, value []byte) []byte {
324: 	body = binary.LittleEndian.AppendUint16(body, code)
325: 	body = binary.LittleEndian.AppendUint16(body, uint16(len(value))) //nolint:gosec // short
326: 	body = append(body, value...)
327: 
328: 	return append(body, make([]byte, pcapngPadding(len(value)))...)
329: }
330: 
331: func pcapngPadding(length int) int {
332: 	return (4 - length%4) % 4
333: }

15: // Snap length bounds of a capture.
16: const (
17: 	// DefaultSnapLength is the snap length of a request without one.
18: 	DefaultSnapLength = 256 << 10
19: 	MinSnapLength     = 64
20: 	MaxSnapLength     = 1 << 20
21: )
22: 
23: // ValidateRequest checks the bounds of a capture request and fills the default snap length.
24: func ValidateRequest(req *clablabruntime.CaptureRequest) error {
25: 	if req.Name == "" {
26: 		return fmt.Errorf("topology name is required")
27: 	}
28: 	if len(req.Targets) == 0 {
29: 		return fmt.Errorf("at least one capture target (node and interface) is required")
30: 	}
31: 	for _, target := range req.Targets {
32: 		if target.Node == "" || target.Interface == "" {
33: 			return fmt.Errorf("capture target %+v needs a node and an interface", target)
34: 		}
35: 	}
36: 	if req.Duration < 0 {
37: 		return fmt.Errorf("capture duration must not be negative")
38: 	}
39: 	if req.PacketLimit < 0 {
40: 		return fmt.Errorf("capture packet limit must not be negative")
41: 	}
42: 	if req.SnapLength == 0 {
43: 		req.SnapLength = DefaultSnapLength
44: 	}
45: 	if req.SnapLength < MinSnapLength || req.SnapLength > MaxSnapLength {
46: 		return fmt.Errorf("capture snap length %d is outside %d to %d bytes", req.SnapLength,
47: 			MinSnapLength, MaxSnapLength)
48: 	}
49: 
50: 	return nil
51: }
52: 
53: // FindInterface matches a requested interface by its name, then by its alias.
54: func FindInterface(
55: 	entries []clablabruntime.CaptureInterface,
56: 	name string,
57: ) (clablabruntime.CaptureInterface, bool) {
58: 	for _, entry := range entries {
59: 		if entry.Interface == name {
60: 			return entry, true
61: 		}
62: 	}
63: 	for _, entry := range entries {
64: 		if entry.Alias != "" && entry.Alias == name {
65: 			return entry, true
66: 		}
67: 	}
68: 
69: 	return clablabruntime.CaptureInterface{}, false
70: }
71: 
72: // DescribeInterfaces lists interfaces for an error message: name (alias), ...
73: func DescribeInterfaces(entries []clablabruntime.CaptureInterface) string {
74: 	if len(entries) == 0 {
75: 		return "none"
76: 	}
77: 
78: 	names := make([]string, 0, len(entries))
79: 	for _, entry := range entries {
80: 		name := entry.Interface
81: 		if entry.Alias != "" {
82: 			name += " (" + entry.Alias + ")"
83: 		}
84: 		names = append(names, name)
85: 	}
86: 
87: 	return strings.Join(names, ", ")
88: }

90: // ReportGap hands a gap to onGap, or logs it as a warning when onGap is nil.
91: func ReportGap(onGap func(clablabruntime.CaptureGap), gap clablabruntime.CaptureGap) {
92: 	if onGap != nil {
93: 		onGap(gap)
94: 		return
95: 	}
96: 
97: 	to := "unknown"
98: 	if !gap.To.IsZero() {
99: 		to = gap.To.Format(time.RFC3339Nano)
100: 	}
101: 	log.Warn("Capture has a gap", "node", gap.Node, "interfaces", strings.Join(gap.Interfaces, ","),
102: 		"from", gap.From.Format(time.RFC3339Nano), "to", to, "reason", gap.Reason)
103: }

105: // Output is the merged pcapng stream of one capture: the section header with one interface per
106: // capture target, then the packets of every target in timestamp order (through a Reorder), up
107: // to an optional packet limit.
108: type Output struct {
109: 	writer  *Writer
110: 	reorder *Reorder
111: 	limit   int64
112: 	written atomic.Int64
113: 	stop    func()
114: 
115: 	cancelRun context.CancelFunc
116: 	runDone   chan struct{}
117: }
118: 
119: // NewOutput writes the section header and one Interface Description Block per name to w, then
120: // starts the reorder buffer with the given window (zero or less writes packets as they come).
121: // stop is called once the packet limit is reached or a write failed. Close must be called.
122: func NewOutput(
123: 	w io.Writer,
124: 	names []string,
125: 	snapLength, packetLimit int,
126: 	window time.Duration,
127: 	stop func(),
128: ) (*Output, error) {
129: 	writer := NewWriter(w)
130: 	if err := writer.WriteHeader(
131: 		names,
132: 		uint32(snapLength),
133: 	); err != nil { //nolint:gosec // validated
134: 		return nil, err
135: 	}
136: 
137: 	out := &Output{
138: 		writer:  writer,
139: 		reorder: NewReorder(window, writer.WritePacket, stop),
140: 		limit:   int64(packetLimit),
141: 		stop:    stop,
142: 		runDone: make(chan struct{}),
143: 	}
144: 
145: 	var runCtx context.Context
146: 	runCtx, out.cancelRun = context.WithCancel(context.Background())
147: 	go func() {
148: 		defer close(out.runDone)
149: 		out.reorder.Run(runCtx)
150: 	}()
151: 
152: 	return out, nil
153: }
154: 
155: // Emit hands a packet of the interface with the given index to the stream. It reports false
156: // once the packet limit is reached and the capture stops, and returns the error of a failed
157: // write.
158: func (o *Output) Emit(id uint32, packet *Packet) (bool, error) {
159: 	if o.limit > 0 {
160: 		count := o.written.Add(1)
161: 		if count > o.limit {
162: 			o.stop()
163: 			return false, nil
164: 		}
165: 		if err := o.reorder.Push(id, packet); err != nil {
166: 			return false, err
167: 		}
168: 		if count == o.limit {
169: 			o.stop()
170: 			return false, nil
171: 		}
172: 
173: 		return true, nil
174: 	}
175: 
176: 	o.written.Add(1)
177: 
178: 	return true, o.reorder.Push(id, packet)
179: }
180: 
181: // Written returns the number of packets handed to the stream so far.
182: func (o *Output) Written() int64 {
183: 	return o.written.Load()
184: }
185: 
186: // Hold keeps packets stamped after timestamp back until Release(key).
187: func (o *Output) Hold(key any, timestamp int64) {
188: 	o.reorder.Hold(key, timestamp)
189: }
190: 
191: // Release removes the hold of key.
192: func (o *Output) Release(key any) {
193: 	o.reorder.Release(key)
194: }
195: 
196: // Close writes the packets still held back and returns the first write error.
197: func (o *Output) Close() error {
198: 	o.cancelRun()
199: 	<-o.runDone
200: 	o.reorder.Flush()
201: 
202: 	return o.writer.Err()
203: }

Reasoning
Notable observations so far:

1. `capture/local.go` `drain()`: after ctx done, drain reads with `time.Now().Before(deadline)` — but ReadPacket can block up to localPollTimeout (100ms), deadline is end+250ms. Potential issue: `drain` loops calling `source.ReadPacket()` — if source returns errReadTimeout after `localDrainQuiet` it returns. OK.

2. `localReader.run`: on ctx done, drain; but note when `r.out.Emit` returns `!more` (packet limit reached), reader returns without drain — fine.

3. `Output.Emit`: increments `written` before push; if `reorder.Push` fails, count already added. Minor.

4. `Reorder.Push` with cursor: `q.cursor != 0 && packet.Timestamp < q.cursor` — late packets written out of order. Note `cursor` only updated in popLocked. `writeLocked` direct writes don't update cursor... Actually in Push, late packet writeLocked does not update cursor — but late packet is behind cursor already, fine.

5. `Reorder.writeDue` holds: computes min timestamp among holds; packets with Timestamp > limit wait. OK.

6. `Output.Close` calls cancelRun then waits, then Flush — but Flush writes remaining packets ignoring holds (flushes all). Good.

7. Potential deadlock in local.go `run`: readers exit when `Emit` returns false... after stop() called (packet limit), sources still open; readers return. wg.Wait. Fine.

8. `drain` deadline: `deadline := end.Add(localDrainTimeout)`; loop condition `time.Now().Before(deadline)`; inside, if errReadTimeout && time.Since(end) < localDrainQuiet → continue; but if time.Since(end) >= localDrainQuiet and errReadTimeout, falls to `if err != nil || ...` → return. OK.

9. In `drain`, `info.Timestamp.After(end)` returns, dropping packets stamped after end — reasonable.

10. capture/local.go reopen: after ctx done reports gap with To zero. OK.

Potential bug: In `localCapture.run`, when `NewOutput` fails, closes sources and returns — but the `captureCtx` cancel timers are deferred, fine.

Potential issue: `openAll` — if `l.open` returns fewer sources than `len(group.names)`? e.g., opened has len != len(names); mapping `sources[group.indexes[idx]]` would panic index out of range if opened shorter, or leave nil entries if longer. openPacketSockets appends one per interface, so equal in practice. Minor.

11. pcapng.go `Next`: peek of 4 bytes for byte-order magic at SHB — if the peek fails with EOF returns ErrUnexpectedEOF even when it's a clean EOF (truncated section header at end). Minor.

Also `if binary.BigEndian.Uint32(magic) == pcapngByteOrderMagic` — big-endian section detection. OK.

12. Writer.WriteHeader: section header block: `section := make([]byte, 16)`, puts magic at 0, major 4, minor 6, section length 8..16 math.MaxUint64. Correct per spec.

13. `pcapngBlock` — total = 12+len(body). Block = 4 type + 4 length + body + 4 total. Good.

14. appendPCAPNGOption padding: appends value then padding of len(value) — correct.

15. `WritePacket` timestamp: `uint64(packet.Timestamp)` — if Timestamp negative (pre-1970), wraps. nolint noted. Minor.

16. Reorder.Run wait computation: `next.Sub(q.now())` could be negative? It computes max(..., time.Millisecond). OK.

17. `resetTimer` — standard.

Now, the bigger files: cmd/capture.go, core/capture.go, core/capture_local.go, labruntime/clabernetes/capture.go (1202 lines), capture_interfaces.go, and diffs to cmd/* (context, inspect, options, root). Let me read cmd/capture.go and core/capture_local.go, core/capture.go.
The `capture` package looks well-structured. Now let me review the command layer and core integration.

108: containerlab -r c9s capture --name srl --target srl1:e1-1 -w srl.pcapng`
109: 
110: 	return c, nil
111: }

113: func captureFn(cmd *cobra.Command, o *Options) error {
114: 	if o.Global.TopologyName == "" && o.Global.TopologyFile == "" {
115: 		return fmt.Errorf("provide either a lab name (--name) or a topology file path (--topo)")
116: 	}
117: 
118: 	if o.Capture.List {
119: 		return captureListFn(cmd, o)
120: 	}
121: 
122: 	targets, err := parseCaptureTargets(o.Capture.Targets)
123: 	if err != nil {
124: 		return err
125: 	}
126: 
127: 	c, err := clabcore.NewContainerLab(o.ToClabOptions()...)
128: 	if err != nil {
129: 		return err
130: 	}
131: 
132: 	// An interrupt ends the capture; the command still finishes the file and exits cleanly.
133: 	// Armed before the file is created, so an interrupt never leaves it empty.
134: 	o.Global.FinishOnCancel.Store(true)
135: 	defer o.Global.FinishOnCancel.Store(false)
136: 
137: 	output := cmd.OutOrStdout()
138: 	if o.Capture.Write != "" && o.Capture.Write != "-" {
139: 		file, err := os.Create(o.Capture.Write)
140: 		if err != nil {
141: 			return fmt.Errorf("failed to create the capture file: %w", err)
142: 		}
143: 		defer file.Close()
144: 		output = file
145: 
146: 		// the file belongs to the user who ran the command, also through sudo or setuid
147: 		if err := clabutils.SetUIDAndGID(o.Capture.Write); err != nil {
148: 			log.Debug("Cannot hand the capture file to the user", "file", o.Capture.Write,
149: 				"error", err)
150: 		}
151: 	}
152: 
153: 	err = c.Capture(cmd.Context(), clablabruntime.CaptureRequest{
154: 		Targets:     targets,
155: 		Duration:    o.Capture.Duration,
156: 		PacketLimit: o.Capture.PacketLimit,
157: 		SnapLength:  o.Capture.SnapLength,
158: 	}, output)
159: 	if err != nil {
160: 		return err
161: 	}
162: 
163: 	if file, ok := output.(*os.File); ok && output != cmd.OutOrStdout() {
164: 		if err := file.Sync(); err != nil {
165: 			return fmt.Errorf("failed to write the capture file: %w", err)
166: 		}
167: 	}
168: 
169: 	return nil
170: }
171: 
172: // parseCaptureTargets parses --target values: <node>:<interface>[,<interface>...]. The node name
173: // ends at the first colon, so interface names may contain colons or slashes.
174: func parseCaptureTargets(values []string) ([]clablabruntime.CaptureTarget, error) {
175: 	if len(values) == 0 {
176: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("provide at least one --target <node>:<interface>[,<interface>...]")
177: 	}
178: 
179: 	targets := make([]clablabruntime.CaptureTarget, 0, len(values))
180: 	for _, value := range values {
181: 		node, interfaces, ok := strings.Cut(strings.TrimSpace(value), ":")
182: 		node = strings.TrimSpace(node)
183: 		if !ok || node == "" || strings.TrimSpace(interfaces) == "" {
184: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid --target %q: use <node>:<interface>[,<interface>...]",
185: 				value)
186: 		}
187: 
188: 		for _, name := range strings.Split(interfaces, ",") {
189: 			name = strings.TrimSpace(name)
190: 			if name == "" {
191: 				return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid --target %q: empty interface name", value)
192: 			}
193: 			targets = append(targets, clablabruntime.CaptureTarget{Node: node, Interface: name})
194: 		}
195: 	}
196: 
197: 	return targets, nil
198: }

200: func captureListFn(cmd *cobra.Command, o *Options) error {
201: 	format := o.Capture.Format
202: 	if format == "" {
203: 		format = clabconstants.FormatTable
204: 	}
205: 	if format != clabconstants.FormatTable && format != clabconstants.FormatJSON {
206: 		return fmt.Errorf("output format %q is not supported, use 'table' or 'json'", format)
207: 	}
208: 	if len(o.Capture.Targets) != 0 {
209: 		return fmt.Errorf("--list lists every running node's interfaces; it takes no --target")
210: 	}
211: 
212: 	c, err := clabcore.NewContainerLab(o.ToClabOptions()...)
213: 	if err != nil {
214: 		return err
215: 	}
216: 
217: 	interfaces, err := c.CaptureInterfaces(cmd.Context())
218: 	if err != nil {
219: 		return err
220: 	}
221: 
222: 	return printCaptureInterfaces(cmd.OutOrStdout(), interfaces, format)
223: }
