1: package core
2: 
3: import (
4: 	"context"
5: 	"fmt"
6: 	"io"
7: 	"slices"
8: 	"sort"
9: 	"strings"
10: 
11: 	clabcapture "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/capture"
12: 	clablabruntime "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/labruntime"
13: 	clablinks "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/links"
14: 	clabnodes "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/nodes"
15: 	clabruntime "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/runtime"
16: )
17: 
18: // localCaptureInterface is a lab link interface of a node on this machine.
19: type localCaptureInterface struct {
20: 	node clabnodes.Node
21: 	info clablabruntime.CaptureInterface
22: }
23: 
24: // localCaptureInterfaces lists the link interfaces of the lab's nodes the topology defines, with
25: // the far end of each link, per node name. Host and management network endpoints are the far
26: // ends of links, not nodes to capture on.
27: func (c *CLab) localCaptureInterfaces() (map[string][]localCaptureInterface, error) {
28: 	if len(c.Nodes) == 0 {
29: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("the topology of lab %q is not available; capture reads the "+
30: 			"lab's links from it, pass it with --topo", c.Config.Name)
31: 	}
32: 	if len(c.Links) == 0 {
33: 		if err := c.ResolveLinks(); err != nil {
34: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to resolve the links of lab %q: %w", c.Config.Name, err)
35: 		}
36: 	}
37: 
38: 	indexes := make([]int, 0, len(c.Links))
39: 	for idx := range c.Links {
40: 		indexes = append(indexes, idx)
41: 	}
42: 	sort.Ints(indexes)
43: 
44: 	result := map[string][]localCaptureInterface{}
45: 	for _, idx := range indexes {
46: 		endpoints := c.Links[idx].GetEndpoints()
47: 		for epIdx, endpoint := range endpoints {
48: 			if endpoint.IsNodeless() || endpoint.IsRuntimeDiscovered() ||
49: 				endpoint.GetNode() == nil {
50: 				continue
51: 			}
52: 			name := endpoint.GetNode().GetShortName()
53: 			node, ok := c.Nodes[name]
54: 			if !ok {
55: 				continue
56: 			}
57: 
58: 			info := clablabruntime.CaptureInterface{
59: 				Node:      name,
60: 				Interface: endpoint.GetIfaceName(),
61: 			}
62: 			if alias := endpoint.GetIfaceAlias(); alias != info.Interface {
63: 				info.Alias = alias
64: 			}
65: 			if len(endpoints) == 2 {
66: 				peer := endpoints[1-epIdx]
67: 				info.PeerNode = capturePeerNode(peer)
68: 				info.PeerInterface = peer.GetIfaceDisplayName()
69: 			}
70: 
71: 			result[name] = append(result[name], localCaptureInterface{node: node, info: info})
72: 		}
73: 	}
74: 
75: 	return result, nil
76: }
77: 
78: // capturePeerNode names the node at the far end of a link: "host" for a host endpoint and
79: // "mgmt-net" for the management network, whose shared link nodes carry other names once a lab
80: // was deployed.
81: func capturePeerNode(peer clablinks.Endpoint) string {
82: 	if peer.IsNodeless() {
83: 		if _, ok := peer.(*clablinks.EndpointBridge); ok {
84: 			return string(clablinks.LinkTypeMgmtNet)
85: 		}
86: 
87: 		return string(clablinks.LinkTypeHost)
88: 	}
89: 	if peer.GetNode() == nil {
90: 		return ""
91: 	}
92: 
93: 	return peer.GetNode().GetShortName()
94: }
95: 
96: // lookupLocalNode finds a lab node by its topology name or its container name.
97: func (c *CLab) lookupLocalNode(name string) (clabnodes.Node, error) {
98: 	if node, ok := c.Nodes[name]; ok {
99: 		return node, nil
100: 	}
101: 	for _, node := range c.Nodes {
102: 		if node.Config().LongName == name {
103: 			return node, nil
104: 		}
105: 	}
106: 
107: 	names := make([]string, 0, len(c.Nodes))
108: 	for nodeName := range c.Nodes {
109: 		names = append(names, nodeName)
110: 	}
111: 	slices.Sort(names)
112: 
113: 	return nil, fmt.Errorf("node %q is not part of lab %q; nodes: %s", name, c.Config.Name,
114: 		strings.Join(names, ", "))
115: }
116: 
117: // nodeRuns reports whether a node's network namespace can be entered.
118: func nodeRuns(ctx context.Context, node clabnodes.Node) bool {
119: 	if node.Config().IsRootNamespaceBased {
120: 		return true
121: 	}
122: 
123: 	return clabruntime.ContainerHasJoinableNetns(node.GetContainerStatus(ctx))
124: }
125: 
126: // localCaptureInterfacesOf implements CaptureInterfaces for Docker and Podman: the requested
127: // nodes, or every running node.
128: func (c *CLab) localCaptureInterfacesOf(
129: 	ctx context.Context,
130: 	nodeNames []string,
131: ) ([]clablabruntime.CaptureInterface, error) {
132: 	if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
133: 		return nil, err
134: 	}
135: 	byNode, err := c.localCaptureInterfaces()
136: 	if err != nil {
137: 		return nil, err
138: 	}
139: 
140: 	var nodes []clabnodes.Node
141: 	if len(nodeNames) == 0 {
142: 		for _, node := range c.Nodes {
143: 			if nodeRuns(ctx, node) {
144: 				nodes = append(nodes, node)
145: 			}
146: 		}
147: 	} else {
148: 		for _, name := range nodeNames {
149: 			node, err := c.lookupLocalNode(name)
150: 			if err != nil {
151: 				return nil, err
152: 			}
153: 			nodes = append(nodes, node)
154: 		}
155: 	}
156: 
157: 	result := make([]clablabruntime.CaptureInterface, 0)
158: 	seen := map[string]bool{}
159: 	for _, node := range nodes {
160: 		name := node.Config().ShortName
161: 		if seen[name] {
162: 			continue
163: 		}
164: 		seen[name] = true
165: 		for _, entry := range byNode[name] {
166: 			result = append(result, entry.info)
167: 		}
168: 	}

170: 
171: 	return result, nil
172: }

174: func sortCaptureInterfaces(interfaces []clablabruntime.CaptureInterface) {
175: 	sort.SliceStable(interfaces, func(i, j int) bool {
176: 		if interfaces[i].Node != interfaces[j].Node {
177: 			return interfaces[i].Node < interfaces[j].Node
178: 		}
179: 
180: 		return interfaces[i].Interface < interfaces[j].Interface
181: 	})
182: }

184: // resolveLocalCaptureTargets checks every target against the node's link interfaces, by name or
185: // alias, and returns them in request order.
186: func (c *CLab) resolveLocalCaptureTargets(
187: 	targets []clablabruntime.CaptureTarget,
188: ) ([]clabcapture.LocalTarget, error) {
189: 	byNode, err := c.localCaptureInterfaces()
190: 	if err != nil {
191: 		return nil, err
192: 	}
193: 
194: 	resolved := make([]clabcapture.LocalTarget, 0, len(targets))
195: 	seen := map[string]bool{}
196: 	for _, target := range targets {
197: 		node, err := c.lookupLocalNode(target.Node)
198: 		if err != nil {
199: 			return nil, err
200: 		}
201: 		name := node.Config().ShortName
202: 
203: 		infos := make([]clablabruntime.CaptureInterface, 0, len(byNode[name]))
204: 		for _, entry := range byNode[name] {
205: 			infos = append(infos, entry.info)
206: 		}
207: 		sortCaptureInterfaces(infos)
208: 		info, ok := clabcapture.FindInterface(infos, target.Interface)
209: 		if !ok {
210: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("interface %q of node %q is not a capturable link "+
211: 				"interface; capturable: %s", target.Interface, target.Node,
212: 				clabcapture.DescribeInterfaces(infos))
213: 		}
214: 
215: 		key := name + "\x00" + info.Interface
216: 		if seen[key] {
217: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("interface %q of node %q is requested more than once",
218: 				info.Interface, target.Node)
219: 		}
220: 		seen[key] = true
221: 
222: 		resolved = append(resolved, clabcapture.LocalTarget{
223: 			Node:      name,
224: 			Interface: info.Interface,
225: 			Exec:      node.ExecFunction,
226: 		})
227: 	}
228: 
229: 	return resolved, nil
230: }

232: // captureLocal implements Capture for Docker and Podman through packet sockets in the nodes'

235: 	ctx context.Context,
236: 	req clablabruntime.CaptureRequest,
237: 	w io.Writer,
238: ) error {

247: 	}

250: 	if err != nil {

252: 	}
253: 
254: 	return clabcapture.CaptureLocal(ctx, req, targets, w)

341: // resolveCaptureTargets locates every target node, checks every interface against the

343: func (r *Runtime) resolveCaptureTargets(
344: 	ctx context.Context,
345: 	req clablabruntime.CaptureRequest,
346: ) (*resolvedCapture, error) {
347: 	nodeOrder := make([]string, 0, len(req.Targets))
348: 	seenNodes := map[string]bool{}
349: 	for _, target := range req.Targets {
350: 		if !seenNodes[target.Node] {
351: 			seenNodes[target.Node] = true
352: 			nodeOrder = append(nodeOrder, target.Node)

354: 	}

357: 		Name: req.Name, Namespace: req.Namespace, Nodes: nodeOrder, Identity: req.Identity,
358: 	})
359: 	if err != nil {
360: 		return nil, err
361: 	}
362: 	byRequest := make(map[string]clablabruntime.NodeLocation, len(nodeOrder))
363: 	for idx, name := range nodeOrder {
364: 		byRequest[name] = locations[idx]
365: 	}
366: 
367: 	listed, err := r.listCaptureInterfaces(ctx, req.Name, locations)
368: 	if err != nil {
369: 		return nil, err
370: 	}

373: 		return nil, err
374: 	}
375: 
376: 	resolved := &resolvedCapture{}
377: 	groups := map[string]*captureGroup{}
378: 	seen := map[string]bool{}
379: 	for _, target := range req.Targets {
380: 		location := byRequest[target.Node]
381: 		entry, ok := findCaptureInterface(listed[location.NodeName], target.Interface)
382: 		if !ok {
383: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("interface %q of node %q is not a capturable link "+
384: 				"interface; capturable: %s", target.Interface, target.Node,
385: 				describeCaptureInterfaces(listed[location.NodeName]))
386: 		}
387: 
388: 		key := location.NodeName + "\x00" + entry.Interface
389: 		if seen[key] {
390: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("interface %q of node %q is requested more than once",
391: 				entry.Interface, target.Node)
392: 		}
393: 		seen[key] = true
394: 
395: 		group := groups[location.NodeName]
396: 		if group == nil {
397: 			group = &captureGroup{
398: 				location: location,
399: 				display:  names.display(location.NodeName),
400: 			}
401: 			groups[location.NodeName] = group
402: 			resolved.groups = append(resolved.groups, group)
403: 		}
404: 
405: 		id := uint32(len(resolved.names)) //nolint:gosec // bounded by the targets
406: 		group.interfaces = append(group.interfaces, entry.Interface)
407: 		group.ids = append(group.ids, id)
408: 		resolved.names = append(resolved.names, group.display+":"+entry.Interface)
409: 	}
410: 
411: 	return resolved, nil
412: }

415: func findCaptureInterface(entries []clabwireInterface, name string) (clabwireInterface, bool) {
416: 	for _, entry := range entries {
417: 		if entry.Interface == name {
418: 			return entry, true
419: 		}

421: 	for _, entry := range entries {

430: func describeCaptureInterfaces(entries []clabwireInterface) string {

447: // Capture streams pcapng from lab link interfaces to w: one section, one Interface Description
448: // Block per target in request order named <node>:<interface>, then the packets of every target.
449: //
450: // Each node's interfaces are captured by one clabwire process in the node's pod. clabwire limits
451: // a capture to one hour, so a longer capture (or one without Duration) chains captures: the next
452: // one starts before the current one ends, and the stream switches at a cut in the overlap. See
453: // captureChain for how packets of the overlap are kept once.
454: //
455: // Packets go out in timestamp order across nodes, through a reorder buffer (captureReorder).
456: //
457: // Every clabwire process runs with stdin attached and --stop-on-stdin-close: a Kubernetes exec
458: // does not stop its process when the stream closes, so containerlab closes stdin whenever a
459: // segment ends (the capture ends, fails, its output fails, or a newer segment took over) and
460: // clabwire ends the capture itself.
461: //
462: // Capture returns when Duration has passed, PacketLimit packets were written, or ctx ends; an
463: // ended ctx is not an error. Every block reaches w in one write, so the stream is a valid capture
464: // whenever it stops. A clabwire Denied or Failed audit record is returned as an error.
465: func (r *Runtime) Capture(
466: 	ctx context.Context,
467: 	req clablabruntime.CaptureRequest,
468: 	w io.Writer,
469: ) error {
470: 	if err := clabcapture.ValidateRequest(&req); err != nil {
471: 		return err
472: 	}
473: 
474: 	r, err := r.connect(ctx, req.Identity)
475: 	if err != nil {
476: 		return err
477: 	}
478: 
479: 	resolved, err := r.resolveCaptureTargets(ctx, req)
480: 	if err != nil {
481: 		return err
482: 	}
483: 
484: 	captureCtx, stop := context.WithCancel(ctx)
485: 	defer stop()
486: 
487: 	out, err := clabcapture.NewOutput(w, resolved.names, req.SnapLength, req.PacketLimit,
488: 		r.captureReorderWindowLength(), stop)
489: 	if err != nil {
490: 		return err
491: 	}
492: 
493: 	run := &captureRun{
494: 		r:       r,
495: 		req:     req,
496: 		out:     out,
497: 		segment: r.captureSegmentLength(),
498: 	}
499: 	if req.Duration > 0 {
500: 		run.deadline = time.Now().Add(req.Duration)
501: 	}
502: 	run.overlap = min(maxCaptureOverlap, run.segment/3)
503: 	run.window = min(maxCaptureCutWindow, run.overlap/4)
504: 
505: 	if req.Duration > 0 {
506: 		// a clabwire process that does not end on its own does not hold the capture open
507: 		var cancelTimeout context.CancelFunc
508: 		captureCtx, cancelTimeout = context.WithTimeout(captureCtx,
509: 			req.Duration+run.overlap+captureEndGrace)
510: 		defer cancelTimeout()
511: 	}
512: 
513: 	group, groupCtx := errgroup.WithContext(captureCtx)
514: 	for _, captureGroup := range resolved.groups {
515: 		chain := &captureChain{capture: run, group: captureGroup}
516: 		group.Go(func() error {
517: 			return chain.run(groupCtx)
518: 		})
519: 	}
520: 
521: 	err = group.Wait()
522: 	if writeErr := out.Close(); writeErr != nil {
523: 		return writeErr
524: 	}
525: 	if err != nil && !(errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) && captureCtx.Err() != nil) {
526: 		return err
527: 	}
528: 
529: 	return nil
530: }
531: 
532: // captureRun is the state a capture's chains share.
533: type captureRun struct {
534: 	r   *Runtime
535: 	req clablabruntime.CaptureRequest
536: 	// out is the merged stream; it writes the packets of every chain in timestamp order and
537: 	// stops every chain once the packet limit is reached.
538: 	out *clabcapture.Output
539: 
540: 	segment  time.Duration
541: 	overlap  time.Duration
542: 	window   time.Duration
543: 	deadline time.Time
544: }
545: 
546: // emit writes a packet under its merged interface ID. It reports false once the packet limit is
547: // reached and the capture stops.
548: func (run *captureRun) emit(id uint32, packet *clabcapture.Packet) (bool, error) {
549: 	return run.out.Emit(id, packet)
550: }
551: 
552: func (run *captureRun) reportGap(gap clablabruntime.CaptureGap) {
553: 	clabcapture.ReportGap(run.req.OnGap, gap)
554: }
555: 
556: // captureSegment is one clabwire capture process of a chain.
557: type captureSegment struct {
558: 	index      int
559: 	localStart time.Time
560: 	duration   time.Duration
561: 	cancel     context.CancelFunc
562: 	// closeStdin closes the stdin of the segment's clabwire process, which ends it; it may be
563: 	// called any number of times.
564: 	closeStdin func()
565: 	// stopTimer closes stdin once the segment is no longer needed after a switch-over.
566: 	stopTimer *time.Timer
567: 	// started and ended are the pod-clock times of the Started and Succeeded audit records.
568: 	started time.Time
569: 	ended   time.Time
570: 	done    bool
571: }
572: 
573: func (s *captureSegment) plannedEnd() time.Time {
574: 	return s.started.Add(s.duration)
575: }
576: 
577: // segmentEvent is something a segment reported: a packet, an audit record, or its end.
578: type segmentEvent struct {
579: 	segment *captureSegment
580: 	packet  *clabcapture.Packet
581: 	audit   *captureAudit
582: 	done    bool
583: 	err     error
584: }
585: 
586: // captureChain runs the chained clabwire captures of one group.
587: //
588: // Chaining and the cut: segment k+1 starts `overlap` before segment k is due to end, so both
589: // capture the same packets for a while. clabwire stamps packets when it reads them, so two
590: // processes give the same packet timestamps a few microseconds apart, and timestamps alone
591: // cannot pair them. The chain therefore cuts in the middle of the overlap and matches packets by
592: // content close to the cut:
593: //
594: //  1. When segment k+1 reports Started (pod clock, from its audit record), the cut is
595: //     T = midpoint of [Started(k+1), Started(k) + duration(k)]: both segments run then.
596: //  2. Segment k keeps streaming live, but only packets stamped before T; it remembers the
597: //     content of what it wrote since segment k+1 started.
598: //  3. Segment k+1's packets are held back until segment k has ended. Then the ones stamped
599: //     before T-W are dropped (segment k had them), the ones stamped within W of T are dropped
600: //     when segment k wrote the same bytes on the same interface, and every other one is written.
601: //     From then on segment k+1 streams live.
602: //
603: // Once the pod clock passed T+W, segment k's stdin is closed so it ends without running to its
604: // planned end. While packets are held back, the chain holds the reorder buffer at T-W, so other
605: // nodes' later packets do not overtake them in the merged stream.
606: //
607: // W (500 ms, less for short test segments) covers the stamping difference. Identical frames on
608: // the same interface within W of the cut can be paired with each other, which can drop a true
609: // repeat; nothing else is lost or doubled. A follow-up segment that does not start in time leaves
610: // a gap, which is reported through CaptureRequest.OnGap (or logged), never silently ignored.
611: type captureChain struct {
612: 	capture *captureRun
613: 	group   *captureGroup
614: 
615: 	events chan segmentEvent
616: 	wg     sync.WaitGroup
617: 
618: 	active *captureSegment
619: 	next   *captureSegment
620: 	// cut is the switch time between active and next, in nanoseconds; zero until known.
621: 	cut int64
622: 	// emitted remembers the content of the packets active wrote while next runs.
623: 	emitted map[uint64]int
624: 	// held are the packets of next until active ends.
625: 	held     []*clabcapture.Packet
626: 	segments int
627: 	retries  int
628: 	// final is set once no further segment is due.
629: 	final bool
630: 	// stopping is set once ctx ended: the segments are asked to end and what they still
631: 	// deliver is written.
632: 	stopping bool
633: }
634: 
635: // run runs the chain until its last segment ended. When ctx ends, it stops the segments and
636: // keeps writing the packets they read until then; a segment that does not end within
637: // captureStdinCloseGrace is cut.
638: func (c *captureChain) run(ctx context.Context) error {
639: 	c.events = make(chan segmentEvent, 256)
640: 	// the segments outlive ctx so they can deliver their last packets; segmentsCtx cuts them
641: 	segmentsCtx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.WithoutCancel(ctx))
642: 	var abort *time.Timer
643: 	defer func() {
644: 		if abort != nil {
645: 			abort.Stop()
646: 		}
647: 		cancel()
648: 		c.drain()
649: 		c.capture.out.Release(c)
650: 	}()
651: 
652: 	c.active = c.start(segmentsCtx, c.segmentDuration(time.Now()))
653: 	timer := time.NewTimer(c.nextStartIn())
654: 	defer timer.Stop()
655: 
656: 	done := ctx.Done()
657: 	for {
658: 		select {
659: 		case <-done:
660: 			done = nil
661: 			c.stop(timer)
662: 			abort = time.AfterFunc(captureStdinCloseGrace, cancel)
663: 		case <-segmentsCtx.Done():
664: 			return nil
665: 		case <-timer.C:
666: 			if c.next == nil && !c.final {
667: 				c.startNext(segmentsCtx)
668: 			}
669: 		case event := <-c.events:
670: 			stop, err := c.handle(segmentsCtx, event, timer)
671: 			if err != nil || stop {
672: 				return err
673: 			}
674: 		}
675: 	}
676: }
677: 
678: // stop ends the chain early, like a deadline would: no further segment starts and the running
679: // ones are asked to end. The chain then writes what they deliver until they ended.
680: func (c *captureChain) stop(timer *time.Timer) {
681: 	c.stopping = true
682: 	c.final = true
683: 	timer.Stop()
684: 	c.active.closeStdin()
685: 	if c.next != nil {
686: 		c.next.closeStdin()
687: 	}
688: }
689: 
690: // drain waits for the segment goroutines after the chain ended.
691: func (c *captureChain) drain() {
692: 	done := make(chan struct{})
693: 	go func() {
694: 		c.wg.Wait()
695: 		close(done)
696: 	}()
697: 	for {
698: 		select {
699: 		case <-done:
700: 			return
701: 		case <-c.events:
702: 		}
703: 	}
704: }
705: 
706: // segmentDuration is the requested duration of a segment starting now.
707: func (c *captureChain) segmentDuration(now time.Time) time.Duration {
708: 	duration := c.capture.segment
709: 	if !c.capture.deadline.IsZero() {
710: 		duration = min(duration, c.capture.deadline.Sub(now))
711: 	}
712: 
713: 	return max(duration, minCaptureSegment)
714: }
715: 
716: // nextStartIn is the time until the follow-up of the active segment is due. It marks the chain
717: // final when none is due.
718: func (c *captureChain) nextStartIn() time.Duration {
719: 	if c.stopping {
720: 		c.final = true
721: 		return maxCaptureSegment
722: 	}
723: 	activeEnd := c.active.localStart.Add(c.active.duration)
724: 	if !c.capture.deadline.IsZero() &&
725: 		!activeEnd.Before(c.capture.deadline.Add(-c.capture.window)) {
726: 		c.final = true
727: 		return maxCaptureSegment
728: 	}
729: 	c.final = false
730: 
731: 	return max(time.Until(activeEnd.Add(-c.capture.overlap)), 0)
732: }
733: 
734: func (c *captureChain) startNext(ctx context.Context) {
735: 	c.next = c.start(ctx, c.segmentDuration(time.Now()))
736: 	c.emitted = map[uint64]int{}
737: 	c.held = nil
738: 	c.cut = 0
739: }
740: 
741: func (c *captureChain) handle(
742: 	ctx context.Context,
743: 	event segmentEvent,
744: 	timer *time.Timer,
745: ) (bool, error) {
746: 	segment := event.segment
747: 
748: 	switch {
749: 	case event.audit != nil:
750: 		return false, c.handleAudit(segment, event.audit)
751: 	case event.packet != nil:
752: 		return c.handlePacket(segment, event.packet)
753: 	case event.done:
754: 		segment.done = true
755: 		if segment.stopTimer != nil {
756: 			segment.stopTimer.Stop()
757: 		}
758: 		if event.err != nil && !c.stopping {
759: 			if segment == c.next && segment.started.IsZero() && c.retries < captureStartRetries {
760: 				// the follow-up did not start; try again while the active one still runs
761: 				c.retries++
762: 				log.Warn("Capture follow-up segment failed to start, retrying",
763: 					"node", c.group.display, "error", event.err)
764: 				c.next = nil
765: 				resetTimer(timer, time.Second)
766: 
767: 				return false, nil
768: 			}
769: 
770: 			return true, fmt.Errorf("capture on c9s node %s/%s/%s failed: %w",
771: 				c.group.location.Namespace, c.capture.req.Name, c.group.display, event.err)
772: 		}
773: 		if segment != c.active {
774: 			return false, nil
775: 		}
776: 
777: 		return c.switchSegments(ctx, timer)
778: 	}
779: 
780: 	return false, nil
781: }
782: 
783: func (c *captureChain) handleAudit(segment *captureSegment, audit *captureAudit) error {
784: 	switch audit.Status {
785: 	case captureAuditStarted:
786: 		segment.started = audit.Time
787: 		log.Debug("Capture segment started", "node", c.group.display, "segment", segment.index,
788: 			"interfaces", strings.Join(c.group.interfaces, ","), "duration", segment.duration)
789: 		if segment == c.next && !c.active.started.IsZero() {
790: 			c.setCut()
791: 		}
792: 		if segment == c.next {
793: 			c.retries = 0
794: 		}
795: 	case captureAuditSucceeded:
796: 		segment.ended = audit.Time
797: 		log.Debug("Capture segment succeeded", "node", c.group.display,
798: 			"segment", segment.index, "packets", audit.Packets)
799: 	case captureAuditDenied, captureAuditFailed:
800: 		return captureAuditError(c.group.display, audit)
801: 	}
802: 
803: 	return nil
804: }
805: 
806: // captureAuditError turns a Denied or Failed clabwire audit record into an error.
807: func captureAuditError(node string, audit *captureAudit) error {
808: 	verb := "failed"
809: 	if audit.Status == captureAuditDenied {
810: 		verb = "was denied"
811: 	}
812: 	interfaces := make([]string, 0, len(audit.Interfaces))
813: 	for _, intf := range audit.Interfaces {
814: 		interfaces = append(interfaces, intf.Name)
815: 	}
816: 
817: 	return fmt.Errorf("capture of %s on node %s %s by clabwire: %s",
818: 		strings.Join(interfaces, ","), node, verb, audit.Reason)
819: }
820: 
821: // setCut places the cut in the middle of the overlap of the active and the next segment, both
822: // measured on the pod clock.
823: func (c *captureChain) setCut() {
824: 	overlapStart := c.next.started
825: 	overlapEnd := c.active.plannedEnd()
826: 	if overlapEnd.Sub(overlapStart) < 2*c.capture.window {
827: 		// the overlap is too short to match packets around a cut: the switch is reported as a
828: 		// gap once the active segment ended
829: 		c.cut = 0
830: 		return
831: 	}
832: 	c.cut = overlapStart.Add(overlapEnd.Sub(overlapStart) / 2).UnixNano()
833: 
834: 	window := c.capture.window.Nanoseconds()
835: 	// Packets the next segment holds back are stamped from T-W on: other chains' packets after
836: 	// that wait in the reorder buffer until the switch, so the merged stream stays in order.
837: 	c.capture.out.Hold(c, c.cut-window)
838: 
839: 	// The active segment only matters for packets stamped before T. Once the pod clock passed
840: 	// T+W, it is closed: packets it read until then are still delivered, and the ones it reads
841: 	// later are stamped after T and dropped anyway. The next segment's Started record was
842: 	// written on the pod clock no later than now, so the pod clock passes T+W no later than
843: 	// (T - Started + W) from now.
844: 	active := c.active
845: 	active.stopTimer = time.AfterFunc(
846: 		time.Duration(c.cut-c.next.started.UnixNano()+window), active.closeStdin)
847: }
848: 
849: func (c *captureChain) handlePacket(
850: 	segment *captureSegment,
851: 	packet *clabcapture.Packet,
852: ) (bool, error) {
853: 	switch segment {
854: 	case c.active:
855: 		if c.cut != 0 && packet.Timestamp >= c.cut {
856: 			return false, nil
857: 		}
858: 		if c.next != nil {
859: 			c.emitted[packetKey(packet)]++
860: 		}
861: 
862: 		return c.emit(packet)
863: 	case c.next:
864: 		c.held = append(c.held, packet)
865: 	}
866: 
867: 	return false, nil
868: }
869: 
870: func (c *captureChain) emit(packet *clabcapture.Packet) (bool, error) {
871: 	if int(packet.InterfaceID) >= len(c.group.ids) {
872: 		return true, fmt.Errorf("clabwire wrote a packet for interface %d of %d",
873: 			packet.InterfaceID, len(c.group.ids))
874: 	}
875: 	more, err := c.capture.emit(c.group.ids[packet.InterfaceID], packet)
876: 
877: 	return !more, err
878: }
879: 
880: // switchSegments makes the next segment the active one after the active one ended, writing the
881: // held packets of the next one that the active one did not write.
882: func (c *captureChain) switchSegments(ctx context.Context, timer *time.Timer) (bool, error) {
883: 	// the held packets are in the reorder buffer once this returns
884: 	defer c.capture.out.Release(c)
885: 
886: 	ended := c.active
887: 	if c.stopping && c.next != nil && c.next.started.IsZero() {
888: 		// the chain is stopping: a follow-up that has not started takes nothing over
889: 		c.next, c.held, c.emitted, c.cut = nil, nil, nil, 0
890: 	}
891: 	if c.final && c.next == nil {
892: 		return true, nil
893: 	}
894: 
895: 	if c.next == nil || c.next.started.IsZero() || c.cut == 0 {
896: 		from := ended.ended
897: 		if from.IsZero() {
898: 			from = ended.plannedEnd()
899: 		}
900: 		gap := clablabruntime.CaptureGap{
901: 			Node: c.group.display, Interfaces: c.group.interfaces, From: from,
902: 			Reason: "the follow-up capture did not overlap the previous one",
903: 		}
904: 		if c.next != nil && !c.next.started.IsZero() {
905: 			gap.To = c.next.started
906: 		}
907: 		c.capture.reportGap(gap)
908: 	}
909: 
910: 	if c.next != nil && c.next.done && !c.stopping {
911: 		// the follow-up already ended (it started too late to take over): keep what it
912: 		// captured and continue with a fresh segment
913: 		for _, packet := range c.held {
914: 			if stop, err := c.emit(packet); stop || err != nil {
915: 				return true, err
916: 			}
917: 		}
918: 		c.next, c.held, c.emitted, c.cut = nil, nil, nil, 0
919: 	}
920: 
921: 	if c.next == nil {
922: 		if !c.capture.deadline.IsZero() &&
923: 			!time.Now().Before(c.capture.deadline.Add(-c.capture.window)) {
924: 			return true, nil
925: 		}
926: 		c.active = c.start(ctx, c.segmentDuration(time.Now()))
927: 		resetTimer(timer, c.nextStartIn())
928: 
929: 		return false, nil
930: 	}
931: 
932: 	window := c.capture.window.Nanoseconds()
933: 	for _, packet := range c.held {
934: 		if c.cut != 0 {
935: 			if packet.Timestamp < c.cut-window {
936: 				continue
937: 			}
938: 			if packet.Timestamp < c.cut+window {
939: 				key := packetKey(packet)
940: 				if c.emitted[key] > 0 {
941: 					c.emitted[key]--
942: 					continue
943: 				}
944: 			}
945: 		}
946: 		if stop, err := c.emit(packet); stop || err != nil {
947: 			return true, err
948: 		}
949: 	}
950: 
951: 	c.active, c.next = c.next, nil
952: 	c.held, c.emitted, c.cut = nil, nil, 0
953: 	if c.active.done {
954: 		// the chain is stopping and the follow-up ended before the active one
955: 		return true, nil
956: 	}
957: 	resetTimer(timer, c.nextStartIn())
958: 
959: 	return false, nil
960: }
961: 
962: func resetTimer(timer *time.Timer, d time.Duration) {
963: 	if !timer.Stop() {
964: 		select {
965: 		case <-timer.C:
966: 		default:
967: 		}
968: 	}
969: 	timer.Reset(d)
970: }
971: 
972: // packetKey identifies a packet by its interface and content.
973: func packetKey(packet *clabcapture.Packet) uint64 {
974: 	hash := fnv.New64a()
975: 	var id [4]byte
976: 	id[0] = byte(packet.InterfaceID)
977: 	id[1] = byte(packet.InterfaceID >> 8)
978: 	_, _ = hash.Write(id[:])
979: 	_, _ = hash.Write(packet.Data)
980: 
981: 	return hash.Sum64()
982: }
983: 
984: // start runs one clabwire capture and reports its packets, audit records and end as events.
985: func (c *captureChain) start(ctx context.Context, duration time.Duration) *captureSegment {
986: 	segmentCtx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
987: 	stdinReader, stdinWriter := io.Pipe()
988: 	segment := &captureSegment{
989: 		index: c.segments, localStart: time.Now(), duration: duration, cancel: cancel,
990: 		closeStdin: func() { _ = stdinWriter.Close() },
991: 	}
992: 	c.segments++
993: 
994: 	command := []string{
995: 		clabwireManager, "node-runtime", "packet-capture",
996: 		"--nodeName", c.group.location.NodeName,
997: 		"--format", "pcapng",
998: 		"--snapLength", strconv.Itoa(c.capture.req.SnapLength),
999: 		"--duration", duration.String(),
1000: 		clabwireStopOnStdinClose,
1001: 	}
1002: 	for _, name := range c.group.interfaces {
1003: 		command = append(command, "--interface", name)
1004: 	}
1005: 	if c.capture.req.PacketLimit > 0 {
1006: 		remaining := int64(c.capture.req.PacketLimit) - c.capture.out.Written()
1007: 		command = append(command, "--packetLimit",
1008: 			strconv.FormatInt(min(max(remaining, 1), maxClabwirePackets), 10))
1009: 	}
1010: 
1011: 	send := func(event segmentEvent) {
1012: 		event.segment = segment
1013: 		select {
1014: 		case c.events <- event:
1015: 		case <-segmentCtx.Done():
1016: 		}
1017: 	}
1018: 
1019: 	stdoutReader, stdoutWriter := io.Pipe()
1020: 	stderr := &auditLineWriter{send: func(audit *captureAudit) { send(segmentEvent{audit: audit}) }}
1021: 
1022: 	// The exec outlives the segment's context by up to captureStdinCloseGrace: when the segment
1023: 	// ends for any reason (the capture is cancelled or failed, the output failed, or a newer
1024: 	// segment took over), its stdin is closed first so clabwire ends on its own, and the stream
1025: 	// is cut only if it does not.
1026: 	execCtx, cancelExec := context.WithCancel(context.WithoutCancel(segmentCtx))
1027: 	execDone := make(chan struct{})
1028: 
1029: 	c.wg.Add(3)
1030: 	readDone := make(chan error, 1)
1031: 	go func() {
1032: 		defer c.wg.Done()
1033: 		readDone <- c.readSegment(stdoutReader, func(packet *clabcapture.Packet) {
1034: 			send(segmentEvent{packet: packet})
1035: 		})
1036: 		_, _ = io.Copy(io.Discard, stdoutReader)
1037: 	}()
1038: 	go func() {
1039: 		defer c.wg.Done()
1040: 		select {
1041: 		case <-execDone:
1042: 			return
1043: 		case <-segmentCtx.Done():
1044: 		}
1045: 		segment.closeStdin()
1046: 		grace := time.NewTimer(captureStdinCloseGrace)
1047: 		defer grace.Stop()
1048: 		select {
1049: 		case <-execDone:
1050: 		case <-grace.C:
1051: 			log.Debug("Capture segment did not end after its stdin closed, cutting the stream",
1052: 				"node", c.group.display, "segment", segment.index)
1053: 			cancelExec()
1054: 		}
1055: 	}()
1056: 	go func() {
1057: 		defer c.wg.Done()
1058: 		defer cancel()
1059: 		defer cancelExec()
1060: 
1061: 		err := c.capture.r.execInPodContainer()(execCtx, c.group.location.Namespace,
1062: 			c.group.location.Pod, clabwireContainer, command, stdinReader, stdoutWriter, stderr)
1063: 		close(execDone)
1064: 		// the process ended: release the stdin copy of the exec stream
1065: 		segment.closeStdin()
1066: 		_ = stdoutWriter.Close()
1067: 		readErr := <-readDone
1068: 		stderr.flush()
1069: 		if err == nil && readErr != nil {
1070: 			err = readErr
1071: 		}
1072: 		if err != nil && stderr.text() != "" {
1073: 			if unsupported := unsupportedClabwire(
1074: 				c.group.location,
1075: 				stderr.text(),
1076: 			); unsupported != nil {
1077: 				err = unsupported
1078: 			} else {
1079: 				err = fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", err, stderr.text())
1080: 			}
1081: 		}
1082: 		send(segmentEvent{done: true, err: err})
1083: 	}()
1084: 
1085: 	return segment
1086: }
1087: 
1088: // unsupportedClabwire recognizes a clabwire that rejects --stop-on-stdin-close, which every
1089: // capture passes: its release predates the capture contract the runtime needs.
1090: func unsupportedClabwire(location clablabruntime.NodeLocation, stderr string) error {

1103: func (c *captureChain) readSegment(stdout io.Reader, packet func(*clabcapture.Packet)) error {
1104: 	reader := clabcapture.NewReader(stdout)
1105: 	interfaces := 0

1107: 		event, err := reader.Next()

1109: 			return nil

1111: 		if errors.Is(err, io.ErrUnexpectedEOF) {

1121: 				return fmt.Errorf("clabwire described interface %q, want %s in order",

1143: func (w *auditLineWriter) Write(data []byte) (int, error) {
1144: 	w.mu.Lock()
1145: 	w.partial = append(w.partial, data...)
1146: 	var lines [][]byte
1147: 	for {
1148: 		idx := bytes.IndexByte(w.partial, '\n')
1149: 		if idx < 0 {

1152: 		lines = append(lines, append([]byte(nil), w.partial[:idx]...))
1153: 		w.partial = w.partial[idx+1:]
1154: 	}
1155: 	w.mu.Unlock()
1156: 
1157: 	for _, line := range lines {
1158: 		w.line(line)
1159: 	}
1160: 
1161: 	return len(data), nil
1162: }

1164: func (w *auditLineWriter) flush() {
1165: 	w.mu.Lock()
1166: 	line := w.partial
1167: 	w.partial = nil
1168: 	w.mu.Unlock()
1169: 	if len(bytes.TrimSpace(line)) != 0 {
1170: 		w.line(line)

1174: func (w *auditLineWriter) line(line []byte) {
1175: 	line = bytes.TrimSpace(line)

1178: 	}

1193: 		w.other = append(w.other, string(line))
1194: 	}
1195: }

1197: func (w *auditLineWriter) text() string {

A clabwire Denied or Failed audit record is returned as an error.\n465: func (r *Runtime) Capture(\n466: \tctx context.Context,\n467: \treq clablabruntime.CaptureRequest,\n468: \tw io.Writer,\n469: ) error {\n470: \tif err := clabcapture.ValidateRequest(&req); err != nil {\n471: \t\treturn err\n472: \t}\n473: \n474: \tr, err := r.connect(ctx, req.Identity)\n475: \tif err != nil {\n476: \t\treturn err\n477: \t}\n478: \n479: \tresolved, err := r.resolveCaptureTargets(ctx, req)\n480: \tif err != nil {\n481: \t\treturn err\n482: \t}\n483: \n484: \tcaptureCtx, stop := context.WithCancel(ctx)\n485: \tdefer stop()\n486: \n487: \tout, err := clabcapture.NewOutput(w, resolved.names, req.SnapLength, req.PacketLimit,\n488: \t\tr.captureReorderWindowLength(), stop)\n489: \tif err != nil {\n490: \t\treturn err\n491: \t}\n492: \n493: \trun := &captureRun{\n494: \t\tr:       r,\n495: \t\treq:     req,\n496: \t\tout:     out,\n497: \t\tsegment: r.captureSegmentLength(),\n498: \t}\n499: \tif req.Duration > 0 {\n500: \t\trun.deadline = time.Now().Add(req.Duration)\n501: \t}\n502: \trun.overlap = min(maxCaptureOverlap, run.segment/3)\n503: \trun.window = min(maxCaptureCutWindow, run.overlap/4)\n504: \n505: \tif req.Duration > 0 {\n506: \t\t// a clabwire process that does not end on its own does not hold the capture open\n507: \t\tvar cancelTimeout context.CancelFunc\n508: \t\tcaptureCtx, cancelTimeout = context.WithTimeout(captureCtx,\n509: \t\t\treq.Duration+run.overlap+captureEndGrace)\n510: \t\tdefer cancelTimeout()\n511: \t}\n512: \n513: \tgroup, groupCtx := errgroup.WithContext(captureCtx)\n514: \tfor _, captureGroup := range resolved.groups {\n515: \t\tchain := &captureChain{capture: run, group: captureGroup}\n516: \t\tgroup.Go(func() error {\n517: \t\t\treturn chain.run(groupCtx)\n518: \t\t})\n519: \t}\n520: \n521: \terr = group.Wait()\n522: \tif writeErr := out.Close(); writeErr != nil {\n523: \t\treturn writeErr\n524: \t}\n525: \tif err != nil && !(errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) && captureCtx.Err() != nil) {\n526: \t\treturn err\n527: \t}\n528: \n529: \treturn nil\n530: }\n531: \n532: // captureRun is the state a capture's chains share.\n533: type captureRun struct {\n534: \tr   *Runtime\n535: \treq clablabruntime.CaptureRequest\n536: \t// out is the merged stream; it writes the packets of every chain in timestamp order and\n537: \t// stops every chain once the packet limit is reached.\n538: \tout *clabcapture.Output\n539: \n540: \tsegment  time.Duration\n541: \toverlap  time.Duration\n542: \twindow   time.Duration\n543: \tdeadline time.Time\n544: }\n545: \n546: // emit writes a packet under its merged interface ID. The chain therefore cuts in the middle of the overlap and matches packets by\n592: // content close to the cut:\n593: //\n594: //  1. When segment k+1 reports Started (pod clock, from its audit record), the cut is\n595: //     T = midpoint of [Started(k+1), Started(k) + duration(k)]: both segments run then.\n596: //  2. Segment k keeps streaming live, but only packets stamped before T; it remembers the\n597: //     content of what it wrote since segment k+1 started.\n598: //  3. Segment k+1's packets are held back until segment k has ended. Then the ones stamped\n599: //     before T-W are dropped (segment k had them), the ones stamped within W of T are dropped\n600: //     when segment k wrote the same bytes on the same interface, and every other one is written.\n601: //     From then on segment k+1 streams live.\n602: //\n603: // Once the pod clock passed T+W, segment k's stdin is closed so it ends without running to its\n604: // planned end. While packets are held back, the chain holds the reorder buffer at T-W, so other\n605: // nodes' later packets do not overtake them in the merged stream.\n606: //\n607: // W (500 ms, less for short test segments) covers the stamping difference. A follow-up segment that does not start in time leaves\n610: // a gap, which is reported through CaptureRequest.OnGap (or logged), never silently ignored.\n611: type captureChain struct {\n612: \tcapture *captureRun\n613: \tgroup   *captureGroup\n614: \n615: \tevents chan segmentEvent\n616: \twg     sync.WaitGroup\n617: \n618: \tactive *captureSegment\n619: \tnext   *captureSegment\n620: \t// cut is the switch time between active and next, in nanoseconds; zero until known.\n621: \tcut int64\n622: \t// emitted remembers the content of the packets active wrote while next runs.\n623: \temitted map[uint64]int\n624: \t// held are the packets of next until active ends.\n625: \theld     []*clabcapture.Packet\n626: \tsegments int\n627: \tretries  int\n628: \t// final is set once no further segment is due.\n629: \tfinal bool\n630: \t// stopping is set once ctx ended: the segments are asked to end and what they still\n631: \t// deliver is written.\n632: \tstopping bool\n633: }\n634: \n635: // run runs the chain until its last segment ended. entries {\n\t\tif entry.Alias != \"\" && entry.Alias == name {\n\t\t\treturn entry, true\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn clabwireInterface{}, false\n}\n\nfunc describeCaptureInterfaces(entries A clabwire Denied or Failed audit record is returned as an error.\nfunc (r *Runtime) Capture(\n\tctx context.Context,\n\treq clablabruntime.CaptureRequest,\n\tw io.Writer,\n) error {\n\tif err := clabcapture.ValidateRequest(&req); err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\tr, err := r.connect(ctx, req.Identity)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\tresolved, err := r.resolveCaptureTargets(ctx, req)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\tcaptureCtx, stop := context.WithCancel(ctx)\n\tdefer stop()\n\n\tout, err := clabcapture.NewOutput(w, resolved.names, req.SnapLength, req.PacketLimit,\n\t\tr.captureReorderWindowLength(), stop)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\trun := &captureRun{\n\t\tr:       r,\n\t\treq:     req,\n\t\tout:     out,\n\t\tsegment: r.captureSegmentLength(),\n\t}\n\tif req.Duration > 0 {\n\t\trun.deadline = time.Now().Add(req.Duration)\n\t}\n\trun.overlap = min(maxCaptureOverlap, run.segment/3)\n\trun.window = min(maxCaptureCutWindow, run.overlap/4)\n\n\tif req.Duration > 0 {\n\t\t// a clabwire process that does not end on its own does not hold the capture open\n\t\tvar cancelTimeout context.CancelFunc\n\t\tcaptureCtx, cancelTimeout = context.WithTimeout(captureCtx,\n\t\t\treq.Duration+run.overlap+captureEndGrace)\n\t\tdefer cancelTimeout()\n\t}\n\n\tgroup, groupCtx := errgroup.WithContext(captureCtx)\n\tfor _, captureGroup := range resolved.groups {\n\t\tchain := &captureChain{capture: run, group: captureGroup}\n\t\tgroup.Go(func() error {\n\t\t\treturn chain.run(groupCtx)\n\t\t})\n\t}\n\n\terr = group.Wait()\n\tif writeErr := out.Close(); writeErr != nil {\n\t\treturn writeErr\n\t}\n\tif err != nil && !(errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) && captureCtx.Err() != nil) {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// captureRun is the state a capture's chains share.\ntype captureRun struct {\n\tr   *Runtime\n\treq clablabruntime.CaptureRequest\n\t// out is the merged stream; it writes the packets of every chain in timestamp order and\n\t// stops every chain once the packet limit is reached.\n\tout *clabcapture.Output\n\n\tsegment  time.Duration\n\toverlap  time.Duration\n\twindow   time.Duration\n\tdeadline time.Time\n}\n\n// emit writes a packet under its merged interface ID. Segment k+1's packets are held back until segment k has ended. A follow-up segment that does not start in time leaves\n// a gap, which is reported through CaptureRequest.OnGap (or logged), never silently ignored.\ntype captureChain struct {\n\tcapture *captureRun\n\tgroup   *captureGroup\n\n\tevents chan segmentEvent\n\twg     sync.WaitGroup\n\n\tactive *captureSegment\n\tnext   *captureSegment\n\t// cut is the switch time between active and next, in nanoseconds; zero until known.\n\tcut int64\n\t// emitted remembers the content of the packets active wrote while next runs.\n\temitted map[uint64]int\n\t// held are the packets of next until active ends.\n\theld     []*clabcapture.Packet\n\tsegments int\n\tretries  int\n\t// final is set once no further segment is due.\n\tfinal bool\n\t// stopping is set once ctx ended: the segments are asked to end and what they still\n\t// deliver is written.\n\tstopping bool\n}\n\n// run runs the chain until its last segment ended. c.segmentDuration(time.Now()))\n\tc.emitted = map[uint64]int{}\n\tc.held = nil\n\tc.cut = 0\n}\n\nfunc (c *captureChain) handle(\n\tctx context.Context,\n\tevent segmentEvent,\n\ttimer *time.Timer,\n) segment succeeded\", \"node\", c.group.display,\n\t\t\t\"segment\", segment.index, \"packets\", audit.Packets)\n\tcase captureAuditDenied, captureAuditFailed:\n\t\treturn audit.Reason)\n}\n\n// setCut places the cut in the middle of the overlap of the active and the next segment, both\n// measured on the pod clock.\nfunc (c *captureChain) setCut() {\n\toverlapStart := 2750: +package core
2751: +
2752: +import (
2753: +	"context"
2754: +	"io"
2755: +
2756: +	clablabruntime "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/labruntime"
2757: +	clabtypes "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/types"
2758: +)
2759: +
2760: +// CaptureInterfaces lists the lab link interfaces Capture accepts for the given nodes, or for
2761: +// every running node, with the peer at the other end of each link. With Docker and Podman, the
2762: +// interfaces come from the topology's links; lab runtimes list them through their packet
2763: +// capturer.
2764: +func (c *CLab) CaptureInterfaces(
2765: +	ctx context.Context,
2766: +	nodeNames ...string,
2767: +) ([]clablabruntime.CaptureInterface, error) {
2768: +	if c.LabRuntime == nil {
2769: +		return c.localCaptureInterfacesOf(ctx, nodeNames)
2770: +	}
2771: +
2772: +	capturer, err := c.packetCapturer()
2773: +	if err != nil {
2774: +		return nil, err
2775: +	}
2776: +
2777: +	return capturer.CaptureInterfaces(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
2778: +		Name:     c.Config.Name,
2779: +		Nodes:    nodeNames,
2780: +		Identity: c.labRuntimeIdentity,
2781: +	})
2782: +}
2783: +
2784: +// Capture streams pcapng from lab link interfaces to w until req.Duration passed,
2785: +// req.PacketLimit packets were written or ctx ends; an ended ctx is not an error. The lab name
2786: +// and identity default to the CLab's. With Docker and Podman, containerlab reads the interfaces
2787: +// itself through packet sockets in the nodes' network namespaces, which needs root; lab
2788: +// runtimes capture through their packet capturer.
2789: +func (c *CLab) Capture(ctx context.Context, req clablabruntime.CaptureRequest, w io.Writer) error {
2790: +	if c.LabRuntime == nil {
2791: +		return c.captureLocal(ctx, req, w)
2792: +	}
2793: +
2794: +	capturer, err := c.packetCapturer()
2795: +	if err != nil {
2796: +		return err
2797: +	}
2798: +
2799: +	if req.Name == "" {
2800: +		req.Name = c.Config.Name
2801: +	}
2802: +	if req.Identity.IsZero() {
2803: +		req.Identity = c.labRuntimeIdentity
2804: +	}
2805: +
2806: +	return capturer.Capture(ctx, req, w)
2807: +}
2808: +
2809: +// LabRuntimeInterfaces lists the link interfaces of the lab's nodes, or of one node, with their
2810: +// state, in the shape ListContainersInterfaces reports for local containers.
2811: +func (c *CLab) LabRuntimeInterfaces(
2812: +	ctx context.Context,
2813: +	nodeName string,
2814: +) ([]*clabtypes.ContainerInterfaces, error) {
2815: +	inspector, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.InterfaceInspector](
2816: +		c, "inspecting interfaces")
2817: +	if err != nil {
2818: +		return nil, err
2819: +	}
2820: +	if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
2821: +		return nil, err
2822: +	}
2823: +
2824: +	req := clablabruntime.NodeRequest{Name: c.Config.Name, Identity: c.labRuntimeIdentity}
2825: +	if nodeName != "" {
2826: +		req.Nodes = []string{nodeName}
2827: +	}
2828: +
2829: +	return inspector.InspectInterfaces(ctx, req)
2830: +}
2831: +
2832: +func (c *CLab) packetCapturer() (clablabruntime.PacketCapturer, error) {
2833: +	capturer, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.PacketCapturer](c, "packet capture")
2834: +	if err != nil {
2835: +		return nil, err
2836: +	}
2837: +	if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
2838: +		return nil, err
2839: +	}
2840: +
2841: +	return capturer, nil
2842: +}

Reasoning
The `cmd/context.go` change: `SignalHandledContext` — when FinishOnCancel is set, the signal handler waits for a second signal, then `os.Exit(1)`. But there's a subtlety: after first signal, the handler cancels the root context; the command finishes its output. If the second signal comes, exit(1). But if the command finishes cleanly and the process exits, the goroutine is still blocked on `<-sigs` — that's fine, process exit cleans it.

Wait — one issue: with FinishOnCancel, the handler cancels ctx and logs "Stopping, press Ctrl+C again to abort". But `SignalHandledContext` cancel happens before this branch? Let me read the full context.go to check.

Also potential issue: `cmd/capture.go` — when capturing with `-w -` (stdout), logs go to stderr presumably; but there's a concern: when writing pcapng to stdout, any log output to stdout would corrupt. The `Run Capture --list -f json` uses stdout. The capture command with `-w -` writes pcapng to stdout. If the `log` package writes to stderr by default in containerlab? Probably fine.

More significant: `captureFn` sets `o.Global.FinishOnCancel.Store(true)` AFTER checking targets and creating `c`, but before creating the file. Then arms. Fine.

Let me now read the head cmd/context.go fully to understand the signal handling flow.

69: 			os.Exit(1)
70: 		}

91: 		return true
92: 	default:
93: 		return false
94: 	}
95: }

97: // destroyCancelledDeploy removes the lab that a cancelled deployment was in the middle of
98: // creating. It runs on a fresh context because the command context is canceled by then.
99: func destroyCancelledDeploy(o *Options) {
100: 	destroyCtx, destroyCancel := context.WithTimeout(
101: 		context.Background(),
102: 		cancelledDestroyTimeout(o),
103: 	)
104: 	defer destroyCancel()
105: 
106: 	// destroyFn requires a cobra.Command but only needs the ctx from it
107: 	destroyCmd := &cobra.Command{}
108: 	destroyCmd.SetContext(destroyCtx)
109: 
110: 	err := destroyFn(destroyCmd, o)
111: 	if err != nil {
112: 		log.Errorf("failed destroying lab after cancellation signal: %v", err)
113: 	}
114: }
115: 
116: // cancelledDestroyTimeout bounds the rollback of a cancelled deployment. Controller-driven
117: // runtimes delete remote resources and wait for the cluster to converge on the deletion,
118: // which legitimately outlasts the bound that is generous for a local teardown.
119: func cancelledDestroyTimeout(o *Options) time.Duration {
120: 	if clablabruntime.IsLabRuntimeName(o.Global.Runtime) {
121: 		return o.Global.Timeout
122: 	}
123: 
124: 	return maxCancelledDestroyTimeout
125: }

Reasoning
One observation: when `FinishOnCancel` is set and the capture finishes cleanly (e.g., duration expires) before the user presses Ctrl+C again, the process exits normally — but the signal-handler goroutine remains blocked on `<-sigs`, which is fine.

However, there's a subtle issue: the second signal during "stopping" exits with code 1 — reasonable.

Another consideration: `defer o.Global.FinishOnCancel.Store(false)` in captureFn — if captureFn returns normally and the user had already sent one Ctrl+C... The context cancel triggers capture end; captureFn returns nil; the goroutine is still waiting for the second signal. Then main returns and the process exits. Fine.

But there's a subtle race: after `FinishOnCancel.Store(false)` (defer runs at captureFn exit), if the handler goroutine is between `GetOptions()` and the `Load()`... Actually the handler reads options once via GetOptions at that point; the `Load()` happens right after. Sequence: signal arrives → cancel() → GetOptions() → Load(). If the capture ends before the signal arrives, no issue. If the signal arrives just before captureFn's defer resets the flag, the handler sees true and waits for a second signal — process exits normally when main returns. No leak issue beyond a goroutine.

Now let me look at the diff hunks I haven't seen in detail: capture/local_test.go, pcapng_test.go, reorder_test.go, cmd/capture_test.go, core/capture_test.go, labruntime_cluster_test.go, docs, and labruntime/clabernetes/capture_test.go (1050 lines). Also the diff for labruntime/runtime.go (interface additions) and clabernetes.go.

I've already seen runtime.go diff tail (PacketCapturer interface etc. at 6410-6474). Let me view the beginning of the runtime.go hunk and clabernetes.go hunk.

1: # capture command
2: 
3: ### Description
4: 
5: The `capture` command captures packets on lab link interfaces of one or more nodes and writes them as one [pcapng](https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-opsawg-pcapng-03.html) stream, to a file or to stdout for Wireshark.
6: 
7: It works with every runtime:
8: 
9: - **Docker and Podman**: containerlab opens a packet socket on each interface inside the node's network namespace. Nothing runs in the node, the node image needs no capture tools, and no extra software is needed on the host: the command needs root, like `deploy`. See [How Docker and Podman captures work](#how-docker-and-podman-captures-work).
10: - **c9s**: the `clabwire` sidecar of each node's pod captures the packets; see the [c9s runtime](../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md#packet-capture).
11: 
12: The output is the same with both. [Edgeshark](../manual/wireshark.md) remains an alternative for Docker labs when you prefer to pick interfaces in a GUI.
13: 
14: --8<-- "docs/cmd/deploy.md:env-vars-flags"
15: 
16: ### Usage
17: 
18: `containerlab [global-flags] capture [local-flags]`
19: 
20: ### Flags
21: 
22: #### topology | name
23: 
24: Use the global `--topo | -t` flag to reference the lab topology file, or use the global `--name` flag to reference an already deployed lab by name. Without either, containerlab looks for a `*.clab.yml` file in the current directory, like the other lab commands.
25: 
26: With Docker and Podman, the capturable interfaces are the links of the topology file, so `--name` needs the topology file the lab was deployed from to still be in place.
27: 
28: #### target
29: 
30: The local `--target` flag selects what to capture, as `<node>:<interface>[,<interface>...]`. Repeat it for more nodes:
31: 
32: ```text
33: --target srl1:e1-1,e1-2 --target srl2:e1-1
34: ```
35: 
36: The node name ends at the first colon, so interface names such as `1/1/3` or `ethernet-1/1` need no quoting. Node names are accepted as the topology file spells them; with Docker and Podman also as the container name (`clab-srl-srl1`), with c9s also as they were sanitized for Kubernetes (`R1` or `r1`). Interfaces are accepted by their name in the node or by the alias the topology used for them (`e1-1` or `ethernet-1/1` for SR Linux). `--list` shows both.
37: 
38: Only lab link interfaces can be captured; the management interface cannot. An interface that is not a link interface of the node fails the command before anything is captured, and the error lists the node's capturable interfaces.
39: 
40: #### duration
41: 
42: The local `--duration` flag stops the capture after the given time (`30s`, `5m`, `2h`). The default `0` captures until the command is interrupted with Ctrl+C or SIGTERM. Captures may run longer than an hour; see [Long captures](#long-captures).
43: 
44: #### packet-limit
45: 
46: The local `--packet-limit` flag stops the capture after that many packets, counted across all targets. `0`, the default, means no limit.
47: 
48: #### snap-length
49: 
50: The local `--snap-length` flag sets how many bytes of each packet are kept, from 64 to 1048576. The default `0` keeps 256 KiB.
51: 
52: #### write
53: 
54: The local `--write | -w` flag names the output file. The default `-` writes to stdout.
55: 
56: #### list
57: 
58: The local `--list` flag lists the interfaces `capture` accepts, for every running node, with the node and interface at the other end of each link, instead of capturing. `--format | -f` selects `table` (default) or `json`.
59: 
60: ### Output
61: 
62: The output is one pcapng section:
63: 
64: - a Section Header Block with `shb_userappl` set to `containerlab`
65: - one Interface Description Block per target, in the order of the `--target` flags, written before any packet: link type Ethernet, the snap length, nanosecond timestamps, and the name `<node>:<interface>` (for example `srl1:e1-1`), with the node named as the topology spells it
66: - Enhanced Packet Blocks of all targets, in timestamp order: packets are held briefly (100 ms with Docker and Podman, 250 ms with c9s) and written ordered by timestamp, so packets of different interfaces come out in order even though each one is read on its own; a packet that arrives later than that is written as it comes
67: 
68: The interface name shows in Wireshark's interface column (`frame.interface_name`), so a capture of several nodes can be filtered by node and interface.
69: 
70: When the capture ends (duration, packet limit, Ctrl+C or SIGTERM), the command finishes the stream and exits with code 0; the file is a valid capture. Status messages go to stderr. With c9s, every `clabwire` capture in the pods ends with the command: containerlab closes its stdin, and `clabwire` (`--stop-on-stdin-close`) stops.
71: 
72: `--list -f json` prints an array:
73: 
74: ```json
75: [
76:   {
77:     "node": "srl1",
78:     "interface": "e1-1",
79:     "alias": "ethernet-1/1",
80:     "peer_node": "srl2",
81:     "peer_interface": "ethernet-1/1"
82:   }
83: ]
84: ```
85: 
86: `alias` is present only when the topology used an alias for the interface. `peer_node` is `host` for a host endpoint and `mgmt-net` for a management network endpoint.
87: 
88: ### How Docker and Podman captures work
89: 
90: For each target, containerlab enters the node's network namespace, opens a Linux packet socket (`AF_PACKET`) bound to the interface, and leaves the namespace again; the socket keeps capturing on that interface. This is what `tcpdump` does inside the node, without needing `tcpdump` in the node or on the host. All sockets are opened before the first byte is written, so a capture that cannot start (a node that does not run, a missing interface) fails without output.
91: 
92: - Packets carry the kernel's receive timestamps, so packets of different nodes compare on one clock.
93: - 802.1Q tags, which the kernel keeps outside the frame, are put back in place, so VLAN traffic shows its tags as on the wire.
94: - Each socket is in promiscuous mode for as long as it is open; the interface returns to its previous state when the capture ends.
95: - An interface that goes down and up again keeps being captured. When an interface disappears, for example while its node restarts, containerlab waits for it and reattaches once the node is back (`containerlab restart --node`). The time it was gone is reported as a warning with its start and end time.
96: 
97: The command needs root (to open packet sockets and enter network namespaces), as other lab commands do.
98: 
99: ### Long captures
100: 
101: Docker and Podman captures have no length limit. With c9s, one `clabwire` capture lasts at most one hour. `capture` chains captures: it starts the next one shortly before the current one ends, lets both run for a few seconds, and switches between them in the middle of that overlap. The repeated section and interface headers of the follow-up are dropped, and packets seen by both captures near the switch are written once (they are matched by content, because each capture stamps packets when it reads them). Once the switch time has passed, the previous capture is stopped through its stdin instead of running to its end. If a follow-up capture does not start in time, the missing interval is reported as a warning with its start and end time; it is never skipped silently. The timestamp order holds across switches: while one node's capture switches, packets of other nodes stamped after the switch wait for it.
102: 
103: ### Examples
104: 
105: #### Capture two nodes for 30 seconds into one file
106: 
107: ```bash
108: containerlab capture -t srl.clab.yml \
109:   --target srl1:e1-1 --target srl2:e1-1 --duration 30s -w srl.pcapng
110: ```
111: 
112: #### Watch a capture live in Wireshark
113: 
114: ```bash
115: containerlab capture --name srl --target srl1:e1-1,e1-2 -w - | wireshark -k -i -
116: ```
117: 
118: #### Capture the first 100 packets with tshark
119: 
120: ```bash
121: containerlab capture --name srl --target srl1:ethernet-1/1 --packet-limit 100 -w - | tshark -r -
122: ```
123: 
124: #### List the capturable interfaces
125: 
126: ```bash
127: containerlab capture --name srl --list
128: ```
129: 
130: #### Capture a c9s lab
131: 
132: ```bash
133: containerlab -r c9s capture --name srl --target srl1:e1-1 --target srl2:e1-1 -w srl.pcapng
134: ```

(End of file - total 134 lines)
</content>

When an interface disappears, for example while its node restarts, containerlab waits for it and reattaches once the node is back (`containerlab restart --node`). The time it was gone is reported as a warning with its start and end time.\n\nThe command needs root (to open packet sockets and enter network namespaces), as other lab commands do.\n\n### Long captures\n\nDocker and Podman captures have no length limit. With c9s, one `clabwire` capture lasts at most one hour. `capture` chains captures: it starts the next one shortly before the current one ends, lets both run for a few seconds, and switches between them in the middle of that overlap. The repeated section and interface headers of the follow-up are dropped, and packets seen by both captures near the switch are written once (they are matched by content, because each capture stamps packets when it reads them). Once the switch time has passed, the previous capture is stopped through its stdin instead of running to its end. If a follow-up capture does not start in time, the missing interval is reported as a warning with its start and end time; it is never skipped silently. The timestamp order holds across switches: while one node's capture switches, packets of other nodes stamped after the switch wait for it.\n\n### Examples\n\n#### Capture two nodes for 30 seconds into one file\n\n```bash\ncontainerlab capture -t srl.clab.yml \\\n  --target srl1:e1-1 --target srl2:e1-1 --duration 30s -w srl.pcapng\n```\n\n#### Watch a capture live in Wireshark\n\n```bash\ncontainerlab capture --name srl --target srl1:e1-1,e1-2 -w - | wireshark -k -i -\n```\n\n#### Capture the first 100 packets with tshark\n\n```bash\ncontainerlab capture --name srl --target srl1:ethernet-1/1 --packet-limit 100 -w - | tshark -r -\n```\n\n#### List the capturable interfaces\n\n```bash\ncontainerlab capture --name srl --list\n```\n\n#### Capture a c9s lab\n\n```bash\ncontainerlab -r c9s capture --name srl --target srl1:e1-1 --target srl2:e1-1 -w srl.pcapng\n```",

2323: +		SnapLength:  o.Capture.SnapLength,
2324: +	}, output)
2325: +	if err != nil {
2326: +		return err
2327: +	}

2330: +		if err := file.Sync(); err != nil {
2331: +			return fmt.Errorf("failed to write the capture file: %w", err)
2332: +		}
2333: +	}
2334: +
2335: +	return nil
2336: +}
2337: +
2338: +// parseCaptureTargets parses --target values: <node>:<interface>[,<interface>...]. The node name
2339: +// ends at the first colon, so interface names may contain colons or slashes.
2340: +func parseCaptureTargets(values []string) ([]clablabruntime.CaptureTarget, error) {
2341: +	if len(values) == 0 {
2342: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("provide at least one --target <node>:<interface>[,<interface>...]")
2343: +	}
2344: +
2345: +	targets := make([]clablabruntime.CaptureTarget, 0, len(values))
2346: +	for _, value := range values {
2347: +		node, interfaces, ok := strings.Cut(strings.TrimSpace(value), ":")
2348: +		node = strings.TrimSpace(node)
2349: +		if !ok || node == "" || strings.TrimSpace(interfaces) == "" {
2350: +			return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid --target %q: use <node>:<interface>[,<interface>...]",
2351: +				value)
2352: +		}
2353: +
2354: +		for _, name := range strings.Split(interfaces, ",") {
2355: +			name = strings.TrimSpace(name)
2356: +			if name == "" {
2357: +				return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid --target %q: empty interface name", value)
2358: +			}
2359: +			targets = append(targets, clablabruntime.CaptureTarget{Node: node, Interface: name})
2360: +		}
2361: +	}
2362: +
2363: +	return targets, nil
2364: +}
2365: +
2366: +func captureListFn(cmd *cobra.Command, o *Options) error {
2367: +	format := o.Capture.Format
2368: +	if format == "" {
2369: +		format = clabconstants.FormatTable
2370: +	}
2371: +	if format != clabconstants.FormatTable && format != clabconstants.FormatJSON {
2372: +		return fmt.Errorf("output format %q is not supported, use 'table' or 'json'", format)
2373: +	}
2374: +	if len(o.Capture.Targets) != 0 {
2375: +		return fmt.Errorf("--list lists every running node's interfaces; it takes no --target")
2376: +	}
2377: +
2378: +	c, err := clabcore.NewContainerLab(o.ToClabOptions()...)
2379: +	if err != nil {
2380: +		return err
2381: +	}
2382: +
2383: +	interfaces, err := c.CaptureInterfaces(cmd.Context())
2384: +	if err != nil {
2385: +		return err
2386: +	}
2387: +
2388: +	return printCaptureInterfaces(cmd.OutOrStdout(), interfaces, format)
2389: +}
2390: +
2391: +func printCaptureInterfaces(
2392: +	w io.Writer,
2393: +	interfaces []clablabruntime.CaptureInterface,
2394: +	format string,
2395: +) error {
2396: +	if format == clabconstants.FormatJSON {
2397: +		if interfaces == nil {
2398: +			interfaces = []clablabruntime.CaptureInterface{}
2399: +		}
2400: +		data, err := json.MarshalIndent(interfaces, "", "  ")
2401: +		if err != nil {
2402: +			return err
2403: +		}
2404: +		_, err = fmt.Fprintln(w, string(data))
2405: +
2406: +		return err
2407: +	}
2408: +
2409: +	table := tableWriter.NewWriter()
2410: +	table.SetOutputMirror(w)
2411: +	table.SetStyle(tableWriter.StyleRounded)
2412: +	table.Style().Format.Header = text.FormatTitle
2413: +	table.Style().Format.HeaderAlign = text.AlignCenter
2414: +	table.AppendHeader(tableWriter.Row{"Node", "Interface", "Alias", "Peer Node", "Peer Interface"})
2415: +	table.SetColumnConfigs([]tableWriter.ColumnConfig{{Number: 1, AutoMerge: true}})
2416: +	for _, intf := range interfaces {
2417: +		alias := intf.Alias
2418: +		if alias == "" {
2419: +			alias = clabconstants.NotApplicable
2420: +		}
2421: +		table.AppendRow(tableWriter.Row{
2422: +			intf.Node, intf.Interface, alias, intf.PeerNode, intf.PeerInterface,
2423: +		})
2424: +	}
2425: +	table.Render()
2426: +
2427: +	return nil
2428: +}
